screening_results.reason: This is a task-based fMRI study of relational reasoning that fits the review’s problem-solving definition (evaluating premises, deriving conclusions via logical/relational operations). It reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses in healthy adult participants (n=12) using SPM99, with stereotactic coordinates (Talairach) reported (e.g., precuneus x=0,y=-62,z=36) and conventional fMRI (BOLD/EPI) methods. Voxelwise activation contrasts (reasoning vs. rest, maintenance vs. rest, reasoning vs. maintenance) are presented. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not between-group/disease comparisons, and is empirical). Full text is complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore it meets I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 and should be included.

This fMRI study uses a nonverbal abstract reasoning task that requires participants to determine the next item in a sequence (goal-directed pattern completion, evaluation of relations, planning/selection of the correct response), which fits the review’s definition of problem solving. It reports whole-brain, task-based BOLD fMRI analyses with within-group (one-sample t-test) results for healthy adult control participants (age 30–50). Stereotactic coordinates are provided in MNI space and voxelwise results are reported in tables/figures. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8 and I9. No exclusion criteria are met (results are not ROI-only, include healthy-group task effects, are empirical). Full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion and appears complete.

The provided full text lacks stereotactic coordinate reporting (Talairach/MNI) of task-related activations required by I7. While the study used task-based fMRI (BOLD) in healthy adults and reports group-level whole-brain regional activations for verbal learning, arithmetic, and divided attention (satisfying I5, I6, and I8), the manuscript text here summarizes regional findings without providing voxelwise coordinate results or tables/figures with coordinates. The article also reads like a summary referring readers to primary articles for detailed methods/results, so the supplied full text appears incomplete for determining whether coordinates exist. Therefore it does not meet I7 and cannot be included. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are directly met based on the supplied content, but fulltext_incomplete is set because core methodological/results details (including coordinates) are missing from the provided document.

This is an event-related task-based fMRI study using a Raven Progressive Matrices relational-reasoning paradigm (meets I5). It includes healthy adult participants (18-25 y) and reports group-level whole-brain analyses for adults (meets I6). Data were normalized to MNI305 space and the manuscript refers to whole-brain contrasts and a Supplementary Table of results, indicating stereotactic coordinate reporting in standardized space (meets I7 and I9). Analyses are BOLD fMRI (meets I8). The full text provided contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion (fulltext_complete). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not non-empirical, includes within-group adult task effects and not only between-group contrasts). Therefore the study satisfies all inclusion criteria and is eligible for inclusion.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults using a verbal ‘chengyu’ riddle task that requires goal-directed problem solving (participants select a novel, reasonable answer among alternatives, involving constraint relaxation, representation change, and selection of solutions). The study reports whole-brain, voxel-wise group-level random-effects analyses (SPM), task-related BOLD activation and contrasts (insight vs. rest, insight vs. noninsight), and provides stereotactic peak coordinates for activations (e.g., LMTG, RIFG, hippocampi). Functional connectivity analyses are reported along with ROI peaks, but whole-brain activation results are clearly presented. Participants are healthy adults. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8 and I9. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Meets all inclusion criteria: (I5) Tasks include problem-solving demands—mechanical puzzles (causal/physical prediction) and social false-belief/mental-state inference that require reasoning and evaluation; (I6) Whole-brain, group-level analyses reported in a healthy adult sample (n=45) with random-effects results; (I7) Task-related stereotactic coordinates are reported in 711-2B/Talairach space (peak coordinates table); (I8) BOLD fMRI analyses are used; (I9) Voxelwise results are reported and summarized in figures/tables. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, peak coordinates, stimuli).

This study reports a task-based fMRI investigation of relational reasoning, which constitutes a form of problem solving (goal-directed evaluation of relations and rule-based operations). It includes whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (SPM5 with FWE correction across the whole brain) and presents stereotactic peak coordinates and BOLD results. An adult group (ages 22–30) was analyzed and reported separately, satisfying the requirement for healthy adult task effects. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for task definition, imaging modality, whole-brain analysis, stereotactic coordinate reporting, and BOLD results. Note: sample includes adolescents and adults, but adult group data and whole-brain results are present and usable for the adult-focused meta-analysis.

Only title/abstract/metadata are provided (full text incomplete). From the abstract we can confirm this is a PET task-based study of simple calculation in healthy adult volunteers and reports PET activation (rCBF) group effects, satisfying I5 (problem-solving by rule-based calculation), I6 (group-level whole-brain activation implied), and I8 (rCBF via PET). However the provided content does not include stereotactic coordinate results in Talairach/MNI space (I7) nor confirmation that voxelwise coordinates are reported in tables/figures/supplementary materials (I9). Because ALL inclusion criteria must be verifiable and I7/I9 cannot be confirmed from the incomplete full text, the study is excluded pending full-text verification. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met.

This is a within-subjects, whole-brain task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that reports stereotactic coordinate results and BOLD analyses (meets I6, I7, I8, I9). However, it does not investigate a problem-solving task as defined by the review (I5). The experimental tasks are false-belief (Theory of Mind) attribution and a Go/No-go inhibitory control task, neither of which require a goal-directed problem-solving process involving planning/sequencing or deriving a previously unknown solution. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study is excluded because it fails to satisfy inclusion criterion I5 (problem-solving task).

The study is a task-based whole-brain fMRI investigation in healthy adults examining visuospatial angle discrimination (BOLD fMRI, group GLM). However, it does not meet the review's definition of a problem-solving task (I5): the task is perceptual/visuospatial discrimination rather than goal-directed problem solving involving planning/sequencing or rule-based operations to derive novel solutions. While the paper includes whole-brain group analysis in healthy adults (I6) and reports BOLD results (I8), it does not clearly provide stereotactic coordinates in the provided full text excerpt (I7 not met). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore the study is excluded.

The study reports a task-based fMRI experiment including a mental rotation task that requires participants to perform rule-based spatial transformations to arrive at correct responses, which fits the review’s operational definition of problem solving. It includes healthy adult control participants and reports whole-brain, group-level analyses (2×2 ANCOVA and task main effects) using BOLD fMRI. Results are reported with stereotactic coordinates in MNI space (e.g., MNI: −12 10 56; 0 −88 −8) and voxelwise activations are described across the brain. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5 (problem-solving task — mental rotation), I6 (whole-brain group-level analyses including healthy adults), I7 (coordinates in MNI space), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), and I9 (voxelwise results available in text/figures). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Although this study used task-based BOLD fMRI with whole-brain, group-level analyses including a healthy adult control group and reports stereotactic coordinates for some effects, the scanned task (a mental rotation visuospatial transformation) does not meet the review’s definition of a problem-solving task (I5). The Raven’s Progressive Matrices (a prototypical problem-solving task) was administered behaviorally but was not performed during imaging; only the mental rotation task was used in the scanner. Therefore the key inclusion criterion I5 (task-based fMRI/PET of a problem-solving task) is not satisfied. Inclusion criteria met: I6, I7, I8, I9. Inclusion criterion not met: I5. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (N=23) using a visuospatial analogical reasoning task that requires goal-directed problem solving (relational integration, inhibition, selection of correct response), meeting the review definition of problem solving. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses with permutation-based correction, provides stereotactic MNI coordinates for activations, and uses BOLD fMRI. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9. No exclusion criteria are met.

This study is an fMRI/TMS investigation of visuospatial angle discrimination (ANGLE) versus color judgment (COLOR). Although it includes healthy adult participants, whole-brain BOLD analyses, and reports Talairach coordinates (satisfying I6, I7, I8, I9), it does not investigate a problem-solving task as defined in the review (goal-directed multi-step problem solving involving planning/sequencing operations within a rule set). The ANGLE task is a perceptual visuospatial judgment/discrimination rather than a problem-solving paradigm meeting I5. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study is excluded because it fails inclusion criterion I5 (problem-solving task).

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults using the Wason selection task, which requires goal-directed, rule-based logical problem solving (identifying which cards would falsify/violate a conditional rule). The study reports group-level random-effects whole-brain analyses (SPM99), BOLD fMRI results, and stereotactic coordinates in MNI space, with voxelwise activations presented in figures/tables. The full text includes methods, behavioral and imaging results, and discussion, so the article appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only; includes healthy-group task effects; empirical data). Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I9 are met.

The paper is an fMRI study of reasoning and episodic-memory-based reasoning in healthy adults and meets several inclusion criteria (I5, I6, I8). However, the provided full text does not report stereotactic coordinates (Talairach or MNI) for task-related activations in the excerpt available, nor does it explicitly state that voxelwise coordinates are available in tables/figures/supplementary material. Therefore I7 (stereotactic coordinates reported) is not satisfied; I9 (acceptability of coordinates in tables/figures) cannot be confirmed from the provided content. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I8. Inclusion criteria not met / not confirmable: I7, I9. Exclusion criteria applied: [].

This is a task-based fMRI study of inductive reasoning/pattern discovery in healthy adults, which meets the meta-analysis definition of problem solving (goal-directed pattern discovery requiring hypothesis generation, evaluation, and rule-based prediction). Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses were performed using SPM8 with normalization to an MNI template and random-effects group maps; results are reported as activations with BA labels and the manuscript refers to figures/tables of voxelwise results, indicating stereotactic reporting. The study used BOLD fMRI (EPI) and contrasts comparing pattern discovery to control conditions. Thus it satisfies I5 (problem-solving task), I6 (whole-brain group-level healthy adults), I7 (results in MNI stereotactic space / reported voxelwise results referenced), I8 (BOLD analysis), and I9 (voxelwise results available in figures/tables). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that used an arithmetic manipulation task (adding four two-digit numbers) which meets the review’s definition of problem solving (a goal-directed task requiring planning/sequencing and execution of rule-based operations to reach a correct solution). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects voxelwise analyses (SPM99) with cluster-level correction, presents activation foci in MNI space, and reports BOLD-based results. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, allowing verification of analyses and stereotactic coordinates. Therefore it satisfies I5 (problem-solving task), I6 (whole-brain group analysis in healthy adults), I7 (stereotactic coordinates in MNI space), I8 (BOLD fMRI measures), and I9 (voxelwise results reported). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

This study is a task-based fMRI investigation of numerical inductive reasoning (a form of problem solving: identifying a rule and computing the next number), conducted in healthy adult participants (young and elderly). It reports whole-brain, voxelwise GLM analyses with within-group (task vs rest) and between-group comparisons. Results are reported in MNI space and refer to supplementary tables of stereotactic coordinates; BOLD fMRI methods (T2*-weighted EPI) are used. All required inclusion criteria are satisfied (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so is complete.

This is an fMRI study of a mental rotation (visuospatial transformation) task. It meets I6 (whole-brain, group-level fMRI analyses in healthy adults), I7 (reports MNI coordinates), I8 (BOLD analysis), and I9 (voxelwise results/tables). However, it does NOT meet I5: the task is mental rotation (visuospatial transformation/same-versus-mirror judgment), which does not fit the review's definition of a problem-solving task that requires goal-directed evaluation, planning/sequencing of actions, and execution of operations to reach a previously unknown solution (e.g., semantic, algebraic, logical, mechanical problem solving). No exclusion criteria are triggered (no E3–E6). Therefore the study is excluded for failing I5.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants that examines mental calculation (abacus mental-operation) which meets the review definition of problem solving: a goal-directed task requiring rule-based operations (arithmetic) to arrive at a correct solution. The study reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses in healthy adults, uses BOLD fMRI, and provides stereotactic coordinates (MNI) for task-related activations. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not patient-only, includes within-group task effects).

This is an empirical task-based BOLD fMRI study in healthy adults using a number-series completion task that requires identifying rules and generating solutions, which fits the review’s problem-solving definition. The paper reports group-level whole-brain contrasts and flexible-factorial ANOVA results, with stereotactic coordinates (MNI) for activations and ROI coordinates, and reports BOLD (fMRI) analyses. Voxelwise/group task effects are described for contrasts (e.g., 1>0, 2>0, 2>1). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not clinical/group-comparisons-only, not non-empirical).

This is a task-based fMRI study of mathematical problem solving in healthy adult participants (N=20). The task meets the review’s problem-solving definition (goal-directed arithmetic operations requiring planning/sequencing and execution). The study reports group-level whole-brain analyses (MVPA classification across 266 brain regions and an exploratory whole-brain contrast), performs group-level statistics (ANOVAs, classifier cross-validation across participants), and reports stereotactic coordinates (e.g., HIPS and angular gyrus in Talairach space). BOLD fMRI acquisition and analyses are described. Voxelwise results are indicated as reported in tables/figures (exploratory whole-brain contrast results are listed). Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5–I9. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not a group comparison-only paper, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete.

This study is an fMRI investigation of auditory verbal working memory (continuous performance/working memory with interference) in nonpsychotic relatives and controls, not a problem-solving task as defined by the review (no goal-directed problem solving, planning/sequencing to reach novel solutions). It does include whole-brain, group-level fMRI (BOLD) effects in healthy adults, but it does not meet the core task criterion. Additionally, the provided full text does not explicitly report stereotactic coordinates in MNI/Talairach space in the excerpt supplied. Therefore I5 (problem-solving task) is not met; I7 (stereotactic coordinates explicitly reported in the provided text) is also not met. Inclusion criteria met: I6, I8. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered based on the provided content. Full text appears complete for screening (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study of analogical reasoning (A:B::C:D) in healthy adults that qualifies as a problem-solving task (inference and generation of a solution). It reports group-level BOLD fMRI analyses with normalized group maps and voxelwise results (including MNI coordinates for RLPFC peaks), satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. Methods and results include GLM-based BOLD analyses and stereotactic coordinates. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met.

Full text appears incomplete (only abstract/metadata provided). Based on available information: the task is a sentence–picture verification paradigm (language/visual strategies), which does not clearly meet the review's definition of problem solving (I5). The paper used task-based fMRI so BOLD analysis is present (I8 satisfied). However, I6 (confirmation of whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses) and I7 (reporting of stereotactic coordinates in Talairach/MNI space) cannot be verified from the abstract alone. Because key inclusion criteria (I5, I6, I7, and possibly I9) are not demonstrably met and the full text is incomplete, I exclude the study. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are explicitly met from the available content.

Exclusion decision: No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level RFX GLM in healthy adults), I7 (data transformed to Talairach space; coordinates reported for subcortical peaks and analyses done in standardized space), I8 (BOLD fMRI analyses), I9 (task-related stereotactic results reported and supplementary material referenced). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (task is a visuospatial angle discrimination/target-detection judgment, not a problem-solving task as defined by the review — it lacks elements of problem formulation followed by planning/sequencing of actions or higher-order critical thinking to derive a novel solution; it is a perceptual/decision task). Full text completeness: fulltext_incomplete=false (full Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion present). Therefore EXCLUDED because it does not meet I5 (problem-solving) despite meeting other imaging and reporting criteria.

This study should be excluded because it reports ROI-based fMRI/DTI analyses rather than whole-brain voxelwise stereotactic results. Exclusion E3 applies: analyses and reported results are ROI-based (fMRI beta values extracted from anatomically defined AAL ROIs and DTI ROIs) and there are no reported whole-brain voxelwise coordinate tables or stereotactic activation coordinates in the provided text. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of arithmetic calculation, a problem-solving task) and I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no evidence of a whole-brain group-level voxelwise analysis reported), I7 (no stereotactic coordinates in MNI/Talairach space are provided in the text), and I9 (no indication that voxelwise results are available in tables/figures/supplement). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore exclude due to ROI-only reporting (E3) and missing whole-brain/coordinate reporting required by inclusion criteria.

This study includes a task that fits the problem-solving definition (Penn Conditional Exclusion Test; abstraction/mental flexibility requires identifying sorting rules and discovering/applying strategies), fulfills whole-brain, task-based fMRI with group-level activation maps in healthy adult participants, and reports BOLD analyses. Data were normalized to MNI space and group-level statistic images and supplemental tables are referenced (whole-brain activation maps and Supplementary Table 2), satisfying stereotactic reporting requirements. Voxelwise results are available in figures/supplement. The sample comprises healthy adults and the manuscript contains full methods, results, and discussion. Therefore I5, I6, I7, I8 and I9 are met. No exclusion criteria apply (study does not report only ROI results, is not a between-group-only comparison, nor non-empirical). Full text appears complete.

This task-based fMRI study in healthy adults examined serial subtraction (problem-solving arithmetic) and multiplication recitation and reports group-level whole-brain activation and BOLD methods. However, the full text does not report stereotactic coordinates (Talairach or MNI) for task-related activations in the provided content (no tables or coordinate lists in main text or figures). Because inclusion criterion I7 (reporting stereotactic coordinates) is not met, the study cannot be included. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Inclusion criteria satisfied: I5 (problem-solving task: serial subtraction), I6 (whole-brain group-level fMRI in healthy adults), I8 (BOLD/fMRI analysis). Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (no stereotactic coordinates reported). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study does not meet the review’s definition of a problem-solving task (I5): the experimental tasks are visuospatial matching/selection problems (choose matching shape or development figure) that appear to measure visuospatial/perceptual processing and speed/accuracy, not goal-directed complex problem solving (planning/sequencing or unknown-solution generation). It does satisfy whole-brain group-level fMRI analysis (I6) and reports BOLD fMRI analyses (I8). However, the manuscript does not report stereotactic coordinates (Talairach or MNI) for task-related increases in the provided full text (I7 not met). No exclusion criteria are triggered (e.g., it is not ROI-only, not non-empirical, and includes within-group task effects). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion are present). Therefore the paper is excluded because it fails to meet I5 and I7.

Full text provided appears incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata). Based on the abstract: the study used 15O-PET in healthy adults performing an analogy mapping task and reports activations, so I5 (task-based problem-solving/analogy), I6 (group-level whole-brain activation reported in text as activations), and I8 (rCBF via PET) appear to be met. However, I cannot verify I7 (reporting of stereotactic coordinates in Talairach/MNI space) nor I9 (coordinates available in tables/figures/supplement) because the full article (methods, results tables/figures, coordinate listings) is not available. Unable to confirm key voxelwise coordinate reporting required for inclusion. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are apparent from the abstract. Therefore I exclude this record due to incomplete full text and inability to confirm I7/I9.

This is an empirical PET study in healthy adults that examines complex mental calculation (a problem-solving task involving goal-directed sequence of operations) and a visuospatial N-back task. It reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise rCBF analyses using SPM99, provides stereotactic coordinates (Talairach/MNI), and presents task-related increases in rCBF. Methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text provided, so the full text appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9) and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study using the Raven's Standard Progressive Matrices (RSPM), which is a problem-solving/analogical reasoning task requiring goal-directed selection and rule-based solution. The study reports whole-brain, voxelwise random-effects group analyses (including healthy control group effects), uses BOLD fMRI, and reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI space (explicitly stated). Voxelwise results are presented in figures and described in the text. Thus all inclusion criteria (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9) are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply: the study does not report only ROIs, does include healthy-group task effects, and is empirical. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Full text incomplete: only title/abstract/metadata provided. From the abstract, the study used BOLD fMRI in healthy adult participants and reports both ROI and image-based (whole-brain) activation patterns, and includes a verbal analogy task that meets our definition of a problem-solving task. Therefore I5, I6, and I8 appear satisfied. However, the abstract does not report stereotactic coordinate results (Talairach/MNI) nor confirm that voxelwise coordinates are provided in tables/figures/supplementary materials, so I7 and I9 cannot be verified. Because not all required inclusion criteria can be confirmed from the available text (notably I7 and I9), I exclude the study pending full-text confirmation. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met based on the abstract.

Provided content contains only title/abstract/metadata (full text incomplete). Abstract confirms task-based fMRI and task-related activations, but does not provide stereotactic coordinates or sufficient methodological detail to verify whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses or that the task meets the review's problem-solving definition. Cannot confirm inclusion criteria I5 (problem-solving task per review definition), I6 (whole-brain group-level analysis), I7 (coordinates in Talairach/MNI), or I9 (coordinate tables/figures). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered based on available content. Excluding due to incomplete/full-text absence preventing verification of all required inclusion criteria.

This study is excluded because it does not meet the review’s problem-solving task criterion. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level fMRI analyses in healthy adult participants are reported), I7 (results reported in standardized stereotactic space/MNI coordinates), and I8 (BOLD fMRI analyses reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (the task is moral decision-making between provided alternatives in everyday conflicts, not a problem-solving task requiring goal-directed planning/sequencing or generation of a previously unknown solution as defined by the meta-analysis objective). Exclusion criteria met: none (no ROI-only reporting, no patient-only contrasts, and the study reports healthy-group task effects). Full text appears complete and contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical task-based BOLD fMRI study in healthy adult participants (young adult females) that examines math calculation (exact and approximate). Approximate calculation requires computational operations, inhibition, and magnitude comparison consistent with the review’s problem-solving definition (executing operations within an algebraic/number framework). The study reports whole-brain random-effects analyses (group-level), provides stereotactic coordinates in MNI space, and reports BOLD results (tables/figures). Full article content (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not non-empirical, includes within-group task effects). Full text appears complete.

This study does not meet I5: the task is a visuospatial matching/identification task (selecting corresponding shapes/development figures) and appears to assess perceptual/visuospatial ability rather than a problem-solving task that requires goal-directed planning, sequencing, and execution of operations (critical thinking processes) as defined by the review. It does meet other inclusion criteria: group whole-brain fMRI analysis in healthy adults (I6), reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI space (I7), reports BOLD fMRI results (I8), and voxelwise results are available in text/figures (I9). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered: the paper includes whole-brain analyses (not only ROI), and reports a healthy-group task effect. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

Excluded because the experimental task does not meet inclusion criterion I5. The study uses a three-dimensional mental rotation (3DMR) task—a visuospatial mental imagery/identity judgment—which is perceptual/transformational rather than a problem-solving task as defined (goal formation, evaluation/planning/sequencing operations to reach a previously unknown solution). It does, however, satisfy I6 (whole-brain group-level fMRI random-effects analyses in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates), I8 (BOLD fMRI), and I9 (voxelwise results are reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This study used the Tower of London (ToL) planning paradigm, which qualifies as a problem-solving task (goal-directed planning/sequencing to reach a solution). It reports whole-brain task effects for the ToL (increasing task load) with group-level analyses and includes healthy adult participants (HCs were part of the sample). Stereotactic coordinates (MNI) are reported for task-related effects/interactions (e.g., left medial dorsolateral PFC x=-27 y=30 z=24) and the study used BOLD fMRI. Voxelwise results are described in the text and ROI/whole-brain thresholds and corrections are reported. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8 and I9. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

The study is an fMRI investigation of instruction-related preparatory activity and working memory manipulation (forward vs. backward recall). While it employs whole-brain BOLD imaging in healthy adults and reports stereotactic coordinates, it does not investigate a problem-solving task as defined by the review (i.e., a task requiring subjects to generate or figure out a way to reach a goal, engage in critical evaluation/planning to arrive at a previously unknown solution). The backward condition is a rule-based memory manipulation rather than an open problem-solving or planning task. Therefore inclusion criterion I5 (problem-solving task) is not met, though I6–I9 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

Full text is complete. This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that reports whole-brain group analyses with BOLD contrasts and stereotactic coordinates (MNI). However, it does not meet I5: the experimental tasks are creative idea-generation/divergent-thinking (Alternate Uses, Name Invention, Object Characteristics, Word Ends) rather than goal-directed problem-solving tasks as defined by I5 (i.e., requiring evaluation, planning/sequencing actions, or executing rule-based operations to arrive at a correct or specified solution). Therefore it fails the core problem-solving inclusion criterion. No exclusion criteria E3–E6 apply. Inclusion criteria met: I6, I7, I8, I9. Inclusion criteria not met: I5. Exclusion criteria applied: [].

This is an fMRI study of ‘theory of mind’ (mental state attribution) using story and cartoon tasks in healthy adults. It meets several methodological criteria for the review (task-based fMRI with BOLD, whole-brain group-level analyses, and stereotactic coordinate reporting). However, it does NOT examine problem-solving as defined by the review (I5): the tasks probe attribution of mental states, not goal-directed problem solving involving evaluation, planning/sequencing actions, or rule-based operations to reach a solution. Therefore it fails the essential inclusion criterion I5. Inclusion criteria met: I6, I7, I8, I9. Inclusion criterion not met: I5. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

Excluded because the task does not meet the review's definition of problem solving (I5): the study used a Judgment of Line Orientation (JLO) visuospatial working memory task, which assesses perceptual/working-memory and attention processes rather than goal-directed problem-solving involving planning/sequencing or critical-thinking operations. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level fMRI analyses in healthy adults), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), and I9 (results available in standard reporting; tables/figures are referenced). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task is not a problem-solving task per the meta-analysis definition), and I7 (stereotactic coordinates are not explicitly reported in the provided full text excerpt). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

(a) Exclusion IDs met: none. (b) Inclusion IDs met: I6 (whole-brain group-level analyses including healthy control participants are reported), I7 (results referenced to Talairach stereotaxic space and reported in tables/figures), I8 (task-based BOLD fMRI was used), I9 (voxelwise results are reported in tables/figures). (c) Inclusion IDs not met: I5 (the experimental task is a verbal fluency/word-generation task, not a problem-solving task as defined by the review which requires goal-directed planning/sequencing/operation-based problem solving across semantic, algebraic, logical, mechanical or similar rule-based frameworks). Although healthy controls are included, the cognitive paradigm does not meet the review’s definition of problem solving; therefore the study does not address the meta-analysis objective and must be excluded. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based PET study in healthy adult participants using whole-brain voxelwise analysis (SPM) of regional cerebral blood flow during creative/story-generation and association tasks. The tasks have an explicit goal (create a story or derive logical associations) and require planning, sequencing of ideas, and generation of novel appropriate solutions, meeting the review’s definition of problem-solving. The study reports group-level whole-brain results in standardized space (Talairach/MNI) and rCBF analyses. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8 and I9. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; no exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met.

This is a task-based whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adults reporting BOLD results and stereotactic coordinates, but the experimental tasks are perceptual/verbal visual-matching (same/different letter or symbol judgments), not problem-solving as defined (no goal-directed planning, sequencing, or generation of previously unknown solutions). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5. Full text appears complete.

Only title/abstract/metadata are provided (fulltext_incomplete=true). The abstract shows an fMRI study using Raven’s Progressive Matrices in healthy adults, so I5 (task-based fMRI problem-solving) and I8 (fMRI BOLD analysis) are met. However, the provided content does not allow verification of I6 (at least one whole-brain group-level analysis) or I7 (stereotactic coordinates reported in Talairach/MNI) or I9 (availability of voxelwise coordinate results). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are evident from the abstract. Because key inclusion criteria (I6, I7, I9) cannot be confirmed from the incomplete full text, the study must be excluded pending receipt of the full article.

This is a task-based group fMRI study in healthy adults performing mental arithmetic (serial addition) and verbal rehearsal. It meets several inclusion criteria (I5: the MO-numeral task involves rule-based mental calculation to reach a goal; I6: group-level, whole-brain second-level SPM analysis was performed; I8: BOLD fMRI was used). However, the provided full text does not report stereotactic coordinates (Talairach or MNI) for task-related activation peaks in the material given here, and there is no explicit indication in the main text that coordinate tables/figures with voxelwise coordinates are available in the provided content. Therefore I7 is not satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Because ALL inclusion criteria must be met and I7 is not met in the supplied full text, the study must be excluded.

This is an event-related task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=15 analyzed) using a simplified Sudoku paradigm that operationalizes problem solving (goal-directed identification and application of heuristic rules). The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (ANOVA across four task conditions) and identifies ROIs from an exploratory whole-brain analysis, plus confirmatory ROI analyses. Data were coregistered to the Talairach coordinate system and BOLD (fMRI) responses are reported; coordinates and ROI locations are described in the Appendix/tables. Multivariate voxel classification and ACT-R modeling are also applied, but the core empirical results include task-related BOLD increases and stereotactic localization. Full methods, results, and discussion are present in the provided full text. Therefore the study meets I5 (task-based problem solving fMRI), I6 (group whole-brain analysis in healthy adults), I7 (stereotactic Talairach space), I8 (BOLD analysis), and I9 (voxelwise results reported in text/tables). No exclusion criteria are met.

The study does not investigate problem-solving as defined in the review. The tasks are visuospatial discriminations/target detection (angle, colour, conjunction) that require perceptual judgements rather than goal-directed planning, sequencing, or critical evaluation to derive previously unknown solutions, so I5 is not met. Although the study is an fMRI experiment with group-level whole-brain analyses in healthy adults (I6 satisfied) and reports BOLD analyses (I8 satisfied), the provided full text does not present stereotactic coordinates (Talairach/MNI) for task-related activations required by I7; voxelwise coordinate results are not shown in the supplied content or tables/figures (I7 not met; I9 not satisfied given absent coordinates). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the paper must be excluded for failure to meet I5 and I7.

The study does not meet the review's definition of a problem-solving task (I5). Although the task involves goal-directed decision-making (defeat the computer) and manipulation, it is fundamentally an investigation of deliberate deception and performance-monitoring/conflict detection rather than assessing problem-solving processes (evaluation, planning/sequencing actions under a rule set to arrive at a correct/novel solution). The study does satisfy I6 (whole-brain, group-level analyses using SPM and voxel-wise FDR thresholds) and I8 (reports PET rCBF and fMRI BOLD analyses). However, stereotactic coordinates (I7) are not provided in the supplied full text (results describe clusters and Brodmann areas but no x,y,z coordinates or tables/figures with coordinates are present), and no indication that coordinate tables/figures are available (I9 not met). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion). Therefore, exclude.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (N=13) using whole-brain BOLD analyses. The cognitive task includes serial subtraction (rule-based arithmetic requiring goal-directed operations to arrive at a correct answer), which fits the review’s problem-solving definition (goal plus applying operations within a rule set). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results with stereotactic localization referenced to Talairach space and presents activation tables/figures (satisfying coordinate reporting). Methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text. Thus inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8 and I9 are satisfied. Note: although the paradigm is a divided-attention verbal learning + arithmetic task rather than a pure problem-solving paradigm, the serial subtraction component constitutes a problem-solving/arithmetical task relevant to the review.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that investigates a representation-matching/problem-solving task involving evaluation, mapping of symbolic and graphical representations, and arithmetic operations (REP1-3). It reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses (two-sample t-tests comparing higher vs lower competence groups) using SPM5, with task-related BOLD results and stereotactic coordinates reported in MNI space (tables/figures). These features satisfy the meta-analysis requirements for a task-based fMRI problem-solving study with whole-brain voxelwise results. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

The study is excluded because it does not meet the review’s definition of a problem-solving task (I5). The experiment investigates anticipatory network reconfiguration for a perceptual discrimination/attention task (color vs. motion) rather than goal-directed problem solving involving planning/sequencing, evaluation, or rule-based operations to reach a novel solution. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level fMRI in healthy adults), I8 (BOLD analysis reported), and I9 (voxelwise results/supplementary maps are indicated). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task is not a problem-solving paradigm as defined) and I7 (stereotactic coordinates in Talairach/MNI are not explicitly reported in the provided full text). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered based on the provided full text. Full text appears complete for screening purposes (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

Exclusion E3 met: the paper reports ROI-based analyses (SSI and ROI functional connectivity) without providing a whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analysis or tables of stereotactic coordinates. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of a problem-solving Tower of London task) and I8 (reports BOLD/fMRI analyses). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no evidence of a reported whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analysis), I7 (no stereotactic Talairach/MNI coordinates reported in the provided full text), and I9 (no indication that voxelwise coordinate results are available in tables/figures/supplementary). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

The study is excluded because it does not report stereotactic coordinate results (Talairach or MNI) required by inclusion criterion I7. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of mental arithmetic—mental addition/subtraction of fractions, which meets the review definition of problem solving), I6 (whole-brain voxelwise random-effects group analyses performed on healthy adult participants), and I8 (task-related fMRI BOLD EPI acquisition and GLM analysis). Inclusion criterion not met: I7 (no stereotactic coordinates for task-related activations are provided in the provided full text; several results are described anatomically and some data are noted as 'data not shown', but no Talairach/MNI coordinates or coordinate tables/figures are present). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. The full text appears to contain core sections (introduction, methods, results, discussion) so fulltext_incomplete is set to false.

Decision: EXCLUDE. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I6 (study includes whole-brain, group-level fMRI analyses including healthy adult controls), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates for task activations), I8 (BOLD fMRI analyses reported), I9 (voxelwise coordinate results reported in the text/ROIs). Inclusion IDs not met: I5. The experimental task is a probabilistic decision-making/beads task (deciding which lake fish originate from), which primarily probes uncertainty monitoring and decision-making rather than a multi-step problem-solving process involving planning/sequencing actions or applying rule-based operations to arrive at a previously unknown solution as defined for this review. Thus the study does not meet the meta-analysis' definition of a problem-solving task. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants (university students) that used an arithmetic word-problem task requiring goal-directed problem solving (encoding, planning/translating, and executing arithmetic operations). The study reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (multiple regression) with BOLD fMRI data, provides stereotactic coordinates in MNI space, and presents significant clusters (cluster-level FWE correction) in tables/figures. All required inclusion criteria (I5–I9) are satisfied. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only reporting, patient-group-only contrasts, non-empirical paper) apply. Full text includes background, methods, results, discussion, and conclusions, so the fulltext appears complete.

This task-based fMRI study examines logical/transitive reasoning (linear-order inference), which fits the review’s problem-solving definition (goal-directed logical/semantic operations to derive previously unpresented relations). It reports whole-brain, group-level analyses (mixed-effects FLAME; cluster-corrected thresholds) and provides stereotactic (MNI) peak coordinates. The imaging modality is BOLD fMRI with voxelwise results reported in text/tables/figures. Although participants include a sub-clinically depressed group, the study also includes a healthy adult control group (non-depressed) and reports task-related activation maps for that group and for all participants combined. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not non-empirical, includes within-group task effects). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that examines probabilistic/inductive reasoning (decision making under uncertainty), which constitutes problem solving (goal-directed inference, evaluating competing hypotheses, and choosing actions based on evidence). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise fixed-effects group analyses (with results corrected for multiple comparisons), provides stereotactic coordinates (converted to Talaraich/MNI space), and reports BOLD fMRI measures. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study of transitive reasoning (logical problem solving) in healthy adults, matching the review’s problem-solving domain. The study used whole-brain GLM analyses (including whole-brain localizer contrasts) at the group level and reported stereotactic coordinates in MNI space. BOLD fMRI analyses are explicitly described and reported. Although several main effects were tested within functionally defined ROIs, the paper also conducted whole-brain localizer contrasts and voxelwise small-volume correction analyses, so results are not limited to ROI-only reporting. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study satisfies the inclusion criteria for task type (I5), group-level whole-brain analysis (I6), stereotactic coordinate reporting (I7), BOLD analysis (I8), and acceptability of voxelwise results presentation (I9). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

The study is a task-based fMRI experiment of analogical reasoning in healthy adults and reports group-level whole-brain analyses using BOLD fMRI, so inclusion criteria I5, I6, and I8 are satisfied. However, the provided full text does not report stereotactic coordinates (Talairach or MNI) for task-related increases; although the methods describe transformation to Talairach space and display of activation by Brodmann areas, no coordinate tables or coordinate values are present in the supplied content. Because inclusion criterion I7 (explicit stereotactic coordinate results) is not met in the provided text, the study cannot be included. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This study does not meet inclusion criterion I5. Although it is a task-based, whole-brain BOLD fMRI study in healthy adults reporting stereotactic coordinates (satisfying I6, I7, I8, and I9), the experimental task is associative learning/conditional label retrieval (mapping chords to arbitrary numbers) and investigation of conditional associative memory rather than a problem-solving task as defined in the review (goal-directed planning, evaluation, sequencing actions or executing operations to derive a previously unknown solution). No elements of planning/critical evaluation or rule-based problem solving to reach a novel solution are present; the task tests learned stimulus–label retrieval. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I6, I7, I8, I9. Inclusion IDs not met: I5.

This is a task-based BOLD fMRI study of relational/analogy and visuo-spatial reasoning that meets the meta-analysis objective of problem-solving across domains. It (I5) uses goal-directed tasks requiring relation extraction, mapping, inference, and verification (problem-solving operations). It includes healthy adult participants and reports group-level, whole-brain contrasts (I6). Task-related activation is reported with stereotactic MNI coordinates (I7). The study uses BOLD fMRI (I8) and presents voxelwise results/coordinates in the main text (I9). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; empirical healthy-group task effects present). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, task-based PET study in 15 healthy adults using whole-brain SPM voxelwise analyses of rCBF during a maze-learning task that requires planning/sequencing and trial-and-error to find a path (meets problem-solving definition). The paper reports stereotactic Talairach coordinates for activation foci and provides group-level task-related rCBF increases. The full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9, and violates no exclusion criteria.

The study uses an fMRI Sudoku problem-solving task in healthy elderly adults and reports BOLD responses, but the analyses are restricted to predefined bilateral PCC/precuneus ROIs with no whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results or stereotactic coordinates reported. Therefore it does not meet the whole-brain/coordinate reporting requirements for inclusion. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study of problem solving (Tower of London) in healthy adult participants (n=22). It reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses using SPM99 with cluster-level correction and provides stereotactic labeling/coordinates (Talairach) in tables/figures. The imaging modality is BOLD fMRI (EPI). Voxelwise/task-related results are presented in tables and figures. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review (I5–I9). Full text appears complete with Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and Appendix.

Excluded because the study does not provide group-level whole-brain effects in healthy adult individuals (Exclusion E5). This is a single-subject (n=1) study of a 16-year-old abacus expert, so it fails inclusion criterion I6 (requires group-level effects in healthy adults). The study does meet several other inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI of a mental addition task that fits the review's problem-solving definition), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates/Talairach), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), and I9 (voxelwise coordinate results reported). However, because I6 is not satisfied (no group-level healthy adult sample) the study must be excluded.

This is an empirical, task-based BOLD fMRI study using a verbal Trail Making Test (vTMT) that requires rule-based sequencing/alternation (goal-directed planning and execution), fitting the review's problem-solving definition. The study acquired whole-brain BOLD fMRI in seven healthy adult participants and performed group-level (intersubject) analyses using GLM. Results were transformed into Talairach space and reported as activation maps/tables (coordinates), and BOLD analyses and voxelwise, whole-brain inference (p<0.05 corrected, cluster threshold) are described. Full article contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 are met. No exclusion criteria apply.

The provided content is incomplete (only title, abstract, and metadata). While the study is a task-based PET experiment of mental calculation in healthy adults and reports rCBF results (satisfying I5 and I8), the full text required to verify all inclusion criteria is not available. The abstract does not explicitly confirm whole-brain, group-level stereotactic (Talairach/MNI) coordinate reporting (I6 and I7) nor whether voxelwise coordinate results are provided in tables/figures/supplement (I9). Per screening rules, all inclusion criteria must be verifiable; because I6, I7, and I9 cannot be confirmed from the incomplete full text, the study must be excluded at this stage. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered by the available information.

This is an empirical PET study in healthy adult participants comparing abacus experts and non-experts performing mental calculation tasks. The tasks meet the review’s problem-solving definition (goal-directed calculation using rule-based operations and sequencing), and the study reports whole-brain, group-level analyses using SPM2 with images transformed to standardized stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach). It reports rCBF results from 15O-water PET and provides voxelwise activation results presented in tables/figures (task-related increases). Thus it satisfies I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9. Full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided and appears complete for screening.

The REP (reproduction) task requires a clear goal (accurately reproduce a presented visuospatial sequence) and involves planning/sequencing of actions during the delay (mental preparation of sequential motor responses), which fits the review's operational definition of problem solving (planning/sequencing actions to reach a goal). The study is an empirical task-based fMRI BOLD investigation in healthy adults (n=8) with group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses (thresholding corrected across volume). Stereotactic coordinates in Talairach space are reported (tables/figures). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. Therefore inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8 and I9 are met. Note: the study primarily targets working memory with a planning component, so mapping to “problem solving” is somewhat narrow; confidence is moderate-high.

The study does not include a problem-solving task as defined (fails I5). It is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults and reports BOLD analyses and group-level whole-brain processing (meets I6 and I8), but the provided full text does not present stereotactic coordinate results in Talairach/MNI space for task-related increases (fails I7). Full text appears complete. Therefore exclude because it does not meet the core problem-solving criterion (I5) and lacks reported coordinates (I7).

Full text unavailable (API error). Only title, authors, journal metadata present. Cannot verify necessary inclusion criteria: I5 (uncertain if tasks qualify as 'problem-solving' per defined criteria), I6 (uncertain if whole-brain group-level analysis reported), I7 (uncertain if stereotactic coordinates are reported), I8 (uncertain if BOLD or rCBF results reported), I9 (uncertain if voxelwise results/tables provided). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) can be confirmed from the available content. Because core article content (methods, results) is missing, inclusion cannot be confirmed; study is excluded pending full-text retrieval.

This is an empirical whole-brain BOLD fMRI study in healthy adult controls and recovered anorexia patients that reports voxelwise group maps and stereotactic coordinates. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level analysis in healthy adults), I7 (reports coordinates in standard space), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), I9 (voxelwise results reported in tables/figures). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (the task is a social attribution/theory-of-mind perceptual judgment—e.g., “People: All friends?” and “Bumper cars: Same weight?”—rather than a goal-directed problem-solving task involving evaluation, planning/sequencing actions, and executing rule-based operations to arrive at a solution). No exclusion criteria were triggered (exclusion_criteria_applied=[]). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references): fulltext_incomplete=false. Therefore the paper is excluded because it does not study a problem-solving task as defined by I5.

The study is an empirical, whole-brain BOLD fMRI investigation in healthy adults and reports MNI coordinates, but it does not examine problem-solving as defined by the review (goal-directed tasks requiring planning/sequencing or executing operations to arrive at a solution). The tasks are a working memory (listening span) task and an inspection time perceptual speed task, which do not meet the meta-analysis definition of problem solving. Therefore I5 is not satisfied although I6, I7, and I8 (and I9) are met. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based BOLD fMRI study in healthy adult participants performing mental calculation, which fits the review's problem-solving definition (goal-directed, rule-based arithmetic operations). The paper reports whole-brain random-effects group analyses (FWE-corrected), provides stereotactic MNI coordinates for activations, and includes voxelwise/BOLD results. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so appears complete. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5–I9 and violates no exclusion criteria.

While this is an empirical, task-based BOLD fMRI study reporting stereotactic coordinates (I7, I8) and providing voxelwise results in text/tables (I9), it does not meet the requirement for a whole-brain group-level analysis (I6). The 1.5 T dataset imaged only a restricted cerebellar field of view and the 7 T dataset covered the cerebellum (not whole brain), so there is no whole-brain, group-level analysis of task effects in healthy adults. It is also not clear that the tasks are framed as explicit problem-solving paradigms per the review's definition (I5 not clearly met), since the cognitive tasks are verbal working memory and a constrained visuospatial navigation/motor sequencing task. Therefore the study is excluded for failing required inclusion criteria (primarily I6; also I5 not clearly met).

This is an empirical, task-based whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adults using a semantic coherence/remote associates task that requires finding a solution word (clear problem-solving/insight components). The paper reports group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses in MNI stereotactic space with BOLD fMRI contrasts and stereotactic coordinates, and task-related activations are reported across the brain (contrasts and coordinates). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus all inclusion criteria I5–I9 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study meets several methodological inclusion criteria for the review (I6, I7, I8, I9): it is a task-based fMRI study with group-level whole-brain analyses in healthy adult participants (n=9 males), reports stereotactic MNI coordinates, and reports BOLD effects (whole-brain voxelwise contrasts). However, it does NOT meet the meta-analysis substantive inclusion criterion I5: the task is a Piaget-like numerical judgment requiring inhibition of a perceptual heuristic (length-equals-number) and comparative judgment (same-number vs not-the-same-number), but it does not involve multi-step problem solving as defined (planning/sequencing actions to arrive at a previously unknown solution). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore I exclude the study because I5 is not satisfied, despite satisfying I6–I9.

The PET study reports a task in which participants build a mental 6×6 matrix from verbal instructions and must evaluate symmetry relative to an axis — a goal-directed, rule-based evaluation requiring representation, comparison, and execution of operations to arrive at the correct response, satisfying the review’s operational definition of problem solving. The study uses task-based PET with whole-brain, group-level SPM analyses in healthy adult participants (early blind and matched sighted controls), reports rCBF results, and provides stereotactic (MNI) coordinates. Thus it meets I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9. Full text appears complete (contains introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

The study is a task-based H2(15)O PET investigation including healthy adult controls with whole-brain SPM analyses and stereotactic coordinates; however the cognitive task is an N-back working memory task, which does not meet the meta-analysis definition of a problem-solving task (I5). Thus, although it satisfies I6, I7, I8, and I9, it fails I5 and must be excluded. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that implemented a chess problem-solving task (subjects asked to determine the next best move), satisfying the review definition of problem solving (goal-directed planning/choice among moves). The study reports a group-level whole-brain voxelwise contrast (game vs random) using a GLM (fixed-effects group analysis), provides stereotactic Talairach coordinates for activated regions, and uses BOLD-sensitive T2*-weighted EPI acquisition. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text is complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not between-group disease/age/gender comparisons only, and not non-empirical). Therefore all relevant inclusion criteria (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9) are met and the study should be included.

The provided full text is a retraction notice only and does not contain the article’s introduction, methods, participants, results, or stereotactic coordinate tables. Therefore I cannot verify any required inclusion criteria. Specifically, no information is present to confirm (I5) that the task meets the review’s problem-solving definition, (I6) presence of whole-brain group-level effects in healthy adults, (I7) reporting of Talairach/MNI coordinates, (I8) BOLD or rCBF analyses, or (I9) availability of voxelwise coordinate results. No exclusion criteria from the review list are explicitly met based on the available content. Because the core article content is missing (fulltext_incomplete=true), the study is excluded.

The study is a task-based whole-brain fMRI experiment in healthy adults that analyzes BOLD signal during a visuospatial angle-discrimination (clock) task. It meets inclusion criteria I6 (group-level whole-brain analysis in healthy adults), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), I7 (results reported in standardized space as implied by warping to standard space and references to tables of reported activations), and I9 (voxelwise results indicated as reported in tables/figures). However, it does NOT meet I5: the experimental task is a perceptual visuospatial discrimination (detecting a target angle) and modulation of task demand via angle/hand length; it does not constitute a problem-solving task as defined by the review (goal-directed planning, sequencing, or executing rule-based operations to derive a novel solution). Therefore the paper is excluded for failure to meet I5. Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This is an empirical task-based BOLD fMRI study of fluid reasoning/problem-solving (Induction and Visualization tasks) in healthy adults. The tasks require goal-directed reasoning (selecting the correct figure), fitting the review's problem-solving definition. The study reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses (random-effects), seed-based functional connectivity maps and contrasts between task conditions, with statistical thresholds and cluster sizes. Stereotactic coordinates for seeds and clusters are provided (Talairach space) and supplementary materials are referenced for localization tables. BOLD fMRI acquisition and analyses are described. Participants are healthy adult individuals (N=22). Therefore all inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants (n=10) that used arithmetic problem-solving (mental subtraction and multiplication), which meets the review’s definition of problem solving (goal-directed, rule-based operations to arrive at correct solutions). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses (FWE-corrected cluster results), provides stereotactic coordinates in MNI space, and reports BOLD results. Behavioral and neuroimaging methods, results, and discussion are present in full text. It is not ROI-only, not a patient/disease comparison, and is empirical original data. Therefore inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8 and I9 are satisfied; no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is a task-based PET study in healthy adults that used whole-brain SPM analyses and reported rCBF task effects for arithmetic tasks. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (serial subtraction constitutes a problem-solving/calculation task involving goal-directed operations and sequencing), I6 (group-level whole-brain analysis in healthy adults), and I8 (reports rCBF analyses). However, the provided full text does not report stereotactic coordinates in Talairach or MNI space (I7 not satisfied); although standard stereotactic space was used, coordinate results are not given in the provided content or tables. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) were triggered. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study is excluded because it does not meet I7 (reporting of stereotactic coordinates) based on the provided article content.

Full text appears incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). From available information: the study used task-based fMRI in healthy adult males (n=13) and BOLD/fMRI analyses are reported, satisfying I6 and I8. It is unclear whether the task (dynamic visuospatial imagery/three-dimensional cube comparison) meets the review's definition of a problem-solving task (I5) as stated, and the abstract does not report stereotactic coordinates in Talairach/MNI space (I7) or explicit voxelwise whole-brain coordinate tables (I9). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are clearly met based on available content. Because key inclusion criteria (I5 and I7; possibly I9) cannot be confirmed from the provided text and the full text is incomplete, the study is excluded pending access to the complete article.

This study does not meet the review's definition of a problem-solving task (I5). It is a task-based fMRI investigation of written phonemic fluency (language production and lexical retrieval) rather than a goal-directed problem-solving paradigm requiring evaluation, planning/sequencing of actions to reach a solution within a rule set. The full text is complete and shows group-level whole-brain BOLD analyses with stereotactic coordinates (I6, I7, I8, I9 satisfied). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Therefore excluded because I5 (task = problem solving) is not met. Included criteria met: I6, I7, I8, I9. Included criteria not met: I5. Exclusion criteria met: none.

This is a task-based BOLD fMRI study in healthy adults (n=64) using a picture-puzzle task (find differences) that has a clear goal-directed component (identify and report differences to arrive at a correct solution), fitting the review's operational definition of a problem-solving task. The study reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses, provides stereotactic coordinate results (with tables/figures referenced), and conducts BOLD analyses; results include task-related success>failure contrasts and whole-brain ANOVAs. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not patient/age/gender comparisons only, includes healthy-group task effects, and is empirical).

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults performing complex arithmetic (mental addition/subtraction of fractions) with group-level random-effects ICA and GLM whole-brain analyses and BOLD fMRI data. Therefore inclusion criteria I5 (problem-solving task), I6 (whole-brain group analysis), and I8 (BOLD analysis) are satisfied. However, the provided full text does not report stereotactic coordinates (Talairach or MNI) for task-related activations in the main text, tables, or explicitly state that such coordinate tables are available in figures/supplementary materials; thus it fails inclusion criterion I7. Inclusion criterion I9 (allowing coordinates in figures/supplementary material) is not clearly met from the provided content. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Because all inclusion criteria must be met and I7 (and by extension I9) are not satisfied in the provided full text, the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This study does not meet the review definition of a problem-solving task (I5). The task is a semantic synonym-judgment / letter-matching contrast (language/semantic decision), which does not involve goal-directed planning/sequencing or rule-based problem solving across domains as required by the meta-analysis. It does satisfy that whole-brain group-level effects in healthy adults were analyzed (I6) and that BOLD fMRI was used (I8). However, the provided full text does not report stereotactic coordinates (Talairach or MNI) for task-related increases in the excerpt (I7 not met), and no tables/figures in the provided text explicitly present voxelwise coordinates (I9 not met). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Therefore the article must be excluded because it fails to meet the core task-definition inclusion criterion I5 and does not provide stereotactic coordinate reporting required by I7/I9.

This is a whole-brain BOLD fMRI study in healthy adults using a mental-clock task (imagine clock faces, compare angles). The task is goal-directed and requires mental construction and comparison operations, so I5 (problem-solving-like task) is judged met. The study includes group-level whole-brain analyses in healthy adults (I6) and reports BOLD analyses (I8). However, the provided full text does not present stereotactic coordinate results in Talairach or MNI space (no coordinate tables or explicit coordinates are included here), so it fails to meet I7, which is required for inclusion. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. The full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). Therefore, exclude because I7 is not satisfied.

Although this is a task-based, whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adults reporting BOLD effects and stereotactic coordinates, the behavioral task (angle discrimination/visuospatial comparison) is a perceptual discrimination task rather than a problem-solving task as defined by the review (no evidence of goal-directed planning, sequencing, critical-evaluation or executing operations to reach a novel/constructed solution). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level fMRI), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates), I8 (BOLD analysis), I9 (coordinates/tables available). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (does not examine a problem-solving task per the specified definition). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study is a PET experiment in healthy adults and reports group-level, whole-brain analyses (multivariate PCA/CVA and voxelwise univariate comparisons) and rCBF measures, but the experimental task is a two-alternative tactile discrimination (TEST vs CONTROL) rather than a problem-solving task as defined in the review (goal-directed critical thinking, planning/sequencing or rule-based solution-finding across domains). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5. It also does not clearly report stereotactic peak coordinates in the provided full text, so I7 is not demonstrably met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, figures). Because ALL inclusion criteria must be met and I5 is not met (and I7 not demonstrated), the study is excluded.

This is an empirical task-based BOLD fMRI study of matrix/problem solving (Color Relational Complexity task) in 34 healthy adult participants. The task is goal-directed relational/matrix reasoning (meets I5). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects voxelwise analyses (I6), provides stereotactic coordinates in MNI/Talairach space (I7), and uses BOLD fMRI (I8). Voxelwise results and tables/figures are reported (I9). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not patient-group-only, not non-empirical). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete.

While this is an empirical task-based BOLD fMRI study including healthy control participants, it does not report stereotactic coordinate results in Talairach or MNI space (I7 not met). The paper reports group activation maps for five controls but provides extent as voxel counts and figures rather than a coordinates table; therefore the required coordinate reporting is absent. Additionally, the tasks are simple single-digit arithmetic (rule-based calculation) and may not meet the review’s specified definition of a problem-solving task that requires planning/critical evaluation (I5 questionable/not met). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level healthy control activation maps reported), I8 (BOLD fMRI). I9 partially satisfied by figures showing voxelwise maps but without coordinates. No exclusion criteria from the list apply. Full text appears complete.

The study is a task-based whole-brain BOLD fMRI study in healthy adults that reports stereotactic coordinates (MNI) and voxelwise results (I6, I7, I8, I9 satisfied). However, the experimental task is a 3-D mental rotation visuospatial task, which assesses visuospatial transformation and imagery rather than a problem-solving task as defined (goal-directed critical thinking, planning/sequencing actions to reach a solution). Therefore inclusion criterion I5 (problem-solving task) is not met. No exclusion criteria from the review are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I5: the task is an angle discrimination visuospatial perceptual task, not a problem-solving task as defined (goal-directed planning/sequencing/critical thinking to arrive at a novel solution). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level analyses including healthy adult controls), I7 (reports stereotactic peak coordinates), I8 (reports BOLD fMRI analyses), I9 (coordinates/results reported in main text/tables). Exclusion criteria met: none (no E3/E4/E5/E6 apply). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore excluded on the basis of failing I5 while satisfying I6,I7,I8,I9.

This study does not meet the review’s definition of a problem-solving task (I5). The tasks are working-memory n-back face- and location-matching tasks, which involve short-term maintenance and matching rather than goal-directed problem solving, planning/sequencing, or rule-based solution discovery. Additionally, the sample consists of adolescents (mean age 16.9, range 15–18), so it does not meet the requirement of healthy adult participants (I6). The study does, however, report BOLD fMRI analyses (I8) and indicates coordinate results available in supplementary material (I9). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) were triggered: whole-brain analyses were performed (not ROI-only), healthy-group task effects are reported, and this is an empirical fMRI study. Therefore the paper must be excluded because inclusion criteria I5 and I6 are not satisfied.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of problem solving (Raven-style matrix reasoning) in healthy adult participants (right-handed college students, n=8). It reports group-level whole-brain analyses using SPM99 (voxelwise linear-trend and subtraction contrasts), BOLD percent-signal change time-series, and stereotactic coordinates in Talairach space (Tables/Figures report cluster locations). Voxelwise results are presented in figures and tables. All required inclusion criteria are met (I5: problem-solving task; I6: whole-brain group analysis in healthy adults; I7: stereotactic coordinates reported in Talairach space; I8: BOLD analysis; I9: voxelwise results available in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using Raven's Progressive Matrices (a problem-solving/fluid reasoning task), with whole-brain voxelwise BOLD analyses reporting task-related activity and connectivity.
