The paper includes within-group (non-autistic healthy comparison group) whole-brain analyses of task effects and complexity, and identifies peak coordinates for seed selection and results (coordinates referenced and seeds reported), with BOLD methods clearly described. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I5 (problem-solving task), I6 (group-level whole-brain analyses including a healthy group), I7 (stereotactic coordinate results reported/indicated), I8 (BOLD fMRI), and I9 (results/coordinates available in figures/tables). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This study does not meet the meta-analysis conception of a problem-solving task (I5). The fMRI paradigm is a visuospatial matching/discrimination task (selecting a matching geometric shape) rather than a goal-directed problem-solving task requiring planning, sequencing or critical-thinking operations as defined by the inclusion criteria. It does however meet other inclusion criteria: whole-brain, group-level analysis in healthy adults (I6); reporting stereotactic coordinates (Talairach/MNI) (I7); BOLD fMRI analysis (I8); and acceptable reporting of voxelwise results (I9). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

The study uses task-based fMRI (BOLD) with a mental rotation spatial visualization task that meets the meta-analysis definition of problem solving (goal-directed mental transformation to determine ‘same’ vs ‘different’). Participants are healthy adults (college controls) and the paper reports whole-brain, group-level analyses including within-group activation maps for the control (healthy) group. Results include stereotactic coordinate reporting (MNI/Talairach; activation peak tables referenced) and voxelwise whole-brain contrasts. Therefore it satisfies I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is a task-based whole-brain BOLD fMRI study in healthy adults that directly examines semantic event sequencing (ordering pictures), which meets the review's problem-solving definition (has a goal and requires planning/sequencing/selective updating to reach it). The study reports group-level whole-brain analyses (N=12) with multiple-comparison correction (FDR/FWE), provides stereotactic coordinates in MNI space (tables/figures), and includes voxelwise BOLD results. No exclusion criteria are triggered. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I9 are satisfied.

This study uses a mental rotation (visuospatial) task rather than a task that meets our definition of problem solving (goal-directed planning/sequencing/critical thinking to derive a novel or rule-based solution). The fMRI analyses were hypothesis-driven ROI (small volume correction) analyses rather than whole-brain voxelwise group-level analyses; although MNI coordinates and BOLD results are reported for ROIs, no whole-brain group-level results are presented. Therefore it fails the problem-solving task requirement (I5) and the whole-brain group-level analysis requirement (I6), and it reports only ROI results (exclusion E3). It does meet criteria I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI space), I8 (reports BOLD fMRI analysis), and I9 (results reported in main text/tables). Full text appears complete.

Although this is an empirical, whole-brain task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that reports group-level BOLD effects with stereotactic coordinates, it does not meet the review's definition of a problem-solving task (I5). The experimental tasks are semantic relation judgments (taxonomic and sequential relation decisions) that require retrieval and classification of conceptual knowledge rather than engaging goal-directed problem solving involving planning, sequencing actions to reach a goal, or executing operations within a rule-based framework to find a previously unknown solution. Therefore I5 is not satisfied. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level fMRI in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates), I8 (BOLD analysis), I9 (coordinate results available). Inclusion criterion not met: I5. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) applied. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This study uses a task (Tower of London) that meets the review's definition of problem-solving (I5). It reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI space (I7), uses BOLD fMRI (I8), and provides voxelwise results/figures (I9). However, it does not provide whole-brain, group-level task activation results specifically for healthy adults (I6 not met). The primary analyses focus on COMT genotype effects and interactions with MDD, often combining patients and controls or reporting ROI/small-volume-corrected results; main whole-brain task effects for the healthy control group are not reported. The sample is predominantly MDD patients with a smaller healthy control group, and reported whole-brain findings are genotype-related across the combined sample rather than healthy-only task activations. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I6 and meets exclusion criterion E5.

The study uses task-based whole-brain fMRI in healthy adult participants performing a rule-based visuospatial ‘Amidakuji’ mental operation that requires a goal and sequencing/planning of operations to reach it, which fits the meta-analysis definition of problem solving. Group-level random-effects whole-brain analyses were performed, BOLD fMRI was used, and analyses reference MNI stereotactic space (used to define TMS targets). The paper reports voxelwise task-related activations and uses those coordinates for TMS targeting. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not a between-group/disease comparison, and is empirical). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8 and I9.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults but the experimental task is a verbal working memory / semantic relatedness judgment (word pairs; indicate whether words are semantically related). This does not meet the review's operational definition of a problem-solving task (I5) which requires goal-directed problem solving involving planning/sequencing operations to arrive at a correct or novel solution. The paper does meet other imaging and reporting criteria (I6, I7, I8, I9) — whole-brain group GLM, Talairach coordinates, BOLD fMRI analysis, and voxelwise results — but because it fails I5, it must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study using the Wason Selection Task (logical/deontic reasoning) in 14 healthy adult participants. The task requires goal-directed problem solving (identifying rule violations and selecting cards), meeting the problem-solving definition (I5). The study reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses (paired t-tests) with corrected thresholds (I6), provides stereotactic coordinates in MNI space (I7), and uses BOLD fMRI (I8). Coordinate results are reported in the text and supplementary materials (I9). No exclusion criteria are met: the paper presents whole-brain results (not ROI-only), reports healthy-group task effects, and is empirical. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study of a visuo-spatial reasoning (problem-solving) task (VSRT) in healthy adults (n=20). The task has an explicit goal (determine True/False), requires feature integration and rule verification (planning/sequencing and rule-based execution), meeting the problem-solving definition. The study reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (linear trend contrasts across task difficulty) using SPM, with stereotactic normalization to MNI space and reported coordinates. BOLD fMRI acquisition and BOLD-related analyses are described. Voxelwise results and ROIs based on whole-brain contrasts are presented. Therefore it satisfies I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This is a task-based BOLD fMRI study of syllogistic (logical) reasoning in healthy adult participants. The reasoning task meets the review’s problem-solving definition (logical operations applied to reach a conclusion), and the paper reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses (SPM8) in healthy adults. Results are reported with stereotactic coordinates (MNI) and voxelwise activations (main text and Supplementary Material tables/figures). Therefore it satisfies I5 (logical problem-solving task), I6 (whole-brain group-level effects in healthy adults), I7 (stereotactic coordinates in MNI), I8 (BOLD fMRI), and I9 (voxelwise results available in supplements). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study does not investigate a problem-solving task as defined in I5; it examines social truth-telling (evaluative responses about others) rather than goal-directed problem solving, planning, or executing operations to arrive at a correct solution. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain random-effects fMRI analysis in healthy adults), I7 (reports MNI stereotactic coordinates), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), I9 (voxelwise results reported in text/figures). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (task is not a problem-solving task). No exclusion criteria were triggered (none of E3–E6 apply). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the paper is excluded because it fails I5.

Primary reason: The task is a similarity judgment (feature-matching) fMRI experiment, not a problem-solving task as defined in I5 (goal-directed problem solving requiring planning/sequencing to reach a novel solution). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level fMRI analyses in healthy adults) and I8 (BOLD analysis). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (does not examine a problem-solving task per the review definition). I7 (reporting stereotactic coordinates) is not clearly provided in the provided full text (coordinates/maps are referenced as supplemental but not explicitly listed in the main text excerpt), so I7 cannot be confirmed. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion); fulltext_incomplete=false.

The study uses a task-based BOLD fMRI math processing task (ANAM Math) that requires goal-directed calculation and rule-based operations (meets I5). It includes whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses involving healthy adult controls and reports task-related activations (I6). Task-related stereotactic coordinates are reported (Talairach) and voxelwise results are presented (I7, I9). The modality is BOLD fMRI (I8). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion (fulltext complete). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, includes healthy-group task effects, empirical study).

This study should be excluded because it does not investigate a problem-solving task as defined in inclusion criterion I5. The task is a delayed item recognition (working memory) paradigm (letters and shapes) focusing on load-related activation and cognitive reserve, not on goal-directed problem solving involving evaluation, planning/sequencing, or executing operations to reach a solution within an explicit rule-based problem. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level fMRI analyses in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates/Talairach results), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), I9 (voxelwise results available). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task is memory/working-memory, not problem-solving). Exclusion criteria met: none (E3–E6 do not apply). Full text appears complete for screening.

This is an empirical, task-based whole-brain fMRI study using Raven's Standard Progressive Matrices (a fluid reasoning/problem-solving task) with voxelwise, group-level analyses. The paper reports BOLD-based whole-brain results, provides stereotactic (MNI) coordinates in tables/figures, and includes within-group task effects for non-autistic (healthy) adult participants. Although a clinical (autism) group is present, healthy control adult data and group-level healthy-task contrasts are reported. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, allowing assessment against inclusion criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study of deductive (logical) reasoning in healthy adults, so it meets I5 (logical problem-solving task) and I6 (whole-brain, group-level random-effects analysis). It also reports BOLD fMRI results, satisfying I8. However, the provided full text does not report stereotactic coordinates (Talairach or MNI) for task-related activations nor clearly indicate that such coordinate tables/voxelwise results are available in figures or supplements. Inclusion criterion I7 (reporting stereotactic coordinates) is therefore not met; I9 is not clearly satisfied either. No exclusion criteria (E3, E4, E5, E6) apply. Because all inclusion criteria must be met and I7 is not met in the provided full text, the study must be excluded.

This is a task-based, whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adults reporting BOLD results with stereotactic coordinates (meets I6, I7, I8, I9). However, the experimental task was passive viewing of addition expressions with no instruction or requirement to solve problems, plan, evaluate, or execute rule-based operations to reach a goal. Participants made no responses and were not given an explicit problem-solving goal; any calculation appears incidental/automatic. Therefore the study does not meet the review's problem-solving task definition (I5 not met). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Inclusion criteria met: I6, I7, I8, I9. Inclusion criteria not met: I5. Exclusion criteria met: none.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of deductive (logical) reasoning in healthy adults. It directly examines rule-based problem solving (evaluating logical validity under belief interference), satisfying the review’s problem-solving definition (I5). The methods report a whole-brain, group-level random-effects SPM analysis (I6), BOLD fMRI data (I8), and stereotactic/statistical results (MNI/Talairach-style Z/coordinate reporting and referenced tables/figures), satisfying I7 and I9. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion (fulltext complete). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only (E3), not limited to disease/age/gender comparisons (E4), include healthy-group task effects rather than only between-group contrasts (E5), and are empirical (not E6). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This fMRI study includes a formal deductive logic task (logic localizer) requiring participants to judge validity of arguments, which fits the review’s problem-solving definition (goal-directed, rule-based logical operations). It reports whole-brain, group-level BOLD analyses in healthy adult participants, provides stereotactic (Talairach) coordinates in tables/figures, and presents voxelwise task-related results (whole-brain contrasts and regressions). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria are met.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that explicitly investigates problem solving (integration verification task requires a goal and sequential rule-based operations to derive/verify integral solutions). It reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses (SPM2) with voxelwise thresholding (FDR q<.05) and stereotactic coordinates (MNI→Talairach) presented in tables/figures. It uses BOLD fMRI (rCBF not needed) and provides coordinate results in the main text/table. The sample is healthy adult participants. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not a between-group-only contrast, and is empirical). Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion. Thus the study meets all inclusion criteria I5,I6,I7,I8,I9 and should be included in the review.

While this fMRI study uses math (subtraction) tasks that fit an algebraic/problem-solving framework and includes healthy adult controls and whole-brain BOLD analyses, the provided full text does not report stereotactic coordinates (Talairach or MNI) for task-related activation. The methods state Talairach normalization and note supplementary data online, but no coordinate tables or voxelwise coordinate results are present in the supplied text. Because inclusion criterion I7 (reports task-related increases as stereotactic coordinate results) is not met in the provided material, the study must be excluded per the review rules. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (math subtraction tasks meet the problem-solving definition), I6 (whole-brain group-level analyses including healthy adults), I8 (BOLD analysis reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (no stereotactic coordinates reported in the provided text), I9 (no clear evidence in the provided material that coordinates are available in supplementary files). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are explicitly met in the provided text.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants using a rule-based conditional-proposition (Wason selection) task that requires evaluating and applying logical rules to determine correct responses — meeting the review's problem-solving definition (I5). The study used whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses with FDR-corrected voxelwise thresholds, reporting activated brain regions and indicating coordinate results/supplementary materials (satisfying I6, I7, I9). The neuroimaging modality is BOLD fMRI (I8). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not non-empirical, includes within-group task effects). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; supplementary coordinate tables are referenced.

This study meets the review objective and all required inclusion criteria. It is a task-based fMRI study of rule-based arithmetic tasks (addition, subtraction, multiplication), which qualify as problem-solving under the meta-analysis definition (goal-directed operations using an algebraic/rule set) (I5). It includes healthy adult participants and reports group-level whole-brain analyses using SPM with voxel-wise statistics (random-effects, voxel-by-voxel ANOVA) (I6). The study used BOLD fMRI (I8). The methods state spatial normalization to a standard SPM99 EPI template (MNI space) and describe voxel-wise activation maps and activation foci with references to figures/tables showing results, consistent with reporting stereotactic results (I7) and acceptable voxelwise reporting in figures/tables (I9). Core article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present in the provided full text, so fulltext_incomplete is false. No exclusion criteria apply.

The Embedded Figures Task used here is a visuospatial perceptual/search task rather than a problem-solving task as defined by the review (no evidence of goal-directed planning, sequencing of actions, or execution of operations within a rule-based/problem-solving framework). While the study satisfies multiple methodological inclusion requirements (whole-brain task-based fMRI with BOLD analyses, group-level effects including healthy adult controls, and stereotactic coordinates reported), it does not meet I5 (study of a problem-solving task per the review’s definition). Therefore it is excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered by the paper.

The study is excluded because the task is a reversal learning/reward prediction error paradigm (reward-based learning), which does not meet the review's definition of a problem-solving task (I5 not met). Additionally, the reported imaging results are focused on ventral striatum using small-volume correction (ROI-focused), and the paper does not present whole-brain, voxelwise task-effects at group level required by the review (E3 applies; I6 not met). The study does meet several technical reporting criteria: it reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI space (I7), uses BOLD fMRI analyses (I8), and provides voxelwise results/figures (I9). Full text appears complete. Therefore excluded for failing to meet the core task definition and whole-brain analysis requirement.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults directly comparing logical reasoning and mathematical calculation (problem-solving tasks involving goal-directed evaluation/planning/execution under rule sets). It implemented whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses (ANOVA across subjects) with cluster correction and reports ROIs and activation maps; BOLD fMRI was used. The manuscript indicates stereotactic localization of activations (ROIs listed in tables/figures) consistent with reporting coordinates in standardized space. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so it appears complete for screening purposes.

This study is excluded because it does not investigate a problem-solving task as defined by the review (fails inclusion criterion I5). The task is a visuospatial working memory (PAL) paradigm manipulating mnemonic load, not a goal-directed problem-solving task requiring planning/sequencing to reach a novel solution. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level fMRI analyses with healthy control participants), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates, e.g., MNI), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), I9 (voxelwise results reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task is working memory, not problem solving). Exclusion criteria met: none (E3–E6 not applicable). Full text appears complete and contains methods, results, and discussion. Given the mismatch with I5, the study must be excluded from the problem-solving meta-analysis.

While this is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adults reporting group-level voxelwise BOLD results (meets I6, I8) and presents voxelwise results in figures (meets I9), it does not examine a problem-solving task as defined by the review (fails I5). The task is a perceptual/spatial perspective-taking/mental-rotation judgment rather than a goal-directed problem solving/planning/execution task. In addition, the manuscript does not report stereotactic coordinates in Talairach or MNI space in the provided text (fails I7). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study reports a task that requires goal-directed manipulation of verbal items using an explicit rule (identify the next letter in the alphabet for highlighted letters) and subsequent decision about probe membership—i.e., sequencing/planning and rule-based operations to arrive at a correct response, meeting the review's operational definition of problem solving. It uses task-based BOLD fMRI with whole-brain, group-level statistics in healthy adults, reports stereotactic coordinates (MNI) of task-related increases, and provides voxelwise results in the main text. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Although this study uses whole-brain task-based BOLD fMRI with group-level healthy adult participants and reports stereotactic coordinates (MNI/Talairach) in tables/figures, it does not clearly examine a problem-solving task as defined by the review. The task is a visuospatial matching/selection task (select the correct figure among alternatives) that primarily assesses visuospatial/perceptual processing and accuracy, without evidence of goal-directed problem-solving processes involving planning, sequencing, or executing rule-based operations to reach a novel solution. Therefore I5 (problem-solving task) is not met. All other relevant inclusion criteria (I6, I7, I8, I9) are satisfied. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

Primary exclusion: the task (Hayling Test) targets verbal initiation/suppression and word-retrieval/inhibition (executive/language processes) rather than a problem-solving task as defined in I5 (goal-directed planning/sequencing and rule-based solution-finding across domains). The study does meet I6 and I8: it is a PET study with group-level whole-brain SPM analyses in healthy adult participants reporting rCBF task effects. However I7 is not met based on the provided full text: stereotactic coordinates (Talairach or MNI) for task-related increases are not reported or visible in the supplied content (results describe regions/Brodmann areas but no coordinates or coordinate tables are present). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore excluded because I5 (problem-solving task) is not satisfied, and I7 (stereotactic coordinates) cannot be confirmed.

This is an fMRI, task-based, within-subject study of causal reasoning in healthy adults that reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses and BOLD results (meets I5, I6, I8). However, the provided full text does not report stereotactic coordinates (Talairach or MNI) for task-related activations — results are described by anatomical regions and Brodmann areas only. Because inclusion criterion I7 (reporting stereotactic coordinates) is not satisfied in the provided document, the study must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered based on the available content. Full text appears complete for methods/results/discussion, so fulltext_incomplete is set to false.

Excluded because the experimental task does not meet inclusion criterion I5: the study investigates theory-of-mind (false belief) and counterfactual inference tasks rather than an explicit problem-solving task involving a goal plus planning/sequencing/execution to reach that goal. The study does meet inclusion criteria I6 (whole-brain group-level fMRI in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates), I8 (BOLD analysis), and I9 (voxelwise results reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

Full text reviewed in full. Primary reason for exclusion: study reports only ROI-based voxelwise analyses rather than a whole-brain group-level analysis (Exclusion E3). Satisfied inclusion criteria: I7 (stereotactic coordinates reported), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis reported), I9 (voxelwise results/coordinates presented in the main text). Not satisfied inclusion criteria: I5 (task is an auditory working-memory/mPASAT task — primarily a verbal working memory/mental arithmetic task and not clearly defined as a problem-solving task as required), and I6 (no whole-brain group-level analysis; between-group statistics were restricted to a priori ROIs). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Thus excluded per E3; lack of I5 and I6 prevents inclusion.

Excluded because the study reports only region-of-interest (AROI) analyses rather than whole-brain voxelwise results (Exclusion E3). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level effects in healthy adults) and I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (the task is a numerical/inhibition Piaget-like judgment, not clearly a multi-step problem-solving task as defined by the review), I7 (no stereotactic coordinates reported for task-related activations in the provided text), I9 (no voxelwise coordinate tables/figures with coordinates are provided in the full text excerpt). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-switching/response-shifting fMRI study assessing attentional control and executive switching, not a problem-solving task as defined by the meta-analysis (no goal-directed problem solving that requires planning/sequencing to discover a new solution). It does include whole-brain group BOLD analyses with stereotactic coordinates. Full text appears complete.

This study does not meet the review’s core content requirement. It is a PET meta-analysis investigating brain networks active during the conscious resting state (REST) across various cognitive tasks, rather than a task-based PET/fMRI study specifically examining a problem-solving task as defined (goal-directed problem solving involving evaluation, planning/sequencing, and rule-based execution). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain analyses in healthy adults), I7 (stereotactic coordinates reported/MNI), I8 (rCBF PET analyses reported), I9 (voxelwise results available in text/tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (does not study a problem-solving task per the review definition; primary aim is resting-state network characterization). Exclusion criteria met: none ([]) . Full text appears complete and contains methods, results and discussion (fulltext_incomplete=false). Therefore EXCLUDED.

The study is an fMRI investigation of attention switching and working memory updating, not a problem-solving task as defined in I5 (no goal-directed problem solving requiring planning/sequencing to reach a (previously unknown) solution). It does, however, meet multiple methodological inclusion criteria: I6 (whole-brain group-level fMRI in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), and I9 (voxelwise results available). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore excluded because I5 is not satisfied.

Full-text review: The task used (2-back n-back) is a verbal working memory task and does NOT meet the review's problem-solving task definition (I5 not met). The study does satisfy other inclusion criteria: I6 (conducts whole-brain group-level analyses including a healthy control group), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates in tables), I8 (reports BOLD fMRI results), and I9 (voxelwise results are reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria are triggered (no ROI-only reporting, healthy-group task effects are present, study is empirical). Therefore excluded because it fails to meet I5 (problem-solving task). Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I6, I7, I8, I9. Inclusion IDs not met: I5.

This is an empirical event-related fMRI study in healthy adult participants that tests three-term relational (deductive) reasoning — a problem-solving task requiring goal-directed evaluation and execution of logical operations. The study reports group-level, whole-brain analyses using SPM with normalization to the MNI template and voxelwise inference (voxel-level correction reported), and BOLD contrast results summarized in the results (with coordinates/tables indicated). Methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study using Raven's Progressive Matrices (a canonical problem-solving/fluid-reasoning task) in 79 healthy adult participants. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level analyses (ICA and within-subject ANOVA) on BOLD fMRI data and presents voxelwise spatial results; Supplementary Table I is described as providing voxel maxima and locations for RPM–rest contrasts (stereotactic coordinates in standardized space). Voxelwise/maps results are presented in figures and supplement. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

This is excluded because the in-scanner task does not meet the review's definition of a problem-solving task (I5). The study uses a three-back working memory task with lure trials to probe attentional control, not a goal-directed novel problem-solving paradigm requiring planning/sequencing to arrive at previously unknown solutions; Raven's Advanced Progressive Matrices (a problem-solving measure) was administered outside the scanner and not used as the imaging task. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level fMRI analysis in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates), I8 (reports BOLD fMRI analyses), I9 (voxelwise results reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (in-scanner task is working memory/attentional control, not a problem-solving task as defined). Exclusion criteria met: none (does not report only ROI, disease/age/gender comparisons, only between-group contrasts, or non-empirical content). Full text appears complete for screening.

This study is an event-related fMRI investigation of working memory (delayed match-to-sample with manipulation) in depressed patients and healthy controls. While it meets several methodological inclusion criteria (whole-brain group analyses in healthy adults, stereotactic coordinates reported, BOLD fMRI analysis, voxelwise results presented), it does NOT examine a problem-solving task as defined in the review (goal-directed problem solving involving planning/sequencing to arrive at a novel solution). The task is a working memory/manipulation paradigm rather than a problem-solving task across domains. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Therefore the study should be excluded for failing I5 (problem-solving task).

This paper is a methodological/review-style article describing approaches and summarizing multiple fMRI/EEG studies of insight rather than reporting an original, task-based whole-brain fMRI/PET experiment with stereotactic coordinate results. It does not present group-level whole-brain coordinate tables (Talairach/MNI) or explicit voxelwise BOLD/rCBF stereotactic results suitable for meta-analysis. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E6 (non-empirical paper / methods review without original human data reported in coordinate space). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no explicit whole-brain group-level stereotactic results reported), I7 (no Talairach/MNI coordinates provided), I5 (the article discusses paradigms but does not present a single detailed task-based fMRI/PET study with methods/results), and I8 (no explicit BOLD/rCBF coordinate analyses provided in the text).

This study does not investigate problem-solving as defined in the meta-analysis objective. It is a task-based whole-brain fMRI study of spontaneous mentalizing/theory-of-mind during virtual reality navigation in healthy adults, reporting MNI coordinates and BOLD results. However, the experimental contrast and behavioral target focus on mentalizing (attributing thoughts/intentions) rather than on problem-solving processes (goal identification plus structured planning/sequencing or rule-based operations to reach a solution). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

I exclude because the experimental task is a letter-matching/branching executive-control paradigm that manipulates working memory and attentional allocation; it does not require participants to formulate and discover a strategy or plan to reach a goal in the sense of problem-solving as defined by I5. (a) Exclusion IDs met: none. (b) Inclusion IDs met: I6 (whole-brain group-level fMRI in healthy adults), I7 (stereotactic coordinates reported), I8 (BOLD/fMRI analyses reported), I9 (voxelwise results reported in tables/figures). (c) Inclusion IDs not met: I5 (task does not operationally meet the review's problem-solving definition—no goal-directed planning/sequencing to find a novel solution). Full text appears complete.

Full text provided appears to be limited to title/abstract/metadata (fulltext_incomplete=true). From the abstract, the study used task-based PET rCBF in healthy adults performing the Wisconsin Card Sorting Test (complex reasoning) and an auditory shadowing task, so it likely meets I5 (problem-solving-like WCST), I6 (whole-brain SPM group analyses in healthy adults), and I8 (rCBF analysis). However, the provided content does not include the full methods/results needed to confirm I7 (reporting of stereotactic coordinates in Talairach/MNI space) nor I9 (voxelwise results available in tables/figures). Because I7 cannot be verified from the incomplete full text, the study does not meet all required inclusion criteria as presented and therefore is excluded pending full-text availability. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are directly met based on the available abstract. Full text incomplete flag set.

This study is a multivariate fMRI classification/feature-selection paper distinguishing when subjects viewed a sentence versus a picture (sentence–picture verification). It does not test a problem-solving task as defined (no goal-directed problem-solving, planning/sequencing, or rule-based solution generation): therefore I5 not met. Although it uses fMRI signals (BOLD) so I8 is met, the paper does not report voxelwise stereotactic coordinate results (Talairach/MNI) or group-level whole-brain statistical activation coordinates; selected voxels are described anatomically but no coordinate tables or group-level stereotactic maps are provided. Thus I7, I6, and I9 are not satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete for screening (methods, results, discussion present). Conclusion: EXCLUDE because it fails I5, I6, I7, and I9 while only satisfying I8.

This PET study reports whole-brain, group-level task effects in healthy adult participants performing the Operation Span (a dual-task involving algebraic equation verification and memory updating). The task involves executing algebraic operations and rule-based evaluation (meeting the review definition of problem-solving operations), and the paper reports voxelwise rCBF analyses with stereotactic coordinates (tables/figures) from whole-brain contrasts. Therefore it satisfies I5 (task involves algebraic/evaluative operations), I6 (whole-brain group-level effects in healthy adults), I7 (stereotactic coordinates reported), I8 (rCBF/PET analysis), and I9 (coordinates reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not limited to between-group/disease comparisons, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study is excluded because it does not examine problem-solving as defined in the review (I5 not met). It is a methodological/chronometry fMRI study of sequential perceptual, motor and verbal processes (visuo-motor tapping, word reading and rehearsal), not a goal-directed problem-solving task requiring planning/sequencing to reach a novel solution. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group analysis in healthy adults), I7 (stereotactic coordinates reported), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), I9 (voxelwise/coordinate results available). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (problem-solving task). Exclusion criteria met: none. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study is a task-based BOLD fMRI investigation of the Trail Making Test (TMT) in healthy adults. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (TMT involves goal-directed planning/sequencing and rule-based execution consistent with problem-solving/set-shifting), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analysis in healthy adults), I8 (reports BOLD fMRI analysis). The manuscript also indicates voxelwise results are available in figures/tables (I9). Inclusion criterion not met / could not be verified: I7 — the provided full text does not contain stereotactic coordinates in Talairach or MNI space (tables/coordinate lists appear omitted). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Because the stereotactic coordinate reporting (I7) could not be confirmed from the supplied full text and the activation tables appear missing, I set fulltext_incomplete=true and exclude the study pending access to the complete article with coordinate tables.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adults investigating analogical reasoning. The task is goal-directed and requires identifying and integrating relations (manipulation, planning/sequencing of relational operations) consistent with the meta-analysis definition of problem solving (I5). The study reports group-level whole-brain analyses (SPM99), BOLD fMRI results, and provides stereotactic coordinates (Talairach) in tables/figures (satisfying I6–I9). The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present and complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not between-group-only, not non-empirical). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

(a) Exclusion criteria met: none. (b) Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task is simple algebraic/arithmetic problem solving X×Y+Z), I6 (whole-brain, group-level voxelwise fMRI analyses in healthy adults using SPM8), I8 (task-based BOLD fMRI reported), I9 (voxelwise results presented in figures). (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I7 — the paper does not report stereotactic coordinates (Talairach or MNI) for task-related increases or provide coordinate tables or numeric coordinate results in the text or supplements. Because I7 is required and is not satisfied, the study must be excluded. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of mental state (theory-of-mind) ascription (beliefs vs desires), not a problem-solving task as defined by the review (goal-directed planning/sequencing/executing operations to arrive at a solution). Inclusion criteria satisfied: I6 (whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses reported), I7 (results reported in standardized stereotactic Talairach space), I8 (BOLD fMRI analyses), I9 (voxelwise/coordinate results available). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (task is not a problem-solving task per the review definition). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore excluded for failing I5.

This is an fMRI study of causal verbal fluency (generating causes/reasons to cue words) in healthy adults. It includes whole-brain group analyses (SPM8), BOLD contrast results, and presumably stereotactic (MNI) reporting, meeting I6, I7, I8 and I9. However, the experimental task is a semantic/verbal fluency / associative retrieval paradigm rather than a domain-general problem-solving task as defined by the review (I5). The task lacks an explicit problem structure requiring planning/sequencing actions to reach a correct or novel solution; participants generate associations/reasons rather than performing goal-directed operations to solve a defined problem. Therefore it does not meet I5 and must be excluded. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical behavioral study of arithmetic strategies in healthy adults but does not include any task-based fMRI or PET data or analyses. The full text is complete. Inclusion criteria met: none (the study examines problem solving behaviorally but does not perform neuroimaging). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (not a task-based fMRI or PET study), I6 (no whole-brain group-level analysis), I7 (no stereotactic coordinates reported), I8 (no BOLD or rCBF analyses reported), I9 (no voxelwise neuroimaging results). No exclusion criteria from the review list apply (e.g., not an ROI-only paper, not a between-group-only contrast, and not a review). Therefore it must be excluded from the meta-analysis focussed on whole-brain task-based fMRI/PET studies.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults using a multiple-choice electric-circuit task that requires evaluating circuits and applying conceptual rules to determine correctness, which fits the review’s problem-solving definition. The study reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM8) in healthy adult participants (n=22), provides stereotactic coordinates in MNI space, and reports BOLD-based fMRI contrasts with coordinate tables/figures. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the record is complete. No exclusion criteria apply.

The study is an fMRI investigation of mental rotation (visual–spatial imagery) in surgery residents. It clearly meets I6 (group-level, whole-brain fMRI contrasts for healthy adult participants) and I8 (reports BOLD fMRI analyses). However, it does not meet I5: the task (Mental Rotations Test) is a visuospatial transformation/imagery task and does not clearly qualify as a problem-solving task as defined (goal-directed planning/sequencing or evaluation operations to arrive at a previously unknown solution). Additionally, the provided full text does not report stereotactic coordinates (Talairach/MNI) for cluster peaks in the excerpt, so I7 is not satisfied based on available content. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (background, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study is excluded because it fails to meet I5 (problem-solving task) and I7 (stereotactic coordinate reporting).

This study is EXCLUDED because it does not investigate a problem-solving task as defined in the review (I5 not met). The reported tasks are letter-detection and visuospatial location decisions on identical word stimuli — perceptual/categorical decision tasks that do not require planning, sequencing, evaluating options, or generating solutions to a novel goal-directed problem. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain task-based fMRI with group-level healthy adult participants), I7 (stereotactic coordinates reported), I8 (BOLD signal reported), I9 (voxelwise results and coordinates reported). Exclusion criteria met: none (no E3–E6 applied). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults using a Kanji-grapheme-puzzle that meets the review’s definition of a problem-solving task (goal-directed combination of elements) and reports whole-brain group analyses using BOLD fMRI. However, the provided full text does not present stereotactic coordinate results (Talairach/MNI) or explicit voxelwise coordinate tables/figures in the content supplied, so it does not satisfy I7 (and I9 is not clearly satisfied from the provided text). Therefore it cannot be included per the requirement to report stereotactic coordinate task-related increases. All other inclusion criteria met are listed below.

This is a task-based fMRI study of scientific (insightful) problem solving in healthy adult participants using an event-related learning-prototype→problem paradigm that meets the review’s problem-solving definition. The study conducted whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses (HFF>OHFF contrast) and corrected for multiple comparisons. Results are reported in stereotactic (Talairach) space with peak coordinates and cluster volumes (voxelwise/clusterwise maps/tables referenced), and analyses are BOLD fMRI. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (participants, tasks, imaging acquisition/analysis), Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8 and I9. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete.

Exclusion rationale: No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level fMRI analysis in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates), I8 (reports BOLD analysis), I9 (voxelwise results provided in tables/figures). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task is a visuospatial matching/selection task, not a problem-solving task as defined by the review — it lacks a requirement to formulate a plan, evaluate alternatives, sequence actions to reach a novel solution or engage critical thinking processes characteristic of problem solving). The full text is complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study is excluded because it does not meet I5.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants that examines mental calculation tasks which require rule-based operations, decomposition/recomposition strategies, and sequencing of steps (i.e., problem-solving processes). The study performed whole-brain statistical parametric mapping at the group level (fixed-effects across subjects), normalized data to a standard template (MNI) and reports activation foci (coordinates) in tables/figures. It used BOLD fMRI (gradient-echo EPI) to assess task-related signal changes. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, enabling adequate assessment. Therefore it satisfies all required inclusion criteria (I5–I9) and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is a methods paper on overt verbal responding during fMRI, not a task-based study of problem solving. Inclusion criteria: I8 is met (fMRI/BOLD data reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (does not study a problem-solving task; task involves verbal responding/artifact evaluation rather than goal-directed problem solving), I6 (unclear/does not explicitly report whole-brain, group-level effects in healthy adults), I7 (no report of stereotactic coordinates in the abstract/full text provided), I9 (no evidence that voxelwise coordinate results are available). No exclusion criteria from the list (E3–E6) are explicitly met. Full text appears incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided), so fulltext_incomplete=true. Given mismatch with the review objective and missing required inclusion elements, exclude.

This is an empirical task-based BOLD fMRI study in healthy adult participants (n=42) using arithmetic problem-solving (multiplication and subtraction, presented in different formats). The arithmetic tasks are goal-directed and require rule-based operations (fits the review's problem-solving definition). The paper reports group-level whole-brain analyses (one-sample t-tests) with voxelwise results in MNI space and cluster-level FWE correction, provides stereotactic coordinates in tables/figures, and describes BOLD acquisition and analyses. Voxelwise results are reported and accessible in the main text/tables. The full article text (background, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is a task-based, whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adults (I6) reporting BOLD results (I8). However, the experimental task is a semantic similarity/judgment task (deciding whether object pairs share manipulation or function), which does not meet the review's definition of a problem-solving task (I5 not met). Additionally, the provided full text appears to be incomplete: it contains placeholders for tables/figures and does not report stereotactic coordinates in Talairach/MNI space within the supplied content, so I7 cannot be verified (fulltext_incomplete=true). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Therefore the study is excluded because it does not satisfy the problem-solving inclusion criterion (I5) and the available text does not permit confirmation of reported stereotactic coordinates (I7).

This is a task-based whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adults that reports Talairach coordinates and BOLD effects, but the task is empathic/emotional-state reasoning (inferring causes of facial expressions) rather than a problem-solving task as defined by I5 (goal-directed planning, sequencing, or executing operations to arrive at a previously unknown solution). Therefore it fails to meet inclusion criterion I5. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level fMRI in healthy adults), I7 (stereotactic coordinates reported in Talairach space), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), I9 (voxelwise results reported in main text/tables). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (task is not a problem-solving task per the review definition). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that uses a rule-guided category judgement and substitution task in which the suppression/anomalous categorisation condition requires rule application and strategy generation to produce alternative category responses (i.e., selection/planning under constraints), which fits the review's broad definition of problem solving. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level analyses (data from n=6 after motion exclusions), uses BOLD T2*-weighted imaging, and provides stereotactic Talairach coordinates for task-related activations. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion with voxelwise results/maps. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=11) using a trial-and-error problem-solving task where subjects must discover a correct stimulus and shift from exploration to exploitation. It reports whole-brain, group-level analyses, provides stereotactic coordinates in MNI space for activation peaks, and uses BOLD fMRI measures. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5 (task-based problem-solving paradigm), I6 (whole-brain group analysis in healthy adults), I7 (MNI coordinates reported), I8 (BOLD/fMRI analysis), and I9 (voxelwise results reported in main text/supplement). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not only group comparisons, includes healthy task effects, and is empirical). Full text appears complete.

The study is excluded because it does not meet I5 (problem-solving task). The fMRI task is a complex visuomotor/ship-control task focused on motor control and visuospatial attention and skill acquisition rather than on problem-solving as defined (goal-directed critical thinking, rule-based sequencing to reach novel solutions). The study does meet other inclusion criteria: I6 (whole-brain, group-level fMRI analyses in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic MNI coordinates), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), and I9 (voxelwise results reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is a task-based fMRI study of deductive/ logical problem solving (conditional and relational reasoning), which fits the review’s definition of problem solving (logical rule-based tasks). It reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses in healthy adult participants (N=13 after exclusions). Results are reported as stereotactic coordinates in MNI space and derive from BOLD fMRI analyses. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria (I5–I9) and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete for screening purposes.

Full text appears incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). (a) Exclusion IDs met: none ( []). (b) Inclusion IDs met: I8 (study uses event-related fMRI/BOLD). (c) Inclusion IDs not met / cannot be verified from provided content: I5 (uncertain whether the number-comparison task qualifies as a 'problem-solving' task per definition), I6 (cannot confirm explicit whole-brain group-level analyses from full text), I7 (stereotactic coordinates in Talairach/MNI not shown in the provided content), I9 (voxelwise results/tables/coordinates cannot be confirmed available). Because the full text is incomplete, I cannot verify all required inclusion criteria. Per instructions, fulltext_incomplete=true takes precedence; study is excluded until full text is available for complete assessment.

This is an fMRI study of mental rotation and visuospatial working memory (manipulation of 2-D matrices and 3-D cubes) in healthy adults, with whole-brain group analyses, stereotactic coordinates (Talairach), and BOLD results reported. Thus it meets I6, I7, I8, and I9. However, the task is mental rotation/working-memory manipulation rather than a problem-solving task as defined by the review (goal-directed problem solving involving planning/sequencing or rule-based operations to derive a novel solution). Therefore it does not meet I5 (problem-solving task). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete. Excluded because I5 is not satisfied.

This is a task-based, empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants that examines logical problem-solving (identifying contradictions; manipulation of logical operators All/Some). The task requires goal-directed critical thinking and application of logical rules to reach judgments, matching the review’s problem-solving definition. The study reports group-level whole-brain BOLD analyses using SPM8, provides stereotactic coordinates in MNI space, and describes task-related BOLD increases and overlaps with EEG sources. All inclusion criteria are met (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9). No exclusion criteria apply. The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete for screening purposes (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This study is a task-based fMRI investigation of decision-making using a modified Iowa Gambling Task in substance-dependent and control participants. It reports whole-brain BOLD results with stereotactic coordinates (MNI) and task-related analyses (satisfying I7, I8, I9). However, it does not examine a problem-solving paradigm as defined by the review (I5): the IGT assesses risk-based decision-making/learning rather than goal-directed problem solving that requires planning/sequencing operations to derive a correct solution. Additionally, the paper does not present a whole-brain group-level task activation map specific to healthy controls (I6 not met); results are reported across the combined sample and as between-group contrasts. Therefore exclusion criterion E5 applies (no healthy-group task effect reported). Full text appears complete. Excluded for failing to meet I5 and I6 and for meeting E5.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI+PET study in healthy adults (n=29) using a two-step sequential decision task that requires prospective planning (model-based control) to maximize reward. The task entails a goal (maximize monetary reward) and planning/sequencing of actions based on transition structure, satisfying the review’s definition of a problem-solving process involving evaluation and planning. The study reports whole-brain, group-level fMRI analyses with BOLD results, provides stereotactic peak coordinates (e.g., x=16,y=8,z=-8; x=42,y=24,z=-14), and includes voxelwise PET Ki maps; coordinates and statistical maps are reported. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I5 (task involves planning/model-based problem solving), I6 (whole-brain group-level effects in healthy adults), I7 (stereotactic coordinates reported), I8 (BOLD analyses reported), and I9 (voxelwise results available). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met: the paper includes whole-brain analyses rather than ROI-only results, reports healthy-group task effects, and is an original empirical study. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Full text is complete. This is a task-based whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adults reporting BOLD coordinate results, but the experimental task is Theory of Mind belief attribution (true/false belief: ‘Where will he search?’) rather than a problem-solving task as defined by the review (goal-directed problem solving requiring evaluation, planning/sequencing actions, and executing operations to arrive at a solution). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (healthy adult group-level whole-brain analysis), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI/Talairach space), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis reported), I9 (voxelwise results available). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (does not study a problem-solving task per the review definition). No exclusion criteria E3–E6 apply. Therefore excluded because it does not meet I5 (task definition).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants that uses an arithmetic subtraction task (Experiment 1) and an order-judgment task (Experiment 2), both involving goal-directed operations and rule-based computations consistent with the review’s definition of problem solving (I5). The paper reports whole-brain group-level analyses (e.g., contrast [digits–words] with bilateral lateral occipital clusters) (I6), provides stereotactic MNI coordinates for task-related activations ([49 −71 9], [−44 −67 14]) (I7), and uses BOLD fMRI (I8). Voxelwise results are reported in figures and described in the text (I9). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and conclusions and appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met. Although sample size is modest (N=12), this affects generalizability rather than eligibility for inclusion.

This is an event-related task-based fMRI study of problem solving (word vs. number problems) in healthy adults (n=15 analyzed) that clearly defines problem-solving tasks and manipulations, meeting I5. Group-level whole-brain analyses were performed (contrasts vs. fixation, 2×2 ANOVA), meeting I6. The methods state images were normalized to MNI space and analyzed with SPM5, and the manuscript refers to activation maps/figures/tables, indicating stereotactic (MNI) reporting of task-related activations, satisfying I7 and I9. The study reports BOLD fMRI results, satisfying I8. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete is false. No exclusion criteria are met.

The study reports a whole-brain task-based fMRI experiment in healthy adult participants performing the PASAT/PVSAT, which requires goal-directed, rule-based arithmetic operations (sequencing and executing addition of successive digits) and thus meets the review's operational definition of a problem-solving task. It provides group-level whole-brain BOLD analyses, reports stereotactic MNI coordinates, and presents voxelwise results (activation/deactivation maps and coordinates). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of chunk decomposition as a problem-solving task in healthy adults. The task requires a defined goal (remove part of a Chinese character to form another valid character) and involves identification, planning/operation (decomposing radicals or strokes) and execution to reach a solution, meeting the review's problem-solving definition. The study reports whole-brain, group-level (random-effects) BOLD fMRI analyses (2×2 factorial), with voxelwise results and cluster statistics, and reports stereotactic coordinates (MNI converted to Talairach) and ERP data. Sample comprises healthy adult participants (N=14 included in fMRI analyses). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; therefore fulltext_incomplete is false.

While this is a task-based whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adults (meets I6, I7, I8, I9), the tasks are visuo-spatial categorical and coordinate judgment tasks (perceptual/decision judgments about dot position and distance). These do not meet the review's definition of problem-solving (I5) — they do not require goal-directed multi-step problem solving, planning/sequencing operations, or generating previously unknown solutions within a rule-based framework. Therefore the study is excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants using a mental-rotation problem which requires a goal (determine whether two cubes are the same/different) and execution of spatial transformation operations (rule-based mental rotation) to arrive at correct responses — consistent with the review’s problem-solving definition. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level analyses (ANOVAs comparing Compare vs Control), uses Talairach stereotactic space for normalization and ROI centers, and reports BOLD signal results with voxelwise findings presented in figures/tables (e.g., Table 2, Figures 2–4). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not limited to ROIs only, the study is not non-empirical, and it includes within-group task effects in healthy adults. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, conclusion). Therefore it meets I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9.

This study does not examine a problem-solving task as defined in inclusion criterion I5. The tasks are visuospatial perception and imagery (angle discrimination, mental clock imagery) requiring perceptual judgment and mental imagery, not goal-directed problem solving involving planning, sequencing, or executing operations to reach a previously unknown solution. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level fMRI analyses in healthy adults) and I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task is not a problem-solving task). I7 (reporting stereotactic coordinates) is not clearly satisfied in the provided full text (Talairach transforms and group maps are described but explicit stereotactic coordinate tables/coordinates are not provided in the excerpt). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion); fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using a reasoning/problem-solving paradigm (Wason card selection task) in healthy adults, directly examining problem-solving across domains (social exchange vs precautionary). It includes group-level random-effects whole-brain analyses and reports voxelwise results with MNI coordinates (e.g., BA10: −30,63,18; BA20: −42,−18,−21). BOLD responses are modeled and reported. The full text contains Introduction, Methods (fMRI acquisition and analysis), Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (whole-brain results are reported in addition to ROI analyses). Therefore all relevant inclusion criteria are satisfied.

This study does not examine a problem-solving task as defined by the review (I5). The experiment uses a digit-sorting working memory paradigm to index cognitive load and relate pupil dilation to BOLD responses; it is framed and analyzed as working memory/executive load rather than goal-directed problem solving requiring planning/sequencing to reach a novel solution. It does meet other inclusion criteria: whole-brain group-level fMRI analysis in healthy adults (I6), reports stereotactic coordinates in Talairach space (I7), and reports BOLD analyses (I8); voxelwise results are presented in figures/tables (I9). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore excluded because I5 not met.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using logical syllogism reasoning (a problem-solving task involving goal-directed evaluation and rule-based operations), conducted in healthy adult participants (n=17, analyses on 15). The study reports whole-brain, group-level (random effects) analyses using SPM8, provides stereotactic MNI coordinates for activations, and uses BOLD contrast (fMRI). Results are reported in-text and as cluster coordinates; supplementary tables are referenced. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9) and does not violate exclusion criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study that administers a verbal reasoning (grammatical transformation) task meeting the definition of problem solving (goal-directed logical inference and rule-based operations). It includes 20 healthy adult control participants and reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses in SPM, with stereotactic coordinates reported (MNI) for multiple task-related activations, and BOLD fMRI results (FIR/BOLD contrasts). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not a review, includes healthy-group task effects). Therefore it satisfies I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 and should be included.

This is a task-based fMRI study of propositional analogy (a goal-directed problem-solving task requiring evaluation/integration of relations to select a correct response), includes a healthy adult group and reports whole-brain group-level analyses, stereotactic coordinates (e.g., -27,50,0; 27,45,16), and BOLD fMRI results. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study using a problem-solving paradigm (Raven-like matrices) that requires goal-directed reasoning, planning/sequence processing, and rule-based operations, satisfying I5. Participants were healthy adults (n=16) and analyses report group-level whole-brain random-effects results, satisfying I6. Results and coordinates are reported in Talairach space (stereotactic coordinates) throughout the imaging results and tables, satisfying I7. The study reports BOLD fMRI analyses (contrasts of conditions), satisfying I8. Whole-brain voxelwise results are presented and ROI analyses are supplemental, and the text indicates these whole-brain results and coordinates are available, satisfying I9. No exclusion criteria apply: the study is empirical, includes healthy-group task effects, and reports whole-brain analyses rather than only ROI or between-group/disease comparisons. The full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete.

Although the study reports whole-brain, group-level task fMRI BOLD results with stereotactic coordinates (satisfying I6, I7, I8, and I9), it does not meet the review's definition of a problem-solving task (I5). The task is a stochastic reinforcement-learning / instrumental conditioning decision task (trial-and-error button presses to maximize reward) rather than a problem-solving paradigm emphasizing explicit evaluation, planning/sequencing of operations toward an unknown solution (e.g., semantic, algebraic, logical, or complex mechanical problem solving). The study focuses on reward-based learning and neural correlates of behavioral change, not on higher-order problem solving across domains. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met.

The study used a mathematical arithmetic series task that requires subjects to identify the rule and select the correct continuation, satisfying the review's definition of problem solving (I5). It is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (N=12) with group-level whole-brain analyses and random-effects statistics (I6). Results were normalized to Talairach space and ROIs/coordinates are reported (I7,I9). The study reports both BOLD and CBF (ASL) analyses and derives CMRO2, meeting the BOLD/rCBF requirement (I8). No exclusion criteria are met: the study reports whole-brain voxelwise group effects (not ROI-only), includes healthy-group within-subject task effects, and is empirical. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and is included for the meta-analysis.

This study does not examine a problem-solving task as defined in the review (I5 not met). It reports an fMRI localizer and uses BOLD analyses to identify a language-related region (so I8 is satisfied), but the manuscript does not provide clear evidence of a whole-brain group-level task-based analysis reported as stereotactic coordinates in standardized space (I6 and I7 not met based on the provided text). I9 is also not satisfied because qualifying voxelwise results or coordinates are not presented in the provided full text. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Therefore the article is excluded because it fails to meet the key inclusion requirement I5 (problem-solving task) and lacks required whole-brain coordinate reporting (I6/I7).

This study is excluded because it does not report stereotactic coordinates in standardized space (Talairach or MNI), so I7 is not met and voxelwise results are not provided as extractable coordinates for coordinate-based meta-analysis (I9 not met). It does meet I5 (mental subtraction qualifies as a problem-solving task involving planning/sequencing operations), I6 (group-level task effects reported in healthy adult subjects via pixel/voxel analyses), and I8 (BOLD fMRI). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete for purposes of screening.

This study does not meet inclusion criterion I5 (problem-solving task). The task is a modified Digit Symbol Test requiring symbol lookup, visual search, working memory updating, and graphomotor responses rather than goal-directed problem solving involving planning, sequencing, or applying rules to derive novel solutions. It does meet I6 (whole-brain, group-level fMRI in healthy adults), I7 (reports coordinates in MNI space), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), and I9 (voxelwise results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and References).

Full text is complete. This study uses a number-comparison (symbolic distance) task and fMRI/Parkinson's patient behavioral testing. It meets I6 (whole-brain, group-level effects in healthy adults in Experiment 2), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates in Talairach space), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), and I9 (voxelwise results/tables reported). However, it does NOT meet I5: the task is a magnitude comparison/decision task (selecting larger/smaller number) and is not a problem-solving task requiring goal formulation, planning/sequencing of actions, or executing operations to arrive at a novel solution. No exclusion criteria are triggered. Therefore EXCLUDED because inclusion criterion I5 is not met.

This is a task-based fMRI study of deductive and inductive reasoning in healthy adults, using group-level random-effects whole-brain SPM analyses and reporting BOLD results; thus it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, and I8. However, the provided full text does not report stereotactic coordinates (Talairach or MNI) for the task-related activations—coordinate tables or explicit coordinate values are not present in the supplied content. Inclusion criterion I7 requires stereotactic coordinate results, so I7 is not satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met based on the provided content. Therefore the study must be excluded because it fails to meet I7 (reporting of standardized coordinates). The full text appears to contain core sections (introduction, methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete is set to false.

Full-text fMRI study of Theory of Mind (self-perspective inhibition and belief reasoning), not a problem-solving task as defined by the review. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level fMRI analyses in healthy adults), I7 (results reported in standard stereotactic space, MNI), I8 (BOLD fMRI analyses), I9 (voxelwise results presented). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (task does not meet the review's definition of problem solving; it examines perspective-taking/ToM and inhibition rather than goal-directed problem-solving requiring evaluation, planning/sequencing, and execution to reach a novel solution). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore excluded for not addressing the review objective (I5).

The study meets all inclusion criteria for the review. The task includes an executive manipulation (create a new probe by advancing two alphabetical letters and deciding match) that constitutes a rule-based operation to reach a goal and thus fits the review's definition of problem solving (I5). It is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants with group-level random-effects analyses (I6). Stereotactic coordinates are reported (MNI and converted to Talairach) (I7). The study reports BOLD fMRI results (I8). Results are reported in the main text with coordinates and figures/tables, satisfying acceptable reporting standards (I9). The provided full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false). No exclusion criteria apply (e.g., not ROI-only, not between-group-only, not non-empirical).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of a problem-solving task (computational estimation/strategy selection) in healthy adult participants. It meets I5: participants had a defined goal (provide the better estimate), selected and executed strategies (evaluating problem features, planning and executing rounding procedures). It meets I6: group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses are reported. It meets I8: BOLD fMRI data were acquired and analyzed. It meets I7/I9: analyses were performed in MNI space and the manuscript references stereotactic coordinates (MNI template usage and ROI coordinates are reported; whole-brain results are indicated in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not a between-group-only comparison, not non-empirical). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; figures/tables referenced but their absence here does not render the full text incomplete. Therefore include.

This study does not investigate a problem-solving task as defined by the review (it uses a time-estimation/performance-monitoring task rather than goal-directed problem solving/planning/sequencing of operations) and therefore fails inclusion I5. Although it reports task-based fMRI BOLD results (I8 met), the imaging results are reported primarily as ROI analyses and the whole-brain analyses reported in the paper did not yield significant task effects or provide stereotactic coordinates for healthy-group task activations. Thus the study effectively reports only ROI results and does not provide healthy-group whole-brain task effects, violating exclusion criteria E3 and E5. Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (problem-solving task), I6 (whole-brain analysis with group-level healthy adult task effects), I7 (stereotactic coordinates reported for task-related increases), and I9 (voxelwise results/coordinates for healthy task effects not provided). The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Given these issues the study is excluded from the meta-analysis.

This task is a semantic event sequencing task requiring planning and sequencing of actions to reach a goal (meets I5). The study used task-based fMRI with BOLD signal analyses (meets I8). Whole-brain, group-level within-group analyses were performed and reported for the healthy Control group, corrected across the whole brain (meets I6). Results are reported in standardized stereotactic space (MNI) with coordinates for activations and contrasts (meets I7). Coordinate reporting in tables/figures is acceptable (meets I9). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete for screening. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, includes healthy-group task effects, is empirical).

The study is a task-based BOLD fMRI investigation in healthy adults (n=19) that experimentally manipulates a reasoning task requiring rule deduction, sequencing, and planning—meeting the review’s problem-solving definition. The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM2) with normalization to MNI space and corrected thresholding, and describes stereotactic coordinates and p-values for contrasts (R>Rc, M>Mc, R>M, M>R). It also includes an anatomically defined ROI analysis but does not rely exclusively on ROI results. Thus it satisfies I5 (problem-solving task), I6 (whole-brain group analysis in healthy adults), I7 (stereotactic coordinates in MNI space), I8 (BOLD fMRI), and I9 (voxelwise results available).
