The study is a task-based fMRI investigation in healthy adults and reports whole-brain analyses with stereotactic coordinates and BOLD results (meets I6, I7, I8, I9). However, the experimental paradigm is a spatial navigation/concurrent spatial discrimination learning task assessing memory strategies (hippocampal vs caudate-based navigation), not a problem-solving task as defined by the review (i.e., tasks requiring critical thinking/planning/sequencing operations across semantic, algebraic, logical, mechanical frameworks). Therefore inclusion criterion I5 (task is a problem-solving task) is not met. Full text appears complete and no exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered.

The study is a whole-brain task-based BOLD fMRI investigation in healthy adults and reports stereotactic coordinates (I6, I7, I8, I9 met). However, the task is a perceptual evidence-integration / belief-revision rating task (rating morphed animal images and updating beliefs) rather than a goal-directed problem-solving task as defined in I5 (no explicit goal requiring planning/sequencing operations to reach a solution within a formal rule framework). Therefore it does not meet I5 and must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that included a healthy adult group performing arithmetic problem-solving tasks (exact and approximate calculation). The tasks meet the review’s problem-solving definition (goal-directed calculation using rule-based operations). Whole-brain, group-level analyses are reported for adults (adult vs. symbol-matching contrasts and adult–child contrasts). Results are reported with Talairach stereotactic coordinates and standard voxelwise thresholds. The imaging modality is BOLD fMRI. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not limited to patient groups or non-empirical). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided and appears complete.

This fMRI study examines autobiographical remembering and autobiographical reasoning (self-reflection, meaning-making) rather than a goal-directed problem-solving task as defined by the review (I5 not met). It does, however, meet I6 (whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses in healthy adults), I7 (reports MNI coordinates), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), and I9 (coordinate results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria are triggered (E3–E6 not met). Therefore the study is excluded because it does not investigate problem-solving processes (I5 not satisfied).

This is a task-based BOLD fMRI study in healthy adults that includes the Wisconsin Card Sorting Test (WCST), a rule-based, goal-directed task requiring subjects to infer and shift sorting rules (evaluating the problem, planning/sequencing actions, and executing rule-conforming operations), which fits the review's problem-solving task definition (I5). The paper reports whole-brain group-level analyses (normalized, smoothed maps, group linear model) and identifies task-related activations with stereotactic coordinates in Talairach space (tables/figures), satisfying I6 and I7. BOLD fMRI analyses are performed and reported, meeting I8, and voxelwise/coordinate results are provided in tables/figures, meeting I9. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (core content present). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Although the sample is small (n=11) and some ROI-based tests are used, whole-brain voxelwise maps and group effects are reported, so the study meets the inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

The study is a methods paper using task-based fMRI in healthy adults (pain and visual-scene tasks) and reports group-level whole-brain BOLD analyses (I6, I8) with results/supplementary materials indicated (I9). However, it does not investigate problem-solving as defined by the review (I5): the experimental tasks involve nociceptive stimulus discrimination and familiar vs. novel scene recognition, which do not meet the review's problem-solving definition (goal-directed planning, sequencing, or rule-based solution processes). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Therefore the study does not satisfy all required inclusion criteria (specifically missing I5) and must be excluded.

Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level fMRI in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic Talairach coordinates), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), I9 (voxelwise results reported/available). This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of insight/problem solving using Chinese logogriphs: participants had a goal (find the correct character) and engaged in problem-solving processes (representational change, decomposition of characters), satisfying I5. It used whole-brain, group-level random-effects analysis on healthy adult participants (n=16), satisfying I6. The study reports BOLD fMRI contrast analyses (Aha vs No-aha), satisfying I8. Although coordinate tables/figures are not reproduced in the provided text, the manuscript explicitly states activations and notes results are summarized in tables/figures, so stereotactic coordinate reporting is indicated (I7) and acceptable per I9. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not non-empirical, includes healthy-group task effects, not limited to group comparisons by disease/age/gender). This is an empirical PET study measuring regional cerebral blood flow during mental calculation (computation vs retrieval) in a calculating prodigy and matched healthy control adults. The task is a problem-solving task involving goal-directed computation and algorithmic operations (I5). Whole-brain analyses were performed using SPM99 with group-level effects in healthy adult controls (I6). The paper reports stereotactic results (see Table 2 and text referencing ACV stereotactic frame; standard SPM output) consistent with Talairach/MNI coordinates (I7). It reports rCBF PET analysis (I8) and provides voxelwise results in tables/figures (I9). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion and References, so fulltext_incomplete=false. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is a task-based fMRI study of mental calculation (arithmetic) in healthy adults, which meets the review’s problem-solving definition (goal-directed operations using rule-based procedures to arrive at correct solutions). The study uses whole-brain EPI coverage and reports group-level random-effects analyses (one-sample t-tests). It reports BOLD fMRI results and provides stereotactic coordinates (MNI transformed to Talairach) for task-related activations. Voxelwise whole-brain contrasts and conjunction analyses are described and thresholded, and coordinate results are available. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not a between-group-only contrast, not non-empirical). Full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This fMRI study is a whole-brain, task-based investigation in healthy adults and reports BOLD results in MNI space; however the behavioral paradigm is rapid perceptual decision-making (Go/No-Go ‘baseball’ trajectory matching) rather than a problem-solving task as defined in I5 (i.e., it does not require extended goal-directed problem solving, planning/sequencing of actions to derive a previously unknown solution within semantic/algebraic/logical/mechanical frameworks). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based PET study using the Tower of Toronto (isomorphic to Tower of Hanoi), a classic problem-solving/planning task (goal-directed, requires planning/sequencing and rule-based operations). It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses in healthy adult participants (n=12), using SPM99 with MNI stereotactic coordinates presented in tables/figures, and PET rCBF (H2O15) measures. Voxelwise task-related increases (cognitive/associative/autonomous vs. reference) are reported. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria I5–I9 and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study of deductive (syllogistic) reasoning in 14 healthy adult subjects. The task meets the review’s problem-solving definition (goal-directed logical evaluation and rule-based operations). The study reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses using SPM, provides stereotactic coordinates referenced to a standardized template, and reports BOLD-related results. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based BOLD fMRI study in healthy adults using a two-digit arithmetic choice task that fits the review’s problem-solving definition (goal-directed arithmetic operations requiring evaluation/comparison and rule-based execution). This PET study examines healthy adults performing the PASAT, which requires rule-based arithmetic (adding two most recent digits) and thus involves problem-solving operations (goal-directed computation, working memory, rule-based execution). No exclusion criteria are met.

This study does not meet the review's definition of a problem-solving task (I5). The experimental tasks are perceptual/dual-task attention and response-selection (color and letter discrimination; dual-task/multitasking training) rather than tasks requiring goal-directed problem solving, planning/sequencing of actions to derive novel solutions, or application of semantic/algebraic/logical rule-based problem solving. It does, however, meet other inclusion criteria: whole-brain group-level fMRI analysis in healthy adults (I6), stereotactic coordinates in MNI space reported (I7), BOLD fMRI analysis (I8), and voxelwise results are reported in text/tables/figures (I9). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore exclude because I5 is not satisfied.

Full text appears incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). While the study is a task-based fMRI investigation of arithmetic computation and clearly reports BOLD fMRI results (satisfying I5 and I8), the available content does not allow verification of other required inclusion criteria: I6 (confirmation of a whole-brain, group-level analysis in healthy adults) and I7 (reporting of stereotactic coordinates in Talairach or MNI space). I9 (where voxelwise results are reported) also cannot be confirmed from the abstract alone. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are apparent from the abstract. Because all inclusion criteria must be verified and the full text is incomplete, I must exclude the study pending full-text review.

(a) Exclusion criteria met: E3 — the study reports primarily VOI/ROI-based analyses (manually delineated VOIs, percent spatial extent within VOIs) and did not provide voxelwise, stereotactic coordinate results. (b) Inclusion criteria met: I5 — task-based fMRI of a problem-solving/planning task (Tower of London); I8 — BOLD fMRI analyses reported. (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I6 — no clear whole‑brain, voxelwise group-level stereotactic analysis in healthy adults (analyses were VOI-based and individualized rather than normalized group SPM in standard space); I7 — no task-related stereotactic coordinates reported in Talairach/MNI space; I9 — no indication that voxelwise coordinate tables/figures are available. Therefore the paper does not meet the requirement for whole-brain, stereotactic voxelwise results in healthy adult group-level analyses, so it must be excluded.

This is an fMRI study of creative literary writing, not a problem-solving task as defined by the review. Although it includes healthy adult participants and reports whole-brain BOLD group-level analyses with stereotactic (MNI) coordinates, the task is creative text continuation judged qualitatively rather than a goal-oriented, rule- or solution-focused problem-solving paradigm (no requirement to identify/plan/execute operations to reach a correct or specified solution). Therefore inclusion criterion I5 (problem-solving task) is not met. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level effects in healthy adults), I7 (reports coordinates in MNI space), I8 (reports BOLD analysis), I9 (voxelwise results reported). Exclusion criteria met: none. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Full text is complete. This is an event-related fMRI study in healthy adults (n=7) using the Wisconsin Card Sorting Test (WCST). It meets I5 (WCST requires identifying/using rules, set-shifting, and trial-and-error problem solving), I7 (reports Talairach coordinates), I8 (BOLD/fMRI analyses reported), and I9 (voxelwise results available in figures/tables). However, the imaging coverage was limited to four contiguous slices (z = 12–36 mm at y = 0 mm) rather than whole-brain coverage; therefore the study does not satisfy I6 (at least one whole-brain group-level analysis). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Because ALL inclusion criteria must be met and I6 is not met, the study is excluded.

This study is excluded. Exclusion IDs met: E3 (reports only ROI results) — the analyses reported are ROI-based β-values and ROI correlation tests rather than a whole-brain, voxelwise group analysis; E5 (doesn't include any healthy-group task effect) — participants are individuals with Williams syndrome with no healthy adult task-based group-level results presented. Inclusion IDs met: I8 (reports a BOLD analysis) — the study uses task-based fMRI and BOLD contrast measures. Inclusion IDs not met: I5 (not a problem-solving task) — tasks are passive auditory/visual/emotion/music stimuli, not goal-directed problem solving; I6 (no whole-brain analysis with group-level effects in healthy adults) — no whole-brain group-level results in healthy adults are reported; I7 (no stereotactic coordinate results for task-related increases in healthy adults) — the paper reports ROI beta-values and ROI definitions in Talairach space but does not present whole-brain coordinate results for healthy adult task effects. Full text appears complete.

Full text appears incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). The abstract describes an event-related fMRI study of syllogistic (logical) reasoning in healthy adults, so it meets I5 (task-based logical problem-solving) and I8 (fMRI/BOLD). However the provided content does not allow verification of whole-brain, group-level analyses and stereotactic coordinate reporting (I6 and I7) or whether voxelwise results are available in tables/figures (I9). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are clearly met. Because I6, I7, and I9 cannot be confirmed from the incomplete full text, the study cannot be confidently included.

This paper reports task-based fMRI BOLD experiments in healthy adults involving mental manipulation (melody reversal and transposition) and group-level whole-brain contrasts, so it meets I5 (task qualifies as problem-solving-like transformation), I6 (group whole-brain analyses), and I8 (BOLD analyses). However, the provided full text does not report stereotactic coordinates (Talairach/MNI) nor tables/figures with voxelwise coordinates in the excerpt supplied, so I7 is not satisfied and I9 cannot be confirmed. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Because ALL inclusion criteria must be met and I7 (and I9) are not met in the provided document, the study is excluded.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants performing difficult math/problem-solving tasks (arithmetic and modular problems), which meet the review's operational definition of problem solving. The study reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses (second-level mean t images) of BOLD data, with stereotactic results presented (tables/figures) in standardized space. Voxelwise results and ROI follow-ups are both reported. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I9 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation of a verbal 2-Back working memory task with breath-hold calibration. It includes whole-brain group analyses, reports stereotactic (MNI) coordinates, and BOLD analyses, and the full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. However, the 2-Back is a working memory/executive function task and does not meet the review's definition of a problem-solving task (goal-directed planning/sequencing or executing operations to arrive at a correct previously unknown solution across semantic, algebraic, logical, mechanical frameworks). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 and must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met.

This is a task-based fMRI study of healthy adult participants (n=22) that investigates relational reasoning (second-order relational integration) using semantic and visuospatial problem-like tasks with correct/incorrect responses. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level GLM analyses and β-series functional connectivity, provides voxelwise stereotactic coordinates in MNI space (tables/figures), and BOLD fMRI results. All required inclusion criteria are met (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only reporting, no patient-group-only contrasts, and it is an empirical study). The provided full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants using a conditional/ deductive reasoning (belief-bias) task that requires applying logical rules to reach conclusions — a problem-solving paradigm per the review definition. The study reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses (SPM8) with voxelwise thresholds and clusters significant at FWE-corrected levels, uses BOLD fMRI, normalizes data to MNI space and reports activation peak coordinates (tables/figures referenced). Voxelwise results are reported and accessible. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not a patient/group-comparison-only study, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria I5–I9 and violates none.

This is a PET whole-brain group study in healthy adults reporting rCBF coordinates (Talairach) for task contrasts, but the tasks are perceptual discrimination/mental rotation of tactile stimuli rather than goal-directed problem-solving as defined by the review (planning/sequencing operations to reach a novel solution). Thus inclusion criterion I5 (problem-solving task) is not met. The study does satisfy I6 (whole-brain group-level PET analysis in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates in Talairach space), I8 (reports rCBF/PET results), and I9 (voxelwise results are reported). No exclusion criteria are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This fMRI study used a rule-based category-learning/matching task (determining whether two exemplars belong to the same category) that requires applying learned classification rules to reach a goal, fitting the review’s problem-solving definition (goal-directed rule-based operations). It reports whole-brain, group-level analyses in Talairach space (data transformed to Talairach; centers/coordinates reported), uses BOLD fMRI, and provides voxelwise/group activation maps. Participants were healthy adults. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the article appears complete. Therefore inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 are met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered.

This is a task-based whole-brain BOLD fMRI study in adults that reports within-group and between-group activation and discusses voxelwise results (meets I6, I8, and I9). However, the experimental task is a visuospatial block design/missing-block identification task aimed at perceptual/visuospatial processing rather than a problem-solving task as defined by the review (i.e., requiring goal-directed evaluation, planning/sequencing, and execution to arrive at a previously unknown solution). The authors characterize the task as testing visualization and breaking down a gestalt, but the paradigm is essentially perceptual matching/identification rather than multi-step problem solving under the review’s I5 definition. Therefore I5 is not met and the study must be excluded.

The study uses an implicit sequence learning (Serial Reaction Time) task probing procedural/implicit learning rather than a problem-solving paradigm as defined in inclusion criterion I5 (no goal-directed evaluation/planning to derive a novel solution within a semantic/algebraic/logical/mechanical rule set). It does, however, meet other inclusion criteria: whole-brain, group-level fMRI analyses including healthy adult participants (I6); stereotactic coordinate reporting in MNI/Talairach space (I7); and BOLD analyses (I8). Task-related activation results are reported in the main text (I9). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore the study is excluded for failing to meet I5 (problem-solving task).

This is an empirical task-based BOLD fMRI study in healthy adults (n=17) using the People Pieces Analogy (PPA) problem-solving task (A:B::C:D). The task meets the review's problem-solving definition: subjects have a goal (verify analogy validity) and must perform rule-based relational integration, interference resolution, and sequential operations to arrive at a correct response. The paper reports whole-brain group-level mixed-effects analyses, provides stereotactic (MNI) coordinates in tables and figures, and reports BOLD results. Voxelwise results and ROI analyses are presented; whole-brain results are central (not ROI-only). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables, references) is present in the provided content.

This is a task-based whole-brain BOLD fMRI study in adults that includes healthy controls and reports group-level stereotactic results (Talairach) and BOLD analyses; however, the task (Embedded Figures Test) probes perceptual/visuospatial detail-focused processing and visual search rather than problem-solving as defined by the review (goal-directed evaluation, planning/sequencing operations, or rule-based solution generation). Therefore it does not meet inclusion criterion I5. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level analyses in healthy adults), I7 (stereotactic coordinates/normalization to Talairach), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), and I9 (qualifying voxelwise results available). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (task is not a problem-solving paradigm per the meta-analysis definition). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study of mental arithmetic (multiplication verification), which meets the review definition of problem solving (goal-directed, rule-based operations to arrive at correct solutions). The study reports whole-brain, random-effects group analyses in healthy adult participants, voxelwise results with stereotactic MNI coordinates (e.g., x = -50, y = -64, z = 28), and BOLD fMRI contrasts. Results are reported voxelwise in the main text and ROI analyses are supplementary; no exclusion criteria apply. Full article text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adult college students solving algebra problems (word/story vs equation formats). It reports whole-brain voxelwise group analyses (voxelwise ANOVAs), stereotactic coordinates referenced to an MNI template, and BOLD fMRI acquisition and results. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion, and none of the exclusion criteria apply. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met.

Although this is a task-based whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adults reporting BOLD results with stereotactic coordinates, the experimental task (pairwise number/date/event comparisons selecting the larger or later item) does not meet the review’s definition of a problem-solving task. The task involves perceptual/semantic comparison and ordering rather than goal-directed problem solving that requires planning, sequencing of actions, or executing operations to arrive at a novel solution. Therefore inclusion criterion I5 is not satisfied, while I6, I7, I8, and I9 are satisfied. The full text appears complete.

This study used a Judgment of Line Orientation (JLO) visuospatial discrimination task, which is a perceptual/angle-judgment task rather than a problem-solving task as defined in I5 (goal-directed evaluation/planning/sequencing/executing rule-based operations to arrive at a novel solution). The study does include whole-brain, group-level fMRI in healthy adults and reports BOLD analyses, but the provided full text does not present stereotactic coordinates in Talairach/MNI space (I7 not met). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Therefore excluded for failure to meet I5 (and I7 not clearly met from provided content).

This is a task-based BOLD fMRI study in healthy adults using a problem-solving task (Hit-N sequential game requiring planning, sequencing, and rule-based actions to reach a goal). The paper reports group-level whole-brain random-effects GLM analyses on 12 healthy subjects, provides stereotactic Talairach coordinates (e.g., (41,19,3); (47,40,3)), and presents BOLD activation results (figures/contrasts and statistical thresholds). All inclusion criteria I5–I9 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, and MRI acquisition/GLM details).

This study is excluded because it does not meet the review's definition of a problem-solving task (I5). The task is a visuo‑spatial relative distance judgment (perceptual comparison) rather than a problem-solving paradigm requiring goal-directed planning, sequencing, or application of rule-based operations to discover a novel solution. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level fMRI analysis in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI space), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), I9 (voxelwise results reported in tables/figures). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task is not a problem‑solving task as defined). Exclusion criteria met: none (no E3–E6 violations). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical PET study in healthy adults (n=19) using task-based imaging of semantic decision-making vs a syllable decision baseline. The semantic decision task involves evaluating relations among items and selecting the appropriate response, which fits the review’s acceptable problem-solving domain (semantic tasks are explicitly included). The study reports whole-brain, group-level rCBF analyses using SPM99 with corrections, provides peak stereotactic coordinates in MNI space, and presents voxelwise task-related activations and contrasts (figures and peak coordinate tables). Therefore it meets I5 (task-based problem-solving/semantic decision), I6 (whole-brain group analyses in healthy adults), I7 (MNI coordinates), I8 (rCBF PET analysis), and I9 (voxelwise results reported). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study of deductive (logical) reasoning in healthy adults, which fits the review’s definition of problem solving (evaluation of premises and application of logical rules to derive conclusions). The experiment used whole-brain BOLD fMRI with group-level analyses in 12 healthy participants (I6), reports stereotactic Talairach coordinates for activated ROIs (I7), and presents voxelwise BOLD results (I8). The task qualifies as problem solving under the meta-analysis definition (logical/semantic rule-based operations; I5). Voxelwise/task-related results are described and localized (satisfying I9). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not a between-group-only comparison, empirical healthy adult data). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete.

This is a methods paper introducing GLMdenoise and a benchmark; the experiments consist of visual, event-related fMRI datasets used to evaluate denoising performance, not problem-solving tasks. Thus it does not meet the core content requirement for the review (I5: problem-solving task). Additionally, the paper does not present whole-brain, group-level task effects across healthy adult participants in stereotactic coordinates as required (I6 and I7). It does report BOLD analyses (I8). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered by this manuscript.

The study is a task-based fMRI experiment in healthy adult participants that includes a clearly defined rule-finding task requiring goal-directed problem solving (formulating hypotheses about an unknown operator, testing, and updating strategies), satisfying the review’s definition of problem solving. Whole-brain group-level analyses were conducted (data normalized to MNI, reported cluster-corrected results), with stereotactic coordinates reported (MNI/Talairach conversions given). The study reports BOLD fMRI results and task-related increases in activation (ventral striatum, frontopolar cortex, DLPFC) and provides psychophysiological interaction analyses. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 are met; no exclusion criteria apply.

This PET study uses task-based, whole-brain SPM analyses of rCBF during go game problem-solving (territorial planning and life-or-death checkmate judgment) in healthy adult participants (professionals and amateurs). Tasks involve goal-directed planning and selecting a correct solution (Task 2), meeting the operational definition of problem solving. Group-level whole-brain analyses were performed and reported using SPM99 (rCBF results), and the manuscript refers to Z-maps and image-based results (typical stereotactic reporting in SPM studies), indicating availability of coordinate-based task-related increases. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. Therefore inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8 and I9 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the review objective. The task is an arithmetic judgment (complex vs. simple equations) that requires rule-based operations and evaluation (qualifies as problem-solving per I5). It is a task-based fMRI study reporting BOLD effects (I8). The authors performed whole-brain, random-effects group analyses in healthy adult participants (I6) and report stereotactic results in Talairach space (I7); voxelwise/ROI derivations are described and coordinates are indicated (I9). No exclusion criteria are triggered (not ROI-only, not between-group only, empirical healthy adult data). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study investigates theory-of-mind/mentalizing using sentence reading about mental states and person/object spatial relations, not a goal-directed problem-solving task as defined in I5 (no evidence of tasks requiring planning/sequencing or executing rule-based operations to reach a solution). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain fMRI analyses in healthy adults) and I8 (BOLD fMRI reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (does not study a problem-solving task per review definition) and I7 (the provided full text describes normalization to Talairach space but does not present explicit stereotactic coordinate results in the supplied content; thus I7 cannot be confirmed). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply based on the provided full text. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based, whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adult participants that examined a task requiring participants to reorder letters into alphabetical order (manipulation), which involves goal-directed planning, sequencing operations according to an explicit rule (alphabetical order) and execution — meeting the review's definition of problem solving. The study reports group-level, whole-brain SPM analyses (random-effects), BOLD-based fMRI results, and stereotactic coordinates in standard MNI space (tables and figures). Voxelwise results are presented in tables and figures. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 and violates no exclusion criteria.

The PASAT requires participants to follow an algebraic/arithmetic rule (add the last two digits) and execute operations to arrive at correct sums, fitting the review’s problem-solving definition (I5). The study is a task-based fMRI (BOLD) experiment (I8), performs whole-brain group-level analyses including healthy adult controls (one-sample RFX for controls) (I6), and reports stereotactic coordinates in Talairach space (I7). Coordinate reporting is available in the main text/tables (I9). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext is complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not solely between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical). Therefore the study meets all listed inclusion criteria and is suitable for the review.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants that examines manipulation of verbal material (counting two letters forward) which requires applying a rule, sequencing/planning, and executing operations to arrive at correct responses — meeting the review’s definition of problem-solving processes. The study reports group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses, provides stereotactic coordinates in MNI space, and uses BOLD fMRI measures. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, allowing verification of analyses and coordinates. Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9). No exclusion criteria apply.

While this is a task-based whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adults reporting BOLD coordinate results, the task is a simple number estimation with manipulation of reward distribution and social comparison; it does not meet the review's definition of a problem-solving task (no goal-directed multi-step problem solving, planning/sequencing, or critical-thinking operations to arrive at a novel solution). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group fMRI in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI), I8 (reports BOLD analysis), I9 (voxelwise results reported/available). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (task is not a problem-solving task per review definition). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Therefore excluded for failure to meet I5.

The study uses a task requiring re-sequencing of verbal items (reverse recitation of months) which constitutes a goal-directed task involving rule-based manipulation/sequencing (meeting the review's problem-solving definition). It reports whole-brain, group-level SPM analyses in healthy adults (n=18), uses task-based BOLD fMRI, and provides stereotactic coordinates in Talairach space. Coordinate results are presented as SPM maps and statistical tables. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so is complete for screening purposes. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that reports whole-brain, group-level BOLD results (mixed-effects whole-brain analyses) and provides stereotactic (MNI) local maxima in tables/figures. The experimental task required participants to predict which box a contestant would open based on presented belief and inferred desire states — a goal-directed judgment that required deductive and abductive reasoning (i.e., evaluating the problem, applying rules about belief/desire, and selecting the correct response), which fits the review's problem-solving definition. All inclusion criteria are therefore met (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only reporting, no patient/group-only contrasts, and this is empirical data). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

While this is an empirical, whole-brain task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that reports group-level BOLD effects and stereotactic coordinates, it does not meet the review's definition of a problem-solving task (I5). The mental rotation task here requires perceptual/spatial transformation and same-vs-mirror judgements rather than goal-directed problem solving involving evaluation, planning/sequencing of actions, or executing operations within a rule-based framework to arrive at a previously unknown solution. Therefore I5 is not satisfied. All other inclusion criteria (I6, I7, I8, I9) are met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based BOLD fMRI study of problem-solving (Tower of London) in healthy adults with group-level random-effects analyses and ROI follow-ups. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based problem-solving fMRI), I6 (group whole-brain analyses indicated), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), I9 (voxelwise results acceptable). However, the provided full text lacks any explicit stereotactic coordinate tables or coordinate listings in Talairach/MNI space—the manuscript text contains placeholders for figures/tables (e.g., “see”, missing tables) which prevents confirmation of criterion I7 (reporting task-related increases as stereotactic coordinates). Because ALL inclusion criteria must be verifiable and I7 is not demonstrated in the supplied content, I exclude this record. The supplied full text appears incomplete (missing figures/tables/coordinate listings), so fulltext_incomplete=true.

Excluded because the study does not meet the review’s inclusion criteria for problem-solving fMRI/PET whole-brain analyses. (a) Exclusion IDs met: none. (b) Inclusion IDs met: none. (c) Inclusion IDs NOT met: I5 (task is a task-switching spatial judgment paradigm, not a problem-solving task as defined), I6 (no whole-brain group-level neuroimaging analysis reported; authors state they do not report imaging data), I7 (no stereotactic coordinate results reported), I8 (no reported BOLD or rCBF analyses/results in the paper), I9 (no voxelwise coordinate tables/figures of neuroimaging results). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion), but because no task-based whole-brain neuroimaging results on problem-solving are reported, the paper cannot be included in the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based BOLD fMRI study of mental arithmetic problem solving in healthy adult participants (n=26). The task is goal-directed and involves planning/sequencing and rule-based operations (procedural strategies vs. fact retrieval), meeting the review's problem-solving definition. The paper reports whole-brain group-level random-effects analyses (ANOVAs), provides stereotactic coordinates (MNI) for activations and ROI peaks, and presents voxelwise results and contrasts, satisfying requirements for reporting BOLD analyses and coordinate data. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only; includes healthy-group task effects).

Although this is a whole-brain, task-based fMRI study in adults that reports stereotactic (Talairach) results and BOLD analyses, the experimental paradigm is a mental-rotation/visuospatial discrimination task rather than a problem-solving task as defined by the review (goal-directed problem solving requiring planning/sequencing or executing rule-based operations to arrive at a previously unknown solution). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level analyses including a healthy control group), I7 (reports coordinates in standard space), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), and I9 (voxelwise results reported/tables). Inclusion criterion not met: I5. No exclusion criteria from E3–E6 apply.

Excluded because the experimental task is a working memory (externally ordered memory) task, not a problem-solving task as defined by inclusion criterion I5. The study does meet I6 (includes whole-brain, group-level fMRI effects in healthy adult participants) and I8 (reports BOLD fMRI analyses). However it does not satisfy I5 (task is not problem-solving), does not clearly report stereotactic coordinates in the text/tables (I7 not met), and no explicit coordinate tables or numeric peak coordinates are provided in the supplied full text (I9 not met). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered by the content. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical, task-based neuroimaging study using both fMRI and PET with the Tower of London (TOL) problem-solving task (goal-directed planning/sequencing). It tested healthy adult participants (two groups of six right-handed adults) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM99) for both BOLD and rCBF measures. Results are presented in stereotactic space (Talairach/MNI translations) with voxel/cluster thresholds and coordinates. Thus it satisfies all inclusion criteria (I5–I9) and does not meet any exclusion criteria (E3–E6). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

Excluded (E3): The study performs multivariate ROI-based analyses (DLPFC, ACC, OFC, hippocampus, temporal ROIs) rather than reporting whole-brain, voxelwise group-level stereotactic coordinates. It uses BOLD fMRI (I8 satisfied) in healthy adult participants, but does not provide whole-brain coordinate results in Talairach/MNI space or voxelwise whole-brain group contrasts (I6 and I7 not met). Additionally, the task is a probabilistic inference/decision-making (beads/Jumping-to-Conclusions) paradigm that primarily assesses evidence accumulation and decision evaluation; it does not clearly meet the meta-analysis definition of a problem-solving task involving planning/sequencing operations to reach a novel solution (I5 not met). No qualifying voxelwise coordinate tables/figures are provided in the full text (I9 not met). Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). Inclusion criteria met: I8. Inclusion criteria not met: I5, I6, I7, I9. Exclusion criteria applied: E3.

This study does not meet the core inclusion criterion I5: the experimental task is a perceptual numerosity comparison (deciding whether dot counts are greater/less) embedded in a monetary inequity context, not a problem-solving task as defined (planning, sequencing, or executing operations to reach a goal/novel solution). It does meet other inclusion criteria: I6 (group-level whole-brain analyses in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic MNI coordinates), I8 (BOLD fMRI analyses), and I9 (voxelwise results presented). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore EXCLUDED because I5 is not satisfied.

Full text is complete. Excluded because the sample comprises adolescents (mean ages ~16.8–16.9), not healthy adults, so inclusion criterion I6 (healthy adult group-level effects) is not met. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of a problem-solving/mental-rotation task), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI space), I8 (reports BOLD analyses), I9 (voxelwise results/coordinates available). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (healthy adult participants). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

The study is a task-based fMRI experiment in healthy adults that examines goal-directed problem solving (visual creativity task requiring participants to assemble shapes into a recognizable object — involves planning, sequencing mental operations, and execution), satisfying I5. It reports whole-brain group-level analyses (FLAME mixed-effects), satisfying I6. Activation peaks are reported in stereotactic space (MNI) in tables/figures, satisfying I7 and I9. The study uses BOLD fMRI, satisfying I8. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not clinical group comparisons only, includes healthy-group task effects, and is empirical). The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so it appears complete.

This is a task-based BOLD fMRI study in healthy adult participants using a rule-based number-updating task that requires evaluation, planning/decision (compare presented number to current memory set), and execution of rule-conforming responses (substitute vs no-substitute). The study reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses and describes stereotactic normalization to MNI space and cluster results (with clusters, anatomical correlates and Brodmann areas shown in a table), meeting the requirement that voxelwise results are available in tables/figures. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I5 (problem-solving-like, rule-based updating), I6 (whole-brain group analyses in healthy adults), I7 (results reported in standardized stereotactic space / MNI normalization and indicated table of cluster results), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), and I9 (voxelwise results available in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply.

Exclusion (E5): The study does not provide a whole-brain, group-level task activation map for healthy adults alone. While it reports whole-brain fMRI results (BOLD) with stereotactic coordinates and combined main effects across patients and controls and between-group contrasts (insomnia vs controls), it does not present a healthy-only group-level task effect required by inclusion criterion I6. Inclusion criteria met: I7 (reports task-related increases in MNI coordinates), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis reported), I9 (voxelwise results reported in tables/figures). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no whole-brain group-level task analysis in healthy adults alone), I5 (task classified as problem-solving is ambiguous — verbal fluency is primarily lexical retrieval/executive search and may not meet the meta-analysis definition of problem solving). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore excluded because E5 is met and critical inclusion criteria I6 (and likely I5) are not satisfied.

The study includes a task (Shepard–Metzler mental rotation) that fits the review's problem‑solving definition: a goal-directed transformation operation requiring mental manipulation to reach a correct decision. It used task-based fMRI (BOLD) with group-level whole-brain SPM analyses in healthy adults (n=15), reported results in MNI space and tables/figures, and also provided ROI percent-signal analyses. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not clinical-group-only, not non-empirical). Therefore it satisfies I5, I6, I7, I8 and I9 and is eligible for inclusion.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that reports whole-brain group analyses (Talairach-space coordinates reported) and BOLD results. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level effects in healthy adults), I7 (stereotactic coordinates in Talairach space), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), I9 (voxelwise results reported in figures/tables). However, it does not meet I5: the Multi-Source Interference Task is a cognitive interference/response-selection paradigm (conflict/stroop-like task) rather than a problem-solving task as defined (goal-directed multi-step planning, sequencing, or critical thinking to arrive at a novel solution). Therefore it fails to satisfy all required inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of problem solving (anagram task) in healthy adult participants. It uses BOLD-weighted EPI, performs whole-brain group-level analyses (stimulus-locked contrasts such as Aha–Rest, Search–Rest, Aha–Search), registers data to MNI space, and reports activation peaks (Table I / text). The task meets the review definition of problem solving (goal-directed anagram solutions requiring cognitive operations), and voxelwise whole-brain results are presented. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, patient/group-comparison-only, non-empirical) are met. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so appears complete for screening.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adults using a number-series numerical-inductive reasoning task that meets the review's definition of problem solving (discovering rules, planning/sequencing to arrive at a correct solution). The study reports whole-brain, group-level analyses in MNI space using BOLD fMRI (task contrasts EASY/DIFFICULT vs CONTROL and IQ group comparisons), and indicates stereotactic results/cluster reporting. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study of algebraic problem solving in healthy adults (meets I5). It uses whole-brain coverage via 408 regions and reports group-level classification results (meets I6) and BOLD/fMRI analyses (meets I8). However, the paper does not report task-related activations as stereotactic coordinates in Talairach or MNI space (I7 not met). It also does not provide voxelwise stereotactic coordinate tables or standardized-space coordinate results in the main text, figures, or supplements (I9 not met). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Because not all required inclusion criteria are satisfied (specifically I7 and I9), the study must be excluded.

This is a task-based whole-brain fMRI study that includes healthy adult participants and reports stereotactic coordinates and BOLD results. However, the experimental paradigm is a working memory (Sternberg) manipulation task, not a problem-solving task as defined by the review (goal-directed problem solving involving evaluation, planning/sequencing actions, and executing rule-based operations to arrive at solutions). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5. No exclusion criteria are triggered: the study reports whole-brain voxelwise analyses (not ROI-only), contains healthy-group task effects (not only between-group contrasts), and is an empirical fMRI study. Full text appears complete.

While this is an empirical, task-based whole-brain fMRI study in adults reporting MNI coordinates and BOLD results (satisfying I6, I7, I8, I9), it does not investigate a task that meets the review's definition of 'problem solving' (I5). The experiments are rhyme-judgment (word reading) and mental rotation/same-different spatial visualization. The rhyme task is linguistic/phonological, not a problem-solving paradigm. The mental rotation task is a spatial visualization/perceptual discrimination task requiring mental transformation but lacks the planning/sequencing/executive problem-solving elements described in I5 (evaluating a problem, planning a sequence of operations to reach a previously unknown solution). Thus the study fails inclusion criterion I5. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met.

This is an fMRI study of the Iowa Gambling Task (IGT) in healthy adults that includes whole-brain group analyses and BOLD results, but it does not meet the review's definition of a problem-solving task. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain fMRI in healthy adults), I8 (reports BOLD fMRI analyses), and I9 (voxelwise/voxelwise-style results shown in figures and Talairach space). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 — the IGT is a decision-making/reward-learning task under ambiguity, not a rule-based/problem-solving task as defined (evaluating, planning/sequencing actions to reach a correct or previously unknown solution within a defined rule framework). I7 (explicit stereotactic coordinate tables for task-related increases) is not clearly reported in the text excerpt. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is an empiricial, task-based fMRI study of mental multidigit addition (exact and approximate) in healthy adult bilinguals. The addition tasks meet the review’s problem-solving definition (goal-directed verification of sums; planning/sequencing operations such as columnwise addition or rounding; rule-based execution). The study reports whole-brain, voxelwise random-effects group analyses, uses BOLD fMRI, and provides stereotactic results in MNI space (with supplementary coordinate tables). Participants are healthy adults. Therefore inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8 and I9 are met, and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study is an fMRI semantic association/lexical-semantic decision task, not a problem-solving task as defined by inclusion criterion I5 (no planning/sequencing or multi-step problem-solving or critical thinking to reach a novel solution). It does meet I6 (whole-brain, group-level analysis in healthy adults) and I8 (task-based BOLD fMRI). The provided text does not explicitly present stereotactic coordinates in Talairach/MNI space (the manuscript states "Clusters and peak voxels ... are listed" but coordinates are not included in the supplied content), so I7 cannot be confirmed from the provided full text. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study is excluded because it does not meet I5 (and I7 is unconfirmed).

This study does not meet the review’s definition of a problem-solving task (I5). The counting Stroop is a conflict/interference/inhibitory control task rather than a goal-directed problem-solving paradigm involving planning/sequencing to derive a previously unknown solution. The paper does include whole-brain, group-level fMRI analyses in healthy adults (I6) and uses task-related BOLD fMRI (I8). However, the full text as provided does not report stereotactic coordinates (Talairach/MNI) for task activations in the supplied content (I7 not met), nor are coordinate tables/voxelwise coordinate results present in the provided material (I9 not met). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Because ALL inclusion criteria must be satisfied and I5 and I7 (and I9 as presented) are not met, the study is excluded.

This is a methodological/review-style paper describing a single-scan dynamic molecular imaging technique and summarizing example applications (emotional processing, executive inhibition, ADHD). It does not present an empirical, whole-brain task-based fMRI or PET study of a problem-solving task in healthy adults, nor does it report stereotactic coordinates (Talairach/MNI) or group-level BOLD/rCBF results. Therefore it qualifies as a non-empirical paper without original human coordinate data (E6). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (does not study a defined problem-solving task), I6 (no whole-brain group-level effects in healthy adults reported), I7 (no stereotactic coordinates reported), I8 (does not report BOLD or rCBF analyses), I9 (no voxelwise coordinate tables/figures provided).

This fMRI study does not investigate problem solving as defined in the review (goal-directed planning/sequencing/evaluative operations to reach a solution). It examines maintenance and representation of abstract task rules and simple semantic/phonological judgments and self-selection of which rule to apply, not complex problem-solving across domains. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level analysis in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates), I8 (BOLD analysis reported), I9 (voxelwise results available). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (does not study a problem-solving task per review definition). No exclusion criteria from E3–E6 are triggered. Full text appears complete. Therefore excluded on the basis of I5 not being satisfied.

This study is excluded because it does not examine a problem-solving task as defined in I5. The paper analyzes Flanker (selective attention/response inhibition), False Belief (theory-of-mind), an attention/working-memory feature-identification task, and a monetary incentive delay task (reward/anticipation), none of which meet the meta-analysis definition of problem solving (goal-directed planning/sequencing to reach an unknown solution within a rule-based framework). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level analyses in healthy adults), I8 (BOLD fMRI analyses), and I9 (voxelwise results reported via figures/tables). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (task-based problem-solving). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This study should be excluded because it does not address problem-solving tasks as defined (it uses a motor sequencing task), and it reports primarily region-of-interest (ROI) analyses without whole-brain stereotactic coordinate results. (a) Exclusion IDs met: E3 (reports only ROI results). (b) Inclusion IDs met: I8 (task-based BOLD fMRI analysis was performed). (c) Inclusion IDs not met: I5 (task is motor sequencing, not a problem-solving task per the review definition), I6 (no whole-brain group-level analysis in healthy adults is reported; analyses are ROI-based), I7 (no stereotactic coordinates in Talairach/MNI space are reported), I9 (no voxelwise coordinate tables/figures/supplementary stereotactic results are provided). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the paper is not eligible for inclusion in this meta-analysis.

The study is a task-based fMRI paper using a complex working memory (working memory span) task (sentence monitoring and word recall/recognition), not a problem-solving paradigm as defined by the review (no evidence the task required goal-directed problem solving, planning/sequencing operations to reach novel solutions). It therefore fails inclusion criterion I5. It does meet several other inclusion criteria: whole-brain group-level effects in healthy adults (controls) (I6), reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI space (I7), reports BOLD fMRI analyses (I8), and provides voxelwise/figure results (I9). No exclusion criteria from the review (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, Conclusions).

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adult volunteers using the Tower of London, a canonical problem-solving/planning task (meets I5). The paper reports whole-brain group-level task effects across participants and within-group contrasts (meets I6). Results include stereotactic coordinates in MNI space in tables/figures (meets I7). The study reports BOLD fMRI analyses (meets I8). Voxelwise results are presented in tables/figures and the main text describes these effects (meets I9). The full text provided contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that includes whole-brain group analyses with stereotactic coordinates and BOLD results. However, the experimental paradigm investigates working memory encoding and chunking strategies for digit sequences (verbal WM and recoding to improve recall), not a problem-solving task as defined by the review (i.e., a goal-directed need to figure out a way to reach a goal via planning/sequencing operations to arrive at a novel or correct solution). Therefore inclusion criterion I5 is not met, though I6, I7, I8 and I9 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Excluded because the task (random number generation) does not meet the review's operational definition of a problem-solving task (I5: goal-directed problem solving involving evaluation, planning/sequencing actions to reach a correct or novel solution). The abstract and metadata indicate this is an empirical PET study reporting regional cerebral blood flow in healthy adult volunteers (meets I6 and I8). However, the provided full text is incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata present), so I cannot verify stereotactic coordinate reporting (I7) or whether voxelwise results are available in tables/figures/supplement (I9). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met based on available information. Therefore the study is excluded because I5 is not satisfied and I7/I9 cannot be confirmed from the incomplete full text.

This is a task-based, whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adults that reports stereotactic coordinates and BOLD results (meets I6, I7, I8, I9). However, the task is a spatial working memory task emphasizing encoding and chunking strategies, not a problem-solving task as defined (no explicit goal-driven need to discover or plan a novel solution, evaluate options, or execute operations to reach a previously unknown solution). Therefore I5 is not met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria are met.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that reports whole-brain (group-level) analyses, stereotactic coordinates (MNI/Talairach), and BOLD results. However, the experimental task is working memory training/maintenance and baseline tasks, not a problem-solving task as defined by the review (goal-oriented problem solving requiring planning/sequencing or executing operations within a rule-based framework). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 (task is not problem solving). No exclusion criteria are otherwise met. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study is an fMRI whole-brain group study in healthy adults reporting BOLD coordinates, but the experimental task is perceptual perspective-taking (right–left judgments about object position/motion) rather than a problem-solving task as defined by the review (no goal-directed problem solving, planning/sequencing to derive previously unknown solutions). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5. All other applicable inclusion criteria (I6, I7, I8, I9) are met; no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based BOLD fMRI study using the Tower of London planning task (a problem-solving paradigm) in healthy adults. It reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses, provides stereotactic coordinates (MNI/Talairach) for task-related activations, and presents BOLD activation results across task loads. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for task definition (I5), whole-brain group analysis in healthy adults (I6), stereotactic coordinate reporting (I7), BOLD analysis (I8), and acceptable reporting of voxelwise results (I9). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

The study does not meet the meta-analysis definition of a problem-solving task (I5). The tasks are match–mismatch and order-judgment paradigms relying on retrieval of familiar landmark or script sequences rather than goal-directed problem solving that requires devising a novel way to reach a goal or executing operations to discover a previously unknown solution. Although the paper uses whole-brain group-level fMRI (I6), reports BOLD analyses (I8), and presents voxelwise/statistical maps (I9), the provided full text does not include stereotactic coordinate tables/values in MNI or Talairach space (I7 not demonstrated in the supplied content). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered by the provided material. Therefore the study is excluded because I5 (problem-solving definition) is not met; additionally I7 (coordinates) is not clearly met in the supplied text.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that directly compares well-structured problem-solving tasks with ill-structured design tasks. The problem-solving condition is defined with explicit goals, legal moves, and unique solutions (meets the review's problem-solving definition). The study reports group-level whole-brain BOLD analyses (SPM5; FWE-corrected whole-brain thresholds), provides stereotactic coordinates in MNI space for task-related activations, and presents voxelwise results in the main text/tables. The sample comprises healthy adult participants. Full article includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text is complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I9 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study is excluded because it does not investigate a problem-solving task as defined in the review (I5 not met). The task is a number identification/priming task (press when target matches a predefined magnitude) and investigates semantic/notation effects and parietal adaptation, not goal-directed problem solving, planning, or sequencing to reach a novel solution. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level fMRI analysis in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI space), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), I9 (voxelwise results reported/available). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task is not a problem-solving task). Exclusion criteria met: none (no E3–E6 violations). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is a task-based BOLD fMRI study in healthy adult participants using the number bisection task, which requires applying rule-based operations to determine whether the central number is the arithmetic mean — meeting the review's problem-solving definition (I5). The study reports random-effects, group-level whole-brain analyses (I6), provides stereotactic coordinates in Talairach space (I7), and reports BOLD fMRI results (I8). Voxelwise/task-related activation patterns and coordinates are described in the main text (I9). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, enabling full assessment. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met.

The study uses task-based fMRI (BOLD) in healthy adult participants performing goal-directed virtual navigation tasks (4/8VM and CSDLT) that require selecting strategies, learning contingencies, planning/sequencing actions to collect objects, and executing navigational operations—consistent with the provided broad definition of problem solving (goal-directed planning and rule-guided actions). It reports group-level whole-brain fMRI analyses (with ROI-restricted searches for hippocampus/caudate but also whole-brain correction procedures), provides stereotactic coordinates for activation peaks, and includes voxelwise BOLD results. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8 and I9; no exclusion criteria are met.

The study uses an n-back working memory task rather than a problem-solving paradigm as defined by the review (goal-directed planning/sequencing to arrive at a solution). Therefore inclusion criterion I5 is not met. Inclusion criteria satisfied: I6 (whole-brain, group-level fMRI analysis in healthy adults), I7 (results reported in MNI stereotactic space / standard space), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), and I9 (voxelwise/cluster results available in figures/maps). No exclusion criteria are triggered (e.g., not ROI-only, includes within-group healthy task effects). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Conclusion: EXCLUDE because the task does not meet the review's definition of problem-solving (I5 not met).

This study is excluded because it does not study a problem-solving task as defined in I5. The task is a NoGo response-inhibition paradigm (establishing and inhibiting prepotent responses), not a problem-solving task involving goal-directed planning, sequencing, or executing operations to reach a previously unknown solution. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain effects in healthy adults present), I7 (stereotactic coordinates reported), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis reported), I9 (voxelwise results reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task is not a problem-solving task). Exclusion criteria met: none. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

Full text provided is incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata). Based on available information, this is an fMRI study of working memory vs. task difficulty, not a problem-solving task as defined in I5. There is no explicit evidence in the provided content that the task involves goal-directed problem solving, planning/sequencing, or applying rule-based operations to reach a solution. The abstract does not report stereotactic coordinates or explicitly state BOLD/rCBF analyses, nor does it provide methods/results to confirm whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results. Therefore it cannot be confirmed to meet the review inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered by the provided information.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of mental-arithmetic problem solving in healthy adults. It uses whole-brain, voxelwise random-effects group analyses (event-related fMRI), reports BOLD activation results with stereotactic Talairach coordinates (Table 1), and presents task-related increases (integration, WM load, arithmetic contrasts). The sample includes healthy adults with scanned subgroup (n=20). All core sections (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, References) are present, so full text appears complete. Therefore it meets I5 (problem-solving task defined by goal-directed arithmetic integration), I6 (whole-brain group-level analysis), I7 (Talairach coordinates reported), I8 (BOLD analysis), and I9 (coordinates in tables). No exclusion criteria apply.

The study uses task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants and reports whole-brain, group-level BOLD results with stereotactic coordinates (Talairach) and voxelwise tables/figures. The mental-operation tasks require subjects to hold a goal (determine final verbal or spatial state) and apply rule-guided sequential updates (advance day or move marker according to numeric instructions), which fits the review’s operational definition of problem solving (goal-directed rule-based planning/sequencing and execution). Methods and results provide whole-brain analyses (random-effects), BOLD contrasts, and coordinates (Table 2, Fig.2). Therefore it meets I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion provided). No exclusion criteria are met.

This is a task-based fMRI study of clinical reasoning using validated MCQs that require goal-directed problem solving (reading, answering, reflecting) consistent with the review’s definition of problem solving. Participants are healthy adult physicians (residents and faculty). The study reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (second-level t-tests with covariates), BOLD results, and stereotactic coordinates in Talairach space with FWE cluster correction. Coordinate tables/figures and beta/ t -statistics are presented. Full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets I5 (problem-solving task), I6 (whole-brain group analyses in healthy adults), I7 (stereotactic coordinate reporting), I8 (BOLD analysis), and I9 (coordinate results provided in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not solely group comparisons, includes healthy-group task effects, and is empirical).

Although this study is a task-based fMRI BOLD study with whole-brain, group-level analyses in healthy adults and reports stereotactic coordinates (meets I6, I7, I8, I9), the experimental task (a modified PASAT) is an attention/working-memory/rapid arithmetic monitoring task rather than a problem-solving task as defined by the review (goal-directed planning/sequencing to find novel or rule-based solutions). The PASAT requires continuous arithmetic and short-term updating rather than the evaluative planning or multi-step problem decomposition characteristic of problem-solving across domains. Therefore I5 (task is a problem-solving task) is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of verbal fluency and task-switching (healthy adults, group-level whole-brain random-effects analysis; Talairach coordinates and BOLD results are reported). It therefore meets I6, I7, I8 and I9. However, the experimental tasks (covert word generation from semantic categories or overlearned sequences and alternating between them) probe attentional switching and verbal fluency rather than a problem-solving paradigm as defined in I5 (no requirement to define a goal and devise/plan a novel sequence of operations to reach a solution or to perform higher-order problem evaluation/planning). Thus I5 is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This study investigates theory-of-mind (false-belief) tasks in children and adults using task-based whole-brain BOLD fMRI and reports stereotactic coordinates. However, it does not examine problem-solving as defined by I5 (goal-directed planning/sequencing/executing operations to reach a previously unknown solution); instead it assesses social-cognitive belief attribution. Thus it fails I5. The full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level analyses in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates/MNI), I8 (BOLD fMRI), I9 (voxelwise results reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (task is ToM/false-belief, not problem-solving per the review definition). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Therefore EXCLUDED.

Although this is an empirical, whole-brain PET study in healthy adults using a task (MCST) that requires rule identification and set-shifting (meets I5) and reports group-level voxelwise results with stereotactic coordinates (meets I6 and I7) and presents voxelwise results in the main text (I9), it does not report BOLD or rCBF analyses. The PET outcome is tracer binding potential ([11C]FLB 457) measuring dopamine release rather than regional cerebral blood flow or BOLD signal. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I8 and must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered.

Although this is an fMRI study with whole-brain, group-level BOLD results reported in standardized (MNI) coordinates, the paradigms are verbal memory and spatial working-memory tasks rather than problem-solving tasks as defined by the review (i.e., goal-directed problem solving requiring evaluation, planning/sequencing actions, or applying rule-based operations to arrive at a novel solution). Thus it meets I6, I7, I8, and I9 but does not meet I5. Full text appears complete.

The study uses a paced overt semantic verbal fluency task (category-driven word generation), which is a language/fluency task rather than a problem-solving task as defined in the review (requires goal-directed planning/sequencing operations to arrive at a solution). Therefore inclusion criterion I5 (task is a problem-solving task) is not met. The study does meet other imaging-related criteria: group-level whole-brain fMRI analyses in healthy adults (I6), reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI space (I7), reports BOLD-based fMRI analyses (I8), and allows voxelwise results presentation (I9). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete. Conclusion: EXCLUDE because I5 not met; other inclusion criteria I6,I7,I8,I9 are satisfied; no exclusion criteria applied.

This is an event-related whole-brain BOLD fMRI study in healthy adult participants performing challenging mental arithmetic under task demands. Mental arithmetic meets the review’s problem-solving definition (goal-directed operations following rule-based algebraic/semantic procedures), satisfying I5. The study reports group-level whole-brain mixed-effects analyses in healthy adults (I6), uses BOLD fMRI (I8), and states that effect maps were transformed to MNI space and that detailed coordinate lists are available (satisfying I7 and I9 per main-text indication that coordinates/tables exist). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not non-empirical, includes healthy-group task effects).

This is a task-based whole-brain fMRI study that uses the Wisconsin Card Sorting (WCS) task (an executive/set-shifting/problem-solving task), includes healthy adult controls with group-level effects (Experiment 1) and uses BOLD fMRI. However, the paper does not report task-related activation increases as stereotactic coordinates (Talairach or MNI). The reported outcomes are whole-brain network metrics, area percentages, and strength-distance plots rather than voxelwise activation coordinates in standardized space. Because inclusion criterion I7 (reports task-related increases as stereotactic coordinate results in Talairach or MNI space) is not met, the study must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is a methods paper applying Bayesian fusion of MEG and fMRI using a visual checkerboard task in a single healthy adult subject. Exclusion criteria met: E3 (reports only ROI-based results / ROI-focused analyses rather than whole-brain, group-level voxelwise effects). Inclusion criteria met: I8 (reports BOLD / fMRI BOLD analyses). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (study does not use a problem-solving task; uses an 8-Hz checkerboard visual stimulation), I6 (no group-level whole-brain analysis in healthy adults; real-data application is a single subject), I7 (no reported task-related stereotactic coordinates for group-level activations in Talairach/MNI space), I9 (no voxelwise group-level coordinate tables/figures of task-related increases are provided). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study does not meet the review’s requirements and is excluded.

Full text is incomplete: provided content is only an HTML skeleton with no introduction, methods, results, or discussion, so core study details cannot be verified. Cannot confirm inclusion criteria: I5 (uncertain whether the task qualifies as a problem-solving task), I6 (unable to verify whole-brain group-level analysis in healthy adults), I7 (no stereotactic coordinates reported in the provided content), I8 (cannot confirm BOLD or rCBF analyses despite title mentioning fMRI), I9 (cannot verify availability of voxelwise coordinate results). No exclusion criteria from the list (E3–E6) can be confirmed from the incomplete text. Therefore excluded due to incomplete full text preventing determination of eligibility.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation in healthy adults of rule-based conditional reasoning (Wason selection-style tasks), which fits the meta-analysis domain of problem-solving (I5). It conducts whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses of healthy adult participants (I6), and reports BOLD fMRI methods and task-related activations (I8). However, the provided full text does not report stereotactic coordinates (Talairach or MNI) for reported activations in the excerpt supplied, and I7 (explicit reporting of coordinates) cannot be confirmed from the available content. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Because ALL inclusion criteria must be met and I7 is not demonstrably satisfied in the provided text, the study must be excluded.
