The study is a task-based fMRI whole-brain group analysis in healthy adults and reports MNI coordinates and BOLD results; however, the experimental paradigm is an SR rule-switching/cognitive control task (updating stimulus–response mappings) rather than a problem-solving task as defined by the review (i.e., requiring goal-directed generation/selection of solutions, planning/sequencing to reach a novel or complex solution). Therefore it does not meet inclusion criterion I5. Inclusion criteria met: I6, I7, I8, I9. Inclusion criterion not met: I5. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

The study is excluded because it does not meet I5: the task is a Stroop color-word interference task measuring cognitive control/inhibition and processing speed, not a problem-solving task as defined (goal-directed planning/sequencing to arrive at a solution). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level fMRI analysis across healthy adults), I7 (results reported in Talairach stereotactic space), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), I9 (voxelwise results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria are triggered (exclusion_criteria_applied = []). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of mental set switching/task set inertia (attribute counting task) rather than a problem-solving task as defined in the review (i.e., goal-directed problems requiring planning/sequencing to arrive at a previously unknown solution). Although the study meets multiple methodological criteria (whole-brain group-level fMRI analyses, stereotactic coordinate reporting, BOLD-based analyses, and coordinates available in text/supplement), it does not examine ‘problem solving’ per the meta-analysis’ I5 definition. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

While this is a task-based, whole-brain BOLD fMRI study with group-level effects, the manuscript does not clearly meet the review's problem-solving definition nor report stereotactic coordinate results for task-related increases. The tasks reported in detail (n-back, JLO, MSIT, COWAT, Word Pair, IAPS, finger tapping, flashing checkerboard) are working memory, visuospatial judgment, attention/conflict, language fluency, memory, emotion, perception and motor paradigms rather than explicit problem-solving (planning/sequencing to reach a goal). Although Tower of London (a planning/problem-solving task) is mentioned, results for it are not presented with coordinate-based activations in the provided full text. Therefore I5 and I7 are not satisfied (I8 and I6 are satisfied). Full text appears complete.

This study is excluded because it does not examine a problem-solving task as defined by the review (it uses a Color-Word Stroop attention/attentional-control paradigm rather than a goal-directed problem-solving task involving planning/sequencing or solution generation) — inclusion criterion I5 not met. In addition, the imaging analyses were constrained to an a priori mask of Stroop-related regions rather than a whole-brain voxelwise search, so inclusion criterion I6 (whole-brain analysis with group-level effects in healthy adults) is not satisfied. The study does meet other technical criteria: it reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI space (I7), uses BOLD fMRI (I8), and presents voxelwise results/coordinates in the main text/tables (I9). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is a single-subject (N=1) fMRI case study reporting within-subject task activations for planning (Tower of London and a VR navigation roadblock task). While it meets several inclusion criteria (I5: task-based fMRI of problem-solving/planning; I7: stereotactic mapping using Talairach coordinates; I8: BOLD fMRI analysis; I9: voxelwise results shown in tables/figures), it does NOT provide group-level, whole-brain effects in healthy adults (no group analysis), thus failing I6. Therefore exclusion criterion E5 applies (no healthy-group task effect/group-level results). Because ALL inclusion criteria must be met and E5 is triggered, the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study of reasoning/problem-solving (Raven-like FIT items: induction, visualization, spatial relations) in healthy adults. Tasks require goal-directed inference and rule-based solution selection consistent with the review's definition of problem solving (I5). The study reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses (second-level voxel-wise analyses; HGF vs LGF and task effects) in healthy adult participants (I6). Stereotactic coordinates are reported in the text and supplementary materials (I7), and analyses are BOLD-based (task-related BOLD signal, percent signal change; I8). Coordinate reporting in figures/tables/supplement is acceptable (I9). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present and sufficient for screening.

This is a task-based fMRI study of arithmetic problem solving in healthy adults (N=28). It reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses (SPM5; data normalized to MNI space) comparing retrieval vs procedural strategies and describes significant activation clusters (e.g., left angular gyrus retrieval>procedural; widespread fronto-parietal procedural>retrieval). BOLD fMRI was used. The manuscript indicates whole-brain contrasts are listed/depicted (tables/figures), satisfying the requirement that stereotactic results are reported or available. Core article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults training and testing complex multiplication problems (a goal-directed procedure requiring planning/sequencing and rule-based operations), reporting group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses. The study used BOLD fMRI, normalized data into Talairach space, applied voxelwise statistical thresholds, and reports activation foci for contrasts (trained vs untrained, etc.), consistent with stereotactic reporting (and acceptable when coordinates are in tables/figures as indicated). Therefore it satisfies I5 (problem-solving arithmetic task), I6 (whole-brain, group-level healthy adults), I7 (data normalized to Talairach stereotactic space and task-related activations reported), I8 (BOLD fMRI analyses), and I9 (voxelwise results indicated as available in main text/tables). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not group-comparison-only, empirical healthy adult task effects present). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adults using a computer-based Trail Making Test (pcTMT) that requires a goal (connect/identify stimuli in sequence), planning/sequencing responses, and executing rule-based operations (number/letter switching), meeting the review’s operational definition of problem-solving/set-shifting. The study conducted whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (one-sample t-tests and mixed-effects ANOVA) in healthy adult participants, used BOLD fMRI, and normalized results to Talairach space; ROI coordinates are reported and the text indicates whole-brain cluster results (coordinates likely presented in figures/tables). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, non-empirical, or patient-only contrasts) apply. Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

The paper does not investigate problem-solving as defined in I5. The tasks used (auditory oddball, Sternberg item recognition, and sensorimotor) probe attention, working memory/recognition, and sensorimotor processing rather than goal-directed problem solving, planning/sequencing, or rule-based solution generation. While the study includes healthy adult groups and whole-brain fMRI analyses, it does not report stereotactic coordinate tables required by I7 (the paper shows spatial component maps but no explicit Talairach/MNI coordinate results in the provided text). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level effects in healthy adults) and I8 (BOLD fMRI analyses). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (problem-solving task as defined) and I7 (stereotactic coordinate results). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

Excluded because the study does not meet the review's definition of a problem-solving task and does not report whole-brain stereotactic results. (a) Exclusion criteria met: E3 (analysis restricted to an anatomical mask/ROI rather than whole-brain). (b) Inclusion criteria met: I8 (task-related BOLD fMRI analysis was performed). (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task is a 1-back matching/visual attention task, not a defined problem-solving task), I6 (no whole-brain group-level analysis in healthy adults; analyses were constrained to a visual-region mask), I7 (no stereotactic coordinates in standard Talairach/MNI space reported). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study is not eligible for inclusion in this meta-analysis.

The study uses task-based fMRI in healthy adults and includes a well-characterized mental rotation task that meets the review’s definition of problem solving (goal-directed spatial transformation/decision to determine if objects are identical or mirrored). It reports whole-brain, group-level GLM analyses (multi-subject results), uses BOLD fMRI, and presents stereotactic coordinates in Talairach space for task-related effects. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and Conclusions. No exclusion criteria apply.

This study reports whole-brain task-based BOLD fMRI in healthy adult participants performing a 3D cube comparison (dynamic visuo-spatial imagery) task that requires applying rules and mental operations to determine whether two cubes are identical—consistent with a problem-solving definition involving goal-directed evaluation and rule-based operations. The study performed group-level analyses (n=8), produced grand mean ITC maps, reported voxelwise results including MNI coordinates for significant clusters, and describes BOLD activation patterns. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply. Note: confidence is moderate (0.70) because the task is primarily visuo-spatial/mental-rotation; its classification as a problem-solving task is reasonable but could be seen as borderline depending on stricter definitions of problem solving.

Exclusion decision based on criterion I5 not met. The study is an fMRI investigation of visuo-spatial mental rotation (visuo-spatial working memory) in healthy adults and thus satisfies I6 (whole-brain random-effects group analyses), I7 (results reported in stereotactic space/BA localization and presumably coordinates in main/supplementary material), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), and I9 (voxelwise results reported/available). However, it does not investigate a problem-solving task as defined by I5: mental rotation requires spatial transformation/manipulation to judge congruence, but does not primarily involve goal-directed problem solving characterized by evaluating a problem, planning/sequencing actions, or executing operations within a rule-based framework to derive a previously unknown solution. Therefore I5 is not satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) were met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation of complex working memory (reading/listening span) with whole-brain BOLD analyses in healthy adults and patient groups. However, the experimental paradigm targets working memory and cognitive effort rather than a problem-solving task as defined by the review (goal-directed problem solving involving evaluation, planning/sequencing of actions, and execution within a rule set to reach a solution). Thus inclusion criterion I5 (study of a problem-solving task as defined) is not met. The paper does meet other inclusion criteria: whole-brain, group-level fMRI analyses in healthy adults (I6), reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI space (I7), reports BOLD analyses (I8), and provides voxelwise results in main text/tables/figures (I9). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study is excluded for not meeting I5.

This is a task-based fMRI study of mental calculation (multiplication) in healthy adults, which fits the review's problem-solving definition (goal-directed operations following rule sets). The paper reports whole-brain group-level fMRI analyses, provides stereotactic coordinates in MNI space (peak coordinates reported), and uses BOLD fMRI. The full article contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion (full text appears complete). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not a between-group-only contrast, and not a non-empirical paper). Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied.

The study used a task involving simple multiplication verification (arithmetic fact retrieval), which constitutes rule-based/problem-solving in the algebraic domain (I5). It tested 10 healthy adult participants and performed group-level, whole-brain random-effects fMRI analyses (I6). The imaging analysis reports BOLD fMRI results and peak voxel localization using Talairach/MNI referencing and cluster-level correction; voxelwise activations are described and reported in figures/tables (I7,I8,I9). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so core content appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, patient-only comparisons, non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis of whole-brain task-based fMRI studies of problem-solving in healthy adults.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants that required participants to learn and apply abstract rules to classify sequences (explicit rule extraction, evaluation of grammaticality, and sequencing of elements), which meets the review’s problem-solving definition. The study reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise BOLD fMRI analyses (random-effects), presents stereotactic Talairach coordinates for task-related activations, and provides voxelwise results (with ROI analyses supplemental). Therefore inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, task-based BOLD fMRI study of arithmetic problem solving (single-digit addition) that includes healthy adult participants (n=20) and reports group-level whole-brain analyses. The task meets the review’s definition of problem solving (goal-directed arithmetic verification requiring rule-based operations and strategy use). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level effects (including cross-sectional comparisons with adults), provides stereotactic coordinates in MNI space, and uses BOLD fMRI analyses. Results are presented in the main text and methods with coordinates and searchlight/ROI findings. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8 and I9. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults using a rule-switching task that requires applying rule-based operations to produce correct responses (goal-directed rule evaluation, planning/sequencing actions and executing responses), meeting the review definition of problem solving. It reports group-level whole-brain second-level analyses (full-factorial SPM), with voxelwise stereotactic coordinates (e.g., caudate 24 20 18; aMPFC 12 52 28) in standardized space after normalization (MNI), and BOLD fMRI results with FWE whole-brain correction. Results (coordinates and contrasts) are reported in text/figures. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I5 (task is mental calculation—a problem-solving/algebraic task), I6 (group-level fMRI effects reported in healthy adults), I8 (BOLD fMRI analyses reported). Inclusion IDs not met: I7 (the paper does not report task-related stereotactic coordinates in Talairach or MNI space in the full text provided), I9 (no tables/figures/supplementary stereotactic coordinate listings are available or clearly indicated). Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). Because the study fails to report stereotactic coordinates (I7) and does not provide voxelwise coordinate results in accessible tables/figures/supplementary materials (I9), it does not satisfy all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This study used a cognitive-control (Preparing to Overcome Prepotency, POP) task to probe locus coeruleus activity under modafinil, not a problem-solving task as defined (goal-directed planning/sequencing to derive a solution across semantic, logical, algebraic, etc.). Thus it fails inclusion criterion I5. The paper is a task-based whole-brain BOLD fMRI study in healthy adults and references coordinate tables in the supplement, so it meets I6, I8, and I9. However, stereotactic coordinate reporting in Talairach/MNI space (I7) is not explicitly verifiable in the provided full text. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Therefore EXCLUDED because it does not investigate a problem-solving task (I5 not met) and I7 is not confirmed.

This is a task-based whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adults that includes a mental calculation (silent subtraction) task that requires executing arithmetic operations according to rules to reach a correct solution, which fits the review’s definition of problem solving. The study reports group-level random-effects (RFX) whole-brain analyses on 81 healthy adults, provides stereotactic coordinates in MNI space, and uses BOLD fMRI (EPI) measures. Results (coordinates, figures, tables) are reported across the paper. Full text contains background, methods, results, and discussion, and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, non-empirical, or absence of healthy-group task effects) are met.

Full text is incomplete: provided 'Full Text Content' contains an API error message rather than the article text, so I cannot verify necessary details. Based on available metadata alone, I cannot confirm any inclusion criteria: I5 (uncertain whether the task is a problem-solving task as defined), I6 (uncertain if task-based whole-brain fMRI or PET with group-level effects in healthy adults was performed), I7 (uncertain if stereotactic coordinates reported), I8 (uncertain whether BOLD or rCBF analyses were reported), I9 (uncertain if voxelwise results reported). No exclusion criteria (E3-E6) can be confirmed from the metadata. Because the full text is missing, the study cannot be reliably assessed for inclusion and is excluded pending full-text retrieval.

The study is task-based fMRI of relational reasoning (meets I5) and reports whole-brain activations with stereotactic coordinates (I7), reports BOLD analyses (I8), and provides voxelwise results described in text/tables (I9). However, it does not present a whole-brain, group-level task effect reported specifically for healthy adult individuals alone (I6 not met). The main whole-brain Relational>Control results are reported across a mixed-age sample and group-level coordinates are presented averaged across age groups; adult-only whole-brain coordinates or adult-only group-level contrasts are not clearly reported in the full text. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Therefore the study is excluded because it fails to satisfy I6 (whole-brain group-level effects in healthy adult individuals).

This is a task-based whole-brain BOLD fMRI study in healthy adults (26 included in fMRI analyses) reporting stereotactic coordinates (Talairach) and whole-brain random effects analyses. However, the experimental paradigm is a sentence–picture matching task probing spatial frame-of-reference interpretations (language and spatial perception/semantics) induced by feedback. It does not constitute a problem-solving paradigm as defined in the review (no goal-directed search/planning or execution of operations to reach a previously unknown solution; rather it is a matching/interpretation judgment). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults using a multi-attribute decision-making paradigm that requires goal-directed evaluation and application of decision heuristics (integration, comparison, selection)—fitting the review's problem-solving definition. It reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses, uses BOLD fMRI, and explicitly aligns data to Talairach stereotactic space; voxelwise results are indicated (tables/figures referenced), satisfying coordinate reporting requirements. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so appears complete.

The study is excluded because it does not examine a problem-solving task as defined by I5; it investigates visual imagery/perception (face imagery) in a case study and controls, not goal-directed problem solving. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (contains whole-brain group-level analyses for healthy controls and MX), I7 (reports stereotactic results in MNI space), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), I9 (voxelwise results reported/available). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (problem-solving task). No exclusion criteria from the list apply. Full text appears complete.

This study uses mental calculation tasks (appropriate as problem-solving) and includes simultaneous fMRI in healthy adults with group-level analyses, and performs BOLD imaging. However, the paper does not report stereotactic coordinates (Talairach or MNI) or any voxelwise coordinate tables in the provided full text; activations are described and shown as images but coordinates are absent. Because Inclusion Criterion I7 (stereotactic coordinate reporting) is not met, the study cannot be included. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based mental calculation problem-solving), I6 (group-level whole-brain fMRI analysis in healthy adults), I8 (BOLD/fMRI reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (no stereotactic coordinates reported), I9 (no indication that voxelwise coordinate results/tables are available). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This study is excluded because it does not investigate problem-solving tasks in healthy adults. It uses a simple auditory-motor sensorimotor tapping task, not a goal-directed problem-solving paradigm (I5 not met). It does not provide whole-brain, group-level problem-solving results in healthy adults (I6 not met). The paper does not report stereotactic activation coordinates for task-related increases (I7 not met; normalization to MNI is mentioned but no coordinates/tables of coordinates are provided). It does, however, report BOLD analyses (I8 met). The analysis is restricted to a priori ROIs and reports ROI-based percent signal change and activation volumes, i.e., ROI-only results, which meets exclusion criterion E3. Full text appears complete. Therefore excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=62, fMRI analyses on 15) that investigates inductive/category-based reasoning (the inclusion fallacy). The task requires participants to evaluate and compare alternative arguments (critical evaluation/semantic logical reasoning), which fits the review's definition of problem solving involving goal-directed evaluation/decision processes. The study reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses using SPM5 with voxelwise thresholds and cluster correction (AlphaSim), provides stereotactic coordinates in MNI space, and reports BOLD fMRI results. All required inclusion criteria are satisfied (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not a clinical/group-comparison-only study, includes healthy-group task effects, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study is an fMRI investigation of sunk-cost decision-making (economic risk/reward choices), not a problem-solving task as defined by the review (i.e., tasks requiring goal-directed planning, sequencing actions, or applying rule-based operations to arrive at a correct/novel solution). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level effects in healthy adults) and I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (the task is an economic decision-making paradigm, not a problem-solving task per the review definition), I7 (the provided full text does not report stereotactic coordinates in Talairach or MNI space in the excerpt), I9 (no confirmation that voxelwise coordinates/tables/figures with coordinates are provided in the provided text). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore excluded for not meeting the primary task-definition inclusion (I5) and lacking explicit coordinate reporting (I7/I9) in the provided content.

This is a task-based BOLD fMRI study in healthy adults that evaluates probabilistic reasoning/decision-making (modified beads/JTC paradigm) where participants have the explicit goal of identifying the source lake and must gather and evaluate evidence (deciding whether to draw more samples) to reach a decision — consistent with problem-solving as defined. The paper reports group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses, provides stereotactic MNI coordinates for activations, includes BOLD fMRI analyses, and reports voxelwise results in text/figures/ROIs. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of problem solving using the Tower of London paradigm (planning and movement execution), conducted in healthy adult participants (right-handed students). It reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses (SPM99) with cluster-level inference and provides stereotactic coordinates (Talairach) for task-related activations. BOLD fMRI was used and voxelwise results are described in the main text and figures. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, enabling assessment against inclusion criteria.

This study does not meet the review’s problem-solving task definition (I5). It reports a visual target identification task manipulating perceptual load and distractors (attention/working memory), not a problem-solving task requiring goal-directed planning, sequencing, or critical evaluation to arrive at a novel/correct solution. Met inclusion criteria: I6 (whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses in healthy adults), I7 (results referenced in MNI stereotactic space and group t-maps/figure coordinates), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), I9 (voxelwise results presented in figures/tables). No exclusion criteria are met (e.g., not ROI-only, includes within-group healthy task effects, is empirical). Therefore excluded because I5 is not satisfied.

This is an fMRI study of verbal working memory using a Sternberg recognition task (maintain and probe consonant lists). While it meets imaging and reporting criteria (whole-brain group fMRI, stereotactic coordinates reported, BOLD analysis, results in tables/figures), it does not investigate problem solving as defined by I5 (no goal-directed problem-solving, planning/sequencing to reach a novel solution; task tests short-term maintenance and recognition rather than evaluating/performing multi-step problem-solving). Therefore I5 is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (includes methods, results, discussion).

Although this is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults with whole-brain voxelwise BOLD analyses and voxel/ROI summaries, it does not report task-related stereotactic coordinates (Talairach/MNI) for activations or peaks in the manuscript text or tables provided here. Therefore inclusion criterion I7 is not met. The study does meet I5 (the motor mental-rotation task involves a goal and rule-based planning/execution), I6 (whole-brain analyses with group-level effects in healthy adults), I8 (BOLD fMRI analyses), and I9 (voxelwise results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

The study uses the Tower of London task, a well-established problem-solving/planning paradigm (goal-directed planning with sequencing of moves), and reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects fMRI analyses in healthy adult participants. Images were normalized to the MNI template and task-related activation coordinates are reported (e.g., MNI coordinates shown), and BOLD (EPI) analyses are explicitly performed and quantified. Voxelwise results are presented in figures/tables in the main text. The full text (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I9 are satisfied, and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study uses a task requiring participants to find a hidden goal in a virtual maze, which meets the review's operational definition of problem solving (goal-directed planning/sequencing and execution). It is a task-based fMRI study reporting BOLD signal results (I8). Whole-brain, group-level analyses for healthy control subjects are reported (ANOVAs and statistical maps), satisfying I6. Task-related activations are reported in standardized stereotactic coordinates (Talairach coordinates reported, e.g., 18 -61 40), satisfying I7. Voxelwise/whole-brain results are described in the main text and maps/tables are indicated as available, satisfying I9. Therefore all required inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8 and I9 are met. The full text provided contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete is false. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

The study is excluded because it does not examine a problem-solving task as defined by the review (I5 not met): the task is a prolonged visual search/fatigue task (attention/perception), not a goal-directed problem-solving task involving planning/sequencing/critical evaluation. It does meet I6 (includes whole-brain, group-level fMRI analyses that include healthy adults) and I8 (reports BOLD fMRI analyses). I7 (reporting stereotactic coordinates in Talairach/MNI space) cannot be confirmed from the provided full text (tables referenced but coordinates not shown). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete.

Full text is complete. The study is an event-related whole-brain BOLD fMRI investigation of an Embedded Figures Task (EFT) in healthy adults. It meets I6 (group-level, whole-brain analysis in healthy adults), I7 (reports Talairach stereotactic coordinates), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), and I9 (voxelwise results shown in figures/tables). However, it does NOT meet I5: the task is a perceptual visual-search/disembedding task (searching for a simple shape within a complex figure) and is best characterized as attentional/perceptual processing rather than a problem-solving task as defined by the review (goal-directed planning, sequencing, rule-based operations to arrive at a novel solution). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Therefore the paper should be excluded because it fails to satisfy inclusion criterion I5.

This is a task-based fMRI study of deductive/logical reasoning (meets I5) using BOLD-sensitive 3D PRESTO (meets I8) and includes healthy adult controls. However, the paper reports results as voxel counts within manually segmented VOIs/Brodmann areas rather than providing stereotactic (Talairach/MNI) coordinates or voxelwise whole-brain coordinate maps. Therefore it does not provide whole-brain voxelwise, stereotactic coordinate results required by I7, and it effectively reports ROI-based results rather than whole-brain coordinate-based group maps, so I6 (whole-brain voxelwise group-level effects with coordinates) is not satisfied. This violates exclusion criterion E3 (reports only ROI results). Inclusion criteria met: I5, I8. Inclusion criteria not met: I6, I7 (and thus I9 not satisfied because no stereotactic coordinates/tables of coordinates are provided). Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (n=15) that investigates relational integration/ reasoning (a form of problem solving akin to Raven-like tasks). The task requires participants to evaluate and integrate relations to reach correct responses, satisfying the problem-solving definition (goal-directed evaluation and relational operations). The paper reports group-level whole-brain fMRI analyses with MNI coordinates (e.g., −36 57 9), and BOLD-based contrasts (Dimension > Feature), meeting neuroimaging reporting requirements. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not clinical-only, not non-empirical).

Full text provided appears to be only title/abstract/metadata (fulltext_incomplete=true). The study uses task-based fMRI in healthy adults and reports load-related PFC activity, so it meets I6 (whole-brain group-level effects reported in abstract via whole-brain imaging in experiment 2) and I8 (fMRI BOLD). However, the task is a working memory sequential-letter load manipulation, which does not meet the review's definition of a problem-solving task (I5 not met). Additionally, the abstract does not report stereotactic coordinates (I7 unverified) nor confirm availability of voxelwise coordinate tables or figures (I9 unverified). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered by the available information. Because the core full text is not provided and the task does not satisfy the problem-solving definition, the study is excluded.

The study is excluded because it does not meet the review’s problem-solving task definition and does not provide whole-brain task-related activations for healthy controls separately. Exclusion criteria met: E5 — the paper primarily reports between-group contrasts (high-risk vs controls) with stereotactic coordinates for those group differences; main task-related activation coordinates for a healthy adult group are not reported independently. Inclusion criteria met: I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI for reported effects), I8 (task-based BOLD fMRI), I9 (voxelwise coordinate results reported in text/figures). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task is a Hayling sentence completion/verbal fluency/executive initiation task and does not clearly satisfy the meta-analysis definition of a problem-solving task requiring planning/sequencing operations across domains), I6 (no clear whole-brain, group-level task effect reported for healthy adults alone). Full text appears complete. Given these gaps, the study is not eligible for inclusion in this meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants using a fluid analogy problem-solving task. It reports group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses (FLAME) and presents stereotactic (MNI) coordinates for activated clusters, and BOLD contrast results. The task meets the review’s definition of problem solving (goal-directed analogy completion requiring rule-based transformations and evaluation/planning), and voxelwise results are reported for group effects. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not non-empirical, includes within-group healthy-task effects). Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results, and discussion.

Excluded because the experimental task (Multi-Source Interference Task, MSIT) is a response-interference/conflict-monitoring task focused on stimulus-response selection and cognitive control, not a problem-solving task as defined in inclusion criterion I5 (goal-directed planning/sequencing to derive a correct or novel solution). The study does satisfy other inclusion criteria: I6 (includes whole-brain group-level effects in healthy adult subjects), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates in standardized space), I8 (reports BOLD fMRI results), and I9 (voxelwise results presented in figures/tables). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete and contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion.

Full text is complete. This study is excluded because it does not meet the review’s definition of a problem-solving task (I5). The tasks are spatial imagery/judgement (coordinate vs categorical clock judgments) rather than goal-directed problem-solving requiring planning/sequencing or operations to derive previously unknown solutions. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level fMRI in healthy adults), I7 (data normalized to Talairach stereotactic space), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), I9 (results presented as maps/figures consistent with stereotactic reporting). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task does not operationalize problem-solving as defined). Exclusion criteria met: none ([]) .

This fMRI study includes a visuospatial planning (Tower of London) task that fits the review's definition of problem solving (goal-directed planning/sequencing to reach a solution). Imaging used task-based BOLD fMRI (I8) and performed whole-brain analyses (two-sample t tests, main task effects reported) with group-level effects that include a healthy control (HC) group and post-hoc comparisons involving HCs (satisfying I6). Results are reported in standardized stereotactic space (MNI) and voxelwise results are available in Supplementary Table S7 and figure plots (satisfying I7 and I9). The task paradigm and analyses meet the operational definition of problem-solving across domains (I5). No exclusion criteria are met: analyses are not ROI-only (E3), the study includes healthy-group task effects rather than only between-group contrasts (not E5), and it is empirical human fMRI data (not E6). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, supplementary references noted). Therefore the study should be included for the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study of a dual working-memory/attention task (Kana Pick-out Test) in healthy young adults. While it provides whole-brain, group-level BOLD analyses normalized to MNI space (methods describe SPM/MNI normalization and conjunction/subtraction contrasts) and likely reports stereotactic coordinates in tables/figures, the experimental task does not meet the review's operational definition of a problem-solving task. The KPT requires parallel vowel detection and story comprehension (divided attention, short-term storage, and executive processes) but does not require formulating or planning novel solutions, sequencing actions to reach a goal beyond routine task execution, or performing critical thinking to derive previously unknown solutions. Therefore I5 (problem-solving task) is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

The paper is a task-based fMRI study of insight/problem-solving using Chinese logogriphs in healthy adults, with whole-brain random-effects analyses and BOLD contrasts reported. However, the provided full text does not include stereotactic coordinate tables or explicit Talairach/MNI coordinates (figures/tables appear omitted: “These results are summarized in and .”), so I cannot verify inclusion criterion I7. Therefore I must exclude due to incomplete reporting of coordinates in the supplied full text. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (problem-solving task), I6 (whole-brain group-level analysis in healthy adults), I8 (BOLD analysis reported), I9 (results indicated to be available in tables/figures). Inclusion criterion not verifiable/met: I7 (stereotactic coordinate results in Talairach or MNI space not present in the provided content). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears incomplete for coordinate verification.

The study is an empirical task-based fMRI investigation in healthy adults that includes a mental calculation (subtraction) task that meets the review's problem-solving definition (goal-directed operations following arithmetic rules). It reports group-level voxelwise BOLD results with stereotactic coordinates (MNI) and provides voxelwise results. However, it does not provide whole-brain coverage: acquisition consisted of 18 axial slices covering the parietal lobe and much of prefrontal cortex but explicitly excluded the orbitofrontal sector, indicating partial brain coverage rather than whole-brain analysis. Because inclusion criterion I6 (at least one whole-brain group-level analysis) is not met, the study must be excluded despite meeting other inclusion criteria.

Exclusion decision: This study is excluded because it does not investigate a problem-solving task as defined by the review (I5 not met). Instead, it uses perceptual discrimination and task-switching paradigms (color/face/motion/spatial-frequency judgments) rather than tasks requiring goal-driven problem solving, planning/sequencing operations, or deriving previously unknown solutions. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level fMRI in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates in Talairach space), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), I9 (voxelwise results reported in tables/figures). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (task-based problem solving). Exclusion criteria met: none ([]) — the paper includes whole-brain analyses and healthy-group task effects. fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an fMRI study of semantic selection (verb generation) and verbal working memory interference (recent-probes). While it meets several methodological criteria (whole-brain/group-level fMRI, stereotactic coordinates, and BOLD analyses), it does not investigate a problem-solving task as defined in the review (I5). The tasks involve semantic retrieval and interference-resolution/selection processes, not goal-directed problem solving requiring planning/sequencing operations to reach an unknown solution. Therefore exclude. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I6, I7, I8, I9. Inclusion IDs not met: I5.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants that directly examines mental arithmetic (subtraction and multiplication) which fits the review’s definition of problem-solving (goal-directed operations to arrive at correct solutions). The study reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses (I6), uses BOLD fMRI (I8), and describes normalization to MNI space and voxelwise cluster results (satisfying I7 and I9 — voxelwise results are indicated as available in figures/tables). The tasks involve goal-directed computational procedures (I5). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not a between-group only contrast, empirical data in healthy adults). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study using a cued word-categorization (task-switching) paradigm that requires rule-based operations (semantic categorizations) and preparatory executive processes consistent with the review's broad definition of problem solving (goal-directed selection and execution of operations within rule sets). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level analyses in healthy adult participants (younger and older), provides stereotactic coordinates (MNI/Talairach), and reports BOLD fMRI results. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Excluded because the experimental task (two-choice prediction/response) probes decision-making and outcome-contingent responding under uncertainty rather than a problem-solving paradigm as defined in I5 (tasks requiring evaluation, planning/sequencing actions and executing operations to reach a previously unknown solution across domains). The study does satisfy I6 (includes whole-brain group-level effects in healthy adult controls), I7 (reports Talairach stereotactic coordinates), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), and I9 (voxelwise results are reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete.

The study is an fMRI investigation with whole-brain, group-level analysis (I6) using BOLD fMRI (I8) and the manuscript indicates voxelwise results/tables are available (I9). However, the experimental task is a semantic true/false verification task, not an explicit goal-directed, multi-step problem-solving paradigm as defined for this review (does not meet I5). Also, the provided full text does not explicitly list stereotactic coordinate tables in the excerpt available here (I7 not clearly met). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore the study is excluded because it does not meet the required definition of a problem-solving task (I5) and stereotactic coordinates are not clearly reported in the provided text (I7).

Although this is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults reporting whole-brain group analyses, stereotactic coordinates (Talairach), and BOLD results (I6, I7, I8, I9 met), the task is perceptual category learning/classification (prototype-distortion; same/different category judgments after training). It does not involve problem solving as defined by the review (goal-directed problem solving requiring planning/sequencing or executing operations to reach a novel solution or apply higher-order critical thinking). The imaging task tests application of learned categories and perceptual discrimination rather than planning or complex rule-based problem solving, so inclusion criterion I5 is not met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants (Chinese university students) using an equation-verification paradigm that requires goal-directed evaluation and execution of arithmetic operations—meeting the review’s problem-solving definition (I5). The study reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses (I6) and uses BOLD fMRI (I8). The manuscript describes voxelwise contrasts with statistical thresholds and refers to activation loci presented in figures/tables (consistent with reporting stereotactic voxelwise results in standard space and acceptable per I9); normalization and SPM2 procedures imply use of standardized space (I7). The article includes full methods, results, and discussion (full text appears complete). Not limited to ROI-only reporting. No exclusion criteria are met.

This study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I5. The task used (Colour Word Interference Test / Stroop) is a cognitive control/response-inhibition and attention interference task that requires following an instructed rule (name the ink color) rather than engaging in problem-solving as defined by I5 (goal-directed need to figure out a way, evaluate the problem, plan or sequence actions, or generate a novel solution). The study does meet other inclusion criteria: I6 (whole-brain, group-level fMRI in healthy adults), I7 (reports results in standardized MNI space), I8 (BOLD/fMRI analysis), and I9 (voxelwise results reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Full text is complete and the study is an fMRI investigation in healthy adults reporting whole-brain, group-level BOLD results with stereotactic coordinates. However, it does not examine a problem-solving task as defined by the review (I5). The tasks are mental-rotation/mental-imagery spatial transformation judgments (imagined self vs. object rotations) requiring perceptual/cognitive transformation and visibility judgments, not goal-directed problem solving involving planning/sequencing operations to reach a previously unknown solution under a rule set. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level analysis in healthy adults), I7 (coordinates in Talairach/MNI), I8 (BOLD fMRI), I9 (voxelwise results reported). No exclusion criteria are met. Hence excluded on the basis of I5 not met.

This article is a narrative/review summary of multiple neuroimaging studies from the authors’ laboratory rather than a single empirical task-based fMRI or PET report presenting original whole-brain, stereotactic coordinate results. It summarizes PET and fMRI work (e.g., MIST mental-arithmetic stress task) but does not itself present group-level, whole-brain coordinate tables or original BOLD/rCBF voxelwise results necessary for meta-analysis inclusion. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E6 (non-empirical/review) and does not satisfy the required inclusion criteria (I5–I9) for primary task-based imaging studies reporting stereotactic coordinates.

This is a task-based fMRI experiment investigating deductive problem-solving (three-term transitive inference / acoustic reasoning), meeting the definition of a problem-solving task. Participants were healthy adults (n=12) and analyses used whole-brain, random-effects SPM5 statistics. Data were normalized to standard stereotactic space and the manuscript reports peak activations and cluster-level voxelwise results (example coordinates given), and BOLD fMRI was used. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion, so core content is present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, patient-group-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) apply.

This study reports whole-brain, task-based BOLD fMRI during the Wisconsin Card Sorting Task, which meets the meta-analysis definition of problem solving (goal-directed rule discovery, evaluation of feedback, planning/executing rule-based responses). It includes group-level whole-brain analyses for healthy adult control subjects and reports stereotactic (Talairach) peak coordinates in tables/figures. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion (appears complete). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; includes healthy-group task effects). Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9.

The study is an fMRI investigation of fairness and intentionality using a modified Ultimatum Game (social decision-making), not a problem-solving task as defined by the review (I5). Although it meets several methodological inclusion criteria — whole-brain group-level analyses including adults (I6), stereotactic coordinate reporting in MNI space (I7), and BOLD fMRI analyses (I8) — and its voxelwise results are available (I9), the task does not involve goal-directed problem solving requiring planning/sequencing operations to reach a correct/optimal solution. No exclusion criteria are triggered. Therefore the paper must be excluded because it fails to meet I5 (problem-solving task).

This study is an fMRI investigation of bimodal (visual and auditory) divided-attention/perceptual discrimination tasks, not a problem-solving task as defined by the review. It includes whole-brain group-level BOLD analyses in healthy adults with stereotactic (MNI) reporting, but it does not involve goal-directed problem solving, planning/sequencing, or execution of rule-based operations to derive novel solutions (I5 not met). Full text appears complete.

The study is excluded because it does not meet I5. Although it is a task-based, whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adults (I6) reporting BOLD results with stereotactic coordinates (MNI) (I7, I8) and provides voxelwise results/supplementary coordinates (I9), the experimental task was an incidental same–different memory/comparison task that explicitly did not require mathematical calculation or goal-directed problem solving. The authors state the task “does not require explicit syntactical parsing or mathematical calculation,” so it does not satisfy the review’s definition of a problem-solving task (goal-directed planning/sequencing to reach a solution) (I5 not met). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

The study examines a goal-directed, dynamic decision task in healthy adults requiring subjects to identify and implement strategies to maximize long-term reward (goal: earn money; need to figure out which deck selections over trials produce maximal payoff). This involves temporal integration, evaluation of outcomes, and sequencing of choices—processes consistent with the review’s definition of problem solving (evaluating the problem, planning/sequencing actions, executing operations under task rules). The study used task-based whole-brain fMRI BOLD analyses at the group level in healthy adults (n=26), reports stereotactic coordinates in Talairach space (Table 2), and provides voxelwise/task-related results in text/figures. Therefore inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not a between-group/disease-only comparison, and is empirical). Full text appears complete with Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion.

This full-text describes a task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants that includes an explicitly described hard non-semantic phoneme-segmentation task characterized by problem-solving, working memory, and meta-linguistic demands. The study reports whole-brain, group-level BOLD analyses with cluster-corrected stereotactic results and ROI analyses; stereotactic/localization is provided using standard atlases and coordinates. The manuscript contains full methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets the review inclusion criteria: (I5) contains a problem-solving task (phoneme segmentation described as problem-solving), (I6) whole-brain group-level fMRI analyses in healthy adults, (I7) stereotactic results reported/labelled, (I8) BOLD fMRI analyses reported, and (I9) voxelwise/whole-brain results presented. No exclusion criteria are met and the full text appears complete.

Full text provided is incomplete (HTML shell only) so core methods/results are unavailable. Based on available metadata (title: fMRI study of context processing in patients with schizophrenia), the study likely does not address problem-solving in healthy adults. Inclusion criteria not met (or cannot be verified): I5 (does not describe a problem-solving task), I6 (does not report group-level effects in healthy adults), I7 (stereotactic coordinates not available in the provided content), I8 (BOLD/rCBF analyses cannot be confirmed), I9 (voxelwise results availability cannot be confirmed). No explicit exclusion criteria from the review are demonstrably met given the incomplete text. Because the full article content (introduction, methods, results) is missing, I cannot reliably evaluate inclusion criteria. Recommend obtaining full text for definitive screening.

Although this is an empirical, whole-brain task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that reports stereotactic coordinates and BOLD analyses, the experimental task (probabilistic category learning/weather-prediction and paired-associate learning) is an associative/category-learning paradigm rather than a problem-solving task as defined by the review (i.e., it does not require planning/sequencing or executing rule-guided operations to reach an explicitly defined goal/solution). Therefore I5 (problem-solving task) is not met, so the study must be excluded.

The task (wayfinding in a virtual town) fits the meta-analysis definition of problem solving: participants have a goal (navigate from one landmark to another) and must plan/sequence actions to derive the shortest route (allocentric cognitive-map-based planning). The study used task-based BOLD fMRI (I8) in healthy adult controls and reports within-group and between-group whole-brain analyses (I6), with standard stereotactic normalization to ICBM/MNI space and references to result tables/figures (voxelwise results expected to be reported) satisfying I7 and I9. Whole-brain statistical thresholds (FWE) are reported and ROI analyses were supplemented by whole-brain results, so this is not ROI-only. Confidence reduced slightly (0.80) because numeric stereotactic coordinates and tables/figures are referenced but not visible in the provided text excerpt; however the methods explicitly describe standardized-space normalization and the results reference tables/figures of activations, supporting inclusion.

The study is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants using the Wisconsin Card Sorting Task (WCST), which requires deducing and applying rules via feedback (goal-directed problem solving, planning/sequencing, and executing rule-based operations). It reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects BOLD analyses across 11 healthy adults, presents stereotactic localization in Talairach space with tables/figures of activation peaks, and provides voxelwise results and thresholding methods. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study using series-completion inductive reasoning tasks that meet the review’s problem-solving definition (identify a rule/goal and apply operations to generate a correct unknown solution). Group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses are reported (with FDR correction). Results include stereotactic coordinates (Talairach/MNI) and BOLD signal analyses. Voxelwise results are reported in main text/supplement. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (N=16) examining analogical reasoning (fluid analogizing and unique-symbol counting). The tasks require evaluating analogy plausibility and applying transformation rules (alphabetic/numeric/order of polygons), which constitute problem-solving operations (goal-directed evaluation and rule-based operations). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses with voxelwise thresholding and cluster correction, provides stereotactic MNI coordinates (e.g., MNI 46,30,-12) and discusses BOLD results. Thus it meets I5 (problem-solving task as defined), I6 (whole-brain group analysis in healthy adults), I7 (stereotactic coordinates in MNI), I8 (BOLD analysis), and I9 (voxelwise results reported). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=16) that investigates analogical reasoning requiring generation of abstract rules and mapping them to targets. The task meets the review’s problem-solving definition (I5): subjects form a goal, discover/apply rules (e.g., linear relations, arithmetic rules, symmetry) and select correct targets, involving evaluation, planning/sequence of operations, and rule-based solution finding. The study reports group-level whole-brain analyses (I6) with BOLD fMRI (I8) and provides stereotactic MNI coordinates for task-related activations (I7). Voxelwise results and ROI analyses with coordinates are presented in the main text (I9). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This paper reports PET rCBF and group-level SPM methods in healthy adults and discusses psychophysiological paradigms, but it does not study a problem-solving task as defined for the review (it examines verbal creative thinking/creativity tasks, not goal-directed problem solving with rule-based solutions) — therefore I5 is not satisfied. From the provided full text, whole-brain group analyses using PET/rCBF and SPM are described (I6 and I8 met), but no stereotactic coordinate tables or explicit coordinate results in Talairach/MNI are present in the supplied content (I7 not met). The supplied full text appears to be incomplete with respect to results/coordinates (fulltext_incomplete=true). Exclusion criteria: none met.

This study meets all inclusion criteria. It is a task-based BOLD fMRI study of a problem-solving task (three-digit addition/subtraction requiring goal-directed, rule-based operations), satisfying I5. It includes group-level whole-brain analyses in healthy adult controls (one-sample t-tests and random-effects analyses), satisfying I6. Results are reported using MNI stereotactic coordinates (I7), and the modality is BOLD fMRI (I8). Voxelwise results and coordinate tables/figures are indicated in the text (I9). The full text includes methods, results, and discussion, so the article appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only (E3), the paper reports healthy-group task effects rather than only group comparisons (E4/E5), and it is empirical human data (not E6). Therefore include.

The study is a task-based whole-brain fMRI investigation reporting Talairach coordinates and BOLD results in both schizophrenic patients and healthy control smokers. However, the experimental task is an auditory n-back working memory/selective attention paradigm, which does not meet the review's definition of a problem-solving task (I5). All other inclusion criteria are satisfied (whole-brain group analyses in healthy adults, stereotactic coordinates reported, and BOLD analysis reported). No exclusion criteria are triggered. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study includes a mental addition task that requires applying arithmetic rules to compute sums, meeting the review's operational definition of problem solving (I5). It reports task-related BOLD fMRI results in healthy adult participants with group-level, whole-brain analyses (transformed into Talairach space) and shows Talairach-group averaged activation maps (I6, I8). The manuscript indicates voxelwise results in standardized Talairach space and presents activation overlays/cluster locations in figures, satisfying the requirement for stereotactic reporting or presentation of voxelwise results (I7, I9). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion; core data and analyses are present, so fulltext_incomplete is false. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adults using the Wason selection task (conditional reasoning/cheater-detection), which qualifies as problem-solving (goal-directed logical evaluation and rule-based operations). It reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses in MNI space with task-related BOLD results (coordinates and tables/figures) and voxelwise contrasts. Methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9, and violates none of the exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study does not meet the primary inclusion criterion I5. Although it is a task-based fMRI study with healthy adult participants and reports whole-brain group-level effects (I6), stereotactic MNI coordinates (I7), and BOLD analyses (I8) — and reporting of voxelwise results is present/acceptable (I9) — the experimental paradigm is a working memory (listening/reading span) task, not a problem-solving task as defined (goal-directed problem solving involving planning/sequencing operations to arrive at a solution). Therefore I5 is not satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3, E4, E5, E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This study does not investigate problem-solving as defined by the review. It is a perceptual detection task manipulating motivation to change response bias, not a task requiring goal-directed problem solving involving planning/sequencing or critical thinking to arrive at a (novel) solution. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (task-based, group-level whole-brain fMRI in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic MNI coordinates), I8 (reports BOLD analysis), I9 (voxelwise results reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (does not examine a problem-solving task as defined). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore exclude on the basis that the core task does not meet the problem-solving definition required by the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that directly examines problem solving: participants learned unsolved technical problems and, during event-related fMRI, judged whether presented heuristic prototypes helped solve those problems (goal-directed problem-solving/insight task). Group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses are reported, with BOLD fMRI data, results given in Talairach stereotactic coordinates (left DLPFC BA9, left AG BA39). Reporting includes voxelwise/cluster-corrected contrasts (RP > UP). Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adults using a syllogistic deductive reasoning task that fits the review’s definition of problem solving (logical operations to reach a conclusion). Methods report whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses (SPM99) with stereotactic normalization to MNI space and coordinate-based results. The study reports BOLD-based fMRI contrasts (reasoning > control) across trial stages and provides tables/figures of activated clusters (coordinates). The sample comprises healthy adult participants and the design and results meet the meta-analysis requirements for whole-brain, voxelwise task effects. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so text is complete and sufficient for data extraction.

This is a task-based fMRI study of theory of mind and attention using story reading, not a problem-solving task as defined by the review (I5 not met). The full text is complete and reports healthy adult participants, whole-brain group analyses (I6), stereotactic coordinates in MNI space (I7), and BOLD analyses (I8). Voxelwise/whole-brain results are reported in tables/figures and supplementary materials (I9). No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study must be excluded because it does not examine problem-solving across domains (fails I5).

This is a task-based PET study in healthy adults that reports whole-brain rCBF analyses with stereotactic coordinates, so it meets I6, I7, I8, and I9. However, the experimental task is a theory-of-mind/mentalizing narrative (imagining why a stranger is crying) rather than a problem-solving task as defined in the review (a goal-directed task requiring evaluation, planning/sequencing, and rule-based operations to reach a solution). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 and must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. The full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This task-based fMRI study in healthy young adults (controls aged 20–26) investigated a complex subtraction task requiring estimation and borrowing, which fits the review definition of problem solving (goal-directed computation, planning/sequencing, rule-based operations). It reports BOLD fMRI whole-brain voxelwise analyses with group-level effects for the healthy control group, uses Talairach standardized space (coordinates reported), and presents voxelwise results in figures/tables. The study also provides region-of-interest analyses but not exclusively. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9) and violates none of the exclusion criteria.

Full text appears incomplete (only abstract/metadata provided). The task used is an N-back verbal working memory task, which does not meet the review's definition of a problem-solving task (I5 not met). From the abstract, the study includes healthy adult volunteers and reports activation maps from PET rCBF data (I6 and I8 met). The abstract does not report stereotactic coordinates (I7 not verifiable) and voxelwise coordinate results are not confirmed in the available content (I9 not verifiable). No exclusion criteria (E3-E6) are clearly met. Because the full text is incomplete and key inclusion criteria (I5, I7, I9) are not satisfied/confirmable, the study is excluded.

Although this is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults with whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses reporting stereotactic coordinates and BOLD results, the experimental tasks (digit identification and symbolic number magnitude comparison) do not meet the review's operational definition of a problem-solving task (I5). The tasks involve simple magnitude judgments and symbol identification rather than goal-directed problem solving that requires evaluating a problem, planning/sequencing actions, or executing rule-based operations to reach a novel or complex solution. Therefore I5 is not satisfied. Inclusion criteria met: I6, I7, I8, I9. Inclusion criteria not met: I5. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

Full text is complete. This is a task-based whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adults that reports group-level effects, stereotactic coordinates (Talairach/MNI), and BOLD analyses. However, the experimental task is a probabilistic guessing/gambling task (predicting card color or suit) with outcomes determined by chance rather than a defined problem requiring planning or executing operations to reach a correct solution. It lacks the core elements of problem solving as specified (goal-directed planning/sequencing to arrive at a correct or previously unknown solution). Therefore I5 (problem-solving task) is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This study does not meet the review's definition of a problem-solving task (I5). Although it is a task-based whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adults and reports stereotactic coordinates and BOLD results, the primary paradigm (occupational choice vs. word-length) probes decision-making/conflict among options and biasing of choices rather than a problem-solving process involving goal-directed planning, sequencing of operations, or deriving a novel correct solution. Therefore I5 is not satisfied. No exclusion criterion from the provided set (E3–E6) applies. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

Full text assessed: study is a task-based whole-brain BOLD fMRI investigation that reports group-level activations for healthy controls (MNI normalization, coordinate tables) and includes BOLD analyses. However, the experimental task (Belief Attribution/false-belief ToM task) probes theory-of-mind/social cognition (inferring beliefs), not a problem-solving task as defined in inclusion criterion I5 (goal-directed problem solving involving planning/sequencing operations within semantic/ logical/algebraic/mechanical rule sets). Therefore I5 is not met. No exclusion criteria are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of conflict, error, and task-switching using a face/body species discrimination task. It meets I6 (whole-brain, group-level fMRI in healthy adults), I7 (reports MNI coordinates), I8 (BOLD analysis), and I9 (voxelwise results reported). It does NOT meet I5: the task is perceptual discrimination and implicit task-switching, not a problem-solving task involving goal-directed planning or critical thinking to generate solutions (e.g., semantic, algebraic, logical problem solving). No exclusion criteria are triggered. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

The study is an fMRI investigation of problem solving using the Tower of London task in 24 healthy adult participants. It reports whole-brain analyses (SPM5 preprocessing, normalization to MNI space), task-related BOLD activations, and stereotactic peak coordinates (MNI) and VOI analyses. The design and analyses address problem-solving processes (internalization and planning), satisfying the review’s definition of problem solving. Group-level voxelwise results are reported and discussed; tables/figures are referenced for coordinates. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text is complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I9 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants that investigates trial-and-error visuomotor sequence learning, which meets the review definition of problem solving (goal-directed sequencing and planning to discover the correct button-order). The study reports whole-brain echo-planar fMRI with group-level analyses across seven healthy adults, provides stereotactic Talairach coordinates (Table 1), and reports task-related BOLD signal changes and voxelwise activation maps and statistics. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion, enabling assessment of brain activation loci. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, non-healthy-only contrasts, between-group-only comparisons, or non-empirical work) apply. Therefore, the study meets inclusion criteria I5–I9 and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

EXCLUDED because the study does not meet key inclusion criteria for this review. Inclusion met: I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates/MNI->Talairach), I8 (task-based BOLD fMRI analysis reported), I9 (voxelwise/whole-brain results reported in main text/analyses). Inclusion not met: I5 (task is an inhibitory control go/no-go task, not a problem-solving task as defined), I6 (participants are children/adolescents and clinical groups; does not include healthy adult individuals). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) were triggered. Full text appears complete. Therefore excluded.

The study is excluded because the experimental task (a forethought/incongruency-detection paradigm requiring yes/no judgments about the plausibility of picture sequences) does not meet the meta-analysis definition of a problem-solving task (I5). The task primarily assesses expectancy/anticipation and recognition of congruency rather than requiring participants to generate plans, sequence actions to reach a goal, or execute operations within a rule set to derive a novel solution. The full text is complete. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (contains whole-brain, group-level analyses including a healthy adult control group), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI space), I8 (task-based BOLD fMRI analyses), and I9 (voxelwise results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (task does not fulfill problem-solving definition).

This study does not investigate problem solving as defined by inclusion criterion I5. While it is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults with whole-brain, group-level analyses reporting stereotactic coordinates and BOLD results, the tasks (coherence discrimination, mental rotation, noun/verb judgment) probe perceptual discrimination, spatial transformation, and semantic classification rather than goal-directed problem-solving involving evaluation, planning/sequencing actions, or executing rule-based operations to reach a novel solution. Therefore I5 is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered by the full text. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group analyses in healthy adults), I7 (stereotactic coordinates reported), I8 (BOLD analysis), I9 (voxelwise results clearly reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (problem-solving task). Exclusion criteria met: none. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The full text is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that reports whole-brain group analyses, stereotactic coordinates (Talairach/MNI), and BOLD results (satisfying I6, I7, I8, I9). However, the experimental task is an auditory n-back verbal working memory task, not a problem-solving task as defined by the review (i.e., tasks requiring goal-directed identification/planning/sequencing to reach a previously unknown solution). Thus inclusion criterion I5 (study of a problem solving task) is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

The study is an empirical whole-brain fMRI investigation that reports group-level BOLD effects with stereotactic coordinates in healthy adults, but the task is a letter-matching task (name vs. physical matching) rather than a problem-solving task as defined by the review (goal-directed planning/sequencing or critical thinking to arrive at a novel solution). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level effects in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates), I8 (BOLD analysis), and I9 (voxelwise results reported/available). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (task-based study of problem solving as defined). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore EXCLUDED because it does not meet the essential problem-solving task criterion (I5).

This is a task-based fMRI study of planning (Tower of London visuospatial planning and an autobiographical planning task) in healthy adult participants. Tower of London clearly meets the meta-analysis definition of problem solving (explicit goal, sequencing of moves under rule constraints to reach a correct solution); the autobiographical planning task involves goal-directed planning and sequencing of steps to reach personal goals. The study reports whole-brain, group-level analyses (spatiotemporal and block PLS), normalizes data to MNI space, and provides stereotactic coordinates for seeds and cluster maxima; it uses BOLD fMRI analyses and reports task-related activity and coordinates (with tables/figures/supplement). It is empirical, not ROI-only, and involves healthy adults. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I9 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that includes whole-brain group analyses (I6) and reports BOLD and ASL (CBF) analyses (I8). However, it does not meet the review’s definition of a problem-solving task (I5): the experimental paradigm is a modified Stroop inhibition/switching task emphasizing interference resolution and task switching, not explicit problem solving (planning/sequencing to arrive at a novel solution) as defined by the meta-analysis. Additionally, the provided full text does not present stereotactic coordinate tables or explicit voxelwise coordinate results in Talairach/MNI space that can be verified (I7 not satisfied). The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study is excluded because it fails to meet inclusion criteria I5 and I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) were triggered.

This is a task-based whole-brain fMRI study of imagined egocentric spatial transformations (hand and perspective rotation). While it meets several technical inclusion criteria (whole-brain group analyses in healthy adults, stereotactic coordinates in MNI space, and BOLD fMRI voxelwise results are reported), it does not meet the review’s conceptual problem-solving definition (I5). The tasks are perceptual/mental-rotation and spatial perspective-taking judgments (left/right decisions about hands/fingers) rather than goal-directed problem solving involving planning/sequencing operations to achieve a novel solution within a rule-based framework. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered.
