This study is an fMRI investigation of perceptual judgments of ‘possible’ vs ‘impossible’ figures (two-pronged trident), not a problem-solving task as defined by the review (no goal-directed planning/sequencing or operations to arrive at a novel solution). Therefore inclusion criterion I5 (task is a problem-solving task) is not met. The paper does meet I6 (whole-brain, group-level fMRI analysis) and I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis). However, stereotactic coordinate results (I7) are not reported in the provided full text, and voxelwise coordinate tables/figures or clear indication of such coordinates (I9) are not present in the supplied content. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Given the lack of a problem-solving paradigm, the study is excluded.

The study is a task-based fMRI experiment in healthy adults and reports whole-brain group analyses and BOLD results (meets I5, I6, I8). However, the provided full text does not report stereotactic coordinates (Talairach or MNI) for task-related activations in the supplied content, and I7 (stereotactic coordinate reporting) is not satisfied. Therefore the study cannot be included. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered in the provided material.

This study does not meet the review’s definition of a problem-solving task (I5). While it is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults with whole-brain, group-level analyses reporting stereotactic coordinates (MNI) and BOLD results (satisfying I6, I7, I8, and I9), the experimental tasks are spatial navigation and memory pointing tasks (SOP and JRD) rather than problem-solving as defined (goal-directed critical thinking, planning/sequencing operations within semantic/algebraic/logical/mechanical rule frameworks to reach an unknown solution). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study with healthy adult controls and whole-brain (MNI-normalized) BOLD analyses (meets I6, I7, I8, I9). However, the tasks used (AX-CPT and color-word Stroop) probe cognitive control/context maintenance and response inhibition rather than problem solving as defined by the review (i.e., having a goal and needing to figure out a way to reach it via evaluation, planning/sequencing actions, and executing operations to arrive at a new or correct solution). Thus inclusion criterion I5 (study of a problem-solving task per the review definition) is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered and the full text appears complete. Conclusion: EXCLUDE because I5 not satisfied; inclusion criteria met: I6, I7, I8, I9; inclusion criterion not met: I5; exclusion criteria applied: [].

The study is an event-related fMRI investigation of semantic property-verification (verifying whether a property belongs to a category). It meets I6 (whole-brain group-level fMRI analysis in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI space), I8 (task-based BOLD fMRI), and I9 (voxelwise results presented in tables/figures). However it does NOT meet I5: the task is a semantic verification/decision task, not a problem-solving task as defined (goal-directed planning/sequencing or execution to arrive at a novel solution). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore the study must be excluded because it fails to satisfy inclusion criterion I5. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Full text is incomplete (only title/abstract provided). From the abstract: task-based event-related fMRI in healthy adults involving attention set shift (likely meets I5) and uses fMRI BOLD (meets I8). However the abstract does not report stereotactic coordinates (I7) nor clearly state whole-brain, voxelwise, group-level coordinate results (I6/I9) that can be verified from available content. Because core full-text methods/results (coordinates, whole-brain analysis confirmation) are missing, unable to confirm all required inclusion criteria, so the study is excluded pending full-text access.

This study does not investigate problem-solving across domains. Tasks are finger flexion (motor) and a 2-back working memory task, which do not meet the review’s definition of problem solving (I5 not met). Although the paper includes group-level whole-brain maps across sessions (satisfying I6), uses BOLD fMRI (I8), and presents voxelwise group maps in figures (I9), it does not report stereotactic coordinate results (Talairach/MNI) for task-related activations in coordinate tables or text (I7 not met). The study’s primary analyses are ROI-based MDC calculations rather than investigations of task-evoked problem-solving activations. No exclusion criteria are triggered. Full text appears complete. Inclusion criteria met: I6, I8, I9. Inclusion criteria not met: I5, I7. Exclusion criteria met: none ([]).

This is a task-based BOLD fMRI study in healthy adults that includes a mental calculation (subtraction) task meeting the review's problem-solving definition (rule-based operations to arrive at a solution). The study reports group-level, voxelwise random-effects analyses (10 healthy adults), normalized to MNI space with peak coordinates and tables, and uses whole-brain voxelwise analysis (within the scanned volume) rather than ROI-only results. BOLD activation results and stereotactic coordinates are reported. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, conclusions) is present. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 and violates no exclusion criteria.

The study is an event-related BOLD fMRI investigation of quantifier comprehension (semantic/language judgment) in healthy young adults. It does not involve a goal-directed problem-solving task as defined (planning, sequencing actions, or executing operations to reach a previously unknown solution). Therefore I5 (problem-solving task) is not met. The study does satisfy I6 (whole-brain group-level effects in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI space), I8 (reports BOLD analyses), and I9 (voxelwise results reported). No exclusion criteria are triggered (none of E3–E6 apply). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Conclusion: EXCLUDE because inclusion criterion I5 is not met; all other applicable inclusion criteria are met.

Excluded because the study reports only ROI-based PET analyses and does not provide whole-brain, voxelwise stereotactic coordinate results required for this review. Exclusion criteria met: E3 (reports only ROI results). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task does not clearly meet the meta-analysis definition of problem-solving; it is probabilistic classification/learning), I6 (no whole-brain group-level voxelwise analysis reported), I7 (no stereotactic coordinates of task-related activations reported), I8 (does not report BOLD or rCBF measures; uses molecular C-raclopride PET binding). Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). Therefore excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI (BOLD) study using the Hayling Sentence Completion Test (a semantic/verbal task that requires goal-directed generation and executive processes consistent with the review’s problem-solving definition). The study reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects SPM analyses including a healthy control group, provides stereotactic coordinates (MNI converted to Talairach), and presents voxelwise results in figures/tables. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so appears complete. Minor note: sample age range includes some participants as young as 16, but the study nevertheless includes a healthy adult control group and group-level whole-brain effects. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria I5–I9 and violates no exclusion criteria.

The study is a whole-brain PET activation study in healthy adult controls and reports voxelwise rCBF coordinates (Talairach) for the verbal fluency (VF) task; thus it meets I6, I7, I8, and I9. However, the primary task is phonological verbal fluency (generate words beginning with a letter), which is a language/lexical retrieval and fluency task rather than a problem-solving task as defined by the review (i.e., tasks requiring evaluation, planning/sequencing of actions to reach a novel or correct solution within a rule-based problem-solving framework). Although VF has a goal and a rule, it lacks critical elements of problem solving such as planning complex action sequences to derive a previously unknown solution and substantive evaluation or sequencing operations characteristic of problem-solving domains. Therefore I5 is not met, and the study is excluded. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I6, I7, I8, I9. Inclusion IDs not met: I5.

This is a task-based fMRI study of problem solving (compound remote associate verbal problems) in healthy young adults. It reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects FMRI analyses and BOLD signal results, including stereotactic Talairach coordinates for clusters (e.g., RH aSTG peak at 44, −9, −9). Voxelwise results are presented in figures and described in the text. The study directly examines problem solving as defined by the review (goal-directed generation of solutions) and meets all imaging and reporting requirements. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided.

Although this study uses whole-brain PET in healthy older adults and reports task-related rCBF stereotactic coordinates, it does not investigate a problem-solving task as defined by the review (I5). The experimental task is a perceptual visual categorization of ellipses (classifying shapes as 'thin' or 'wide'), which involves perceptual discrimination and decision-making but lacks essential problem-solving components such as forming a goal to reach a novel solution, planning or sequencing actions, or applying operations to derive a previously unknown correct solution. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level PET in healthy adults), I7 (Talairach coordinates reported), I8 (rCBF analysis), I9 (voxelwise results available). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task is not a problem-solving task per the review definition). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study investigates task-switching/executive control, not problem-solving as defined by I5 (planning/sequencing operations to reach a solution across domains). While it reports whole-brain group-level fMRI results (I6), uses stereotactic labeling/standard space (Talairach/MNI) and cluster labeling implying coordinates (I7), reports BOLD fMRI analyses (I8), and indicates voxelwise results are available in figures/tables (I9), it does not meet the meta-analysis’s problem-solving task definition (I5). No exclusion criteria are triggered. Therefore excluded.

This fMRI study does not meet the review's definition of a problem-solving task (I5). The experimental task was a one-back relational judgment directing attention to spatial, temporal, or causal relations between identical short sentences; the authors explicitly state there were no explicit correct answers for individual trials and the task did not require planning, sequencing actions, or generating/implementing solutions to reach a goal. Thus I5 is not satisfied. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion (fulltext_incomplete=false). Other inclusion criteria are met: whole-brain group-level analyses in healthy adults (I6); stereotactic coordinate reporting in standardized space (I7); BOLD fMRI analyses (I8); voxelwise results presented in tables/figures (I9). No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore exclude because it does not study problem-solving per the review definition (I5 not met).

The provided 'full text' contains only the References section and lacks core article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore I cannot verify whether the study meets the review's inclusion criteria. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (cannot confirm the task meets the problem-solving definition), I6 (cannot confirm whole-brain, group-level analyses in healthy adults), I7 (cannot confirm stereotactic coordinates reported), I8 (cannot confirm BOLD or rCBF analysis reported), I9 (cannot confirm voxelwise results/tables/figures are available). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) can be established from the truncated content. Because the full text is incomplete, the study must be excluded from the review until a complete article is provided.

This study is an fMRI investigation of mental rotation (visuo-spatial transformation) in healthy adults. It meets I6 (whole-brain group-level fMRI in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates in standardized space), I8 (reports BOLD fMRI analyses), and I9 (voxelwise results described). However, it does not meet I5: the task is a perceptual mental rotation / same-different discrimination and does not clearly constitute a problem-solving task as defined (goal-directed planning, sequencing or execution of operations within a rule-based framework to arrive at a novel solution). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore I exclude due to failure to satisfy I5.

This is a methodological/denoising paper using ICA on fMRI data collected during category learning tasks. Inclusion: I6 (whole-brain group-level analyses in healthy adults) — met; I8 (BOLD analysis) — met. Exclusion: The study does not investigate problem solving as defined by the review (I5). The tasks are category learning/learning paradigms rather than goal-directed problem-solving (planning/sequencing operations to reach a solution). Additionally, the provided full text does not present stereotactic coordinate tables (I7) in the supplied content, so I7 is not clearly satisfied. No exclusion criteria E3–E6 apply. Therefore the paper does not meet all required inclusion criteria (notably I5) and is excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults performing a problem-solving task (mental arithmetic/repeated subtraction). The study performed whole-brain, voxel-wise group analyses (SPM99 normalization to MNI space) and reported BOLD effects associated with task-related contrasts and phase-synchronization regressors; at least one stereotactic coordinate is reported in the text ([−42, −10, 42]) and anatomical activation maps/figures are described. All required imaging outcomes (BOLD) and group-level whole-brain results are present. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for problem-solving fMRI studies in healthy adults.

Excluded because the study does not address the review objective of problem-solving in healthy adults. Inclusion criteria met: I8 (task-based fMRI reporting BOLD activation). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (the task is a Go/NoGo response-inhibition paradigm, not a problem-solving task as defined), I6 (sample comprises ages 8–20, i.e., children/adolescents and young adults — not a healthy adult-only group). I7 (stereotactic coordinates are not clearly reported in the provided text). Exclusion criteria met: none (E3/E4/E5/E6 do not apply). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study is ineligible for inclusion in this meta-analysis.

Although this is an empirical, whole-brain task-based fMRI study reporting BOLD results in MNI space for healthy adult participants, the experimental task centers on moral reasoning (social-ethical and individual gain vs collective loss dilemmas) and investigations of empathy/Theory of Mind. The study does not target problem-solving as defined by the review (a goal-directed problem requiring planning/sequencing or applying explicit rule-based operations to arrive at a correct/novel solution across domains). Therefore inclusion criterion I5 is not met, so the study is excluded. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study used N-back (working memory) and verbal fluency tasks in mixed groups (at-risk, psychosis, controls). While it includes healthy adult controls and reports whole-brain, group-level BOLD fMRI analyses transformed into Talairach space (with cluster/voxel results and tables referenced), the tasks do not meet the meta-analysis definition of a problem-solving task (goal-directed planning/sequencing and execution to arrive at a solution within semantic, algebraic, logical, mechanical or similar rule frameworks). Therefore inclusion criterion I5 is not satisfied, so the study must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered.

Full text is complete and describes a task-based BOLD fMRI study in healthy adults that examines sequencing/planning of actions (script and sentence ordering). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task involves planning/sequencing/evaluation of action order), I6 (whole-brain data were acquired and group-level effects are reported across subjects), and I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis reported). However, the paper does NOT report task-related activations as stereotactic coordinates in Talairach or MNI space (no tables or coordinates provided), so I7 is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Because all inclusion criteria must be satisfied and I7 is unmet, the study must be excluded.

The study is a task-based BOLD fMRI experiment in healthy adults (n=16) that requires participants to infer and apply syntactic rules to classify symbol strings — a goal-directed rule-inference and application task matching the review's problem-solving definition (evaluating patterns, planning/sequence application, executing rule-based judgments). It reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with results in MNI stereotactic coordinates, and uses BOLD fMRI contrasts (including parametric modulations). No exclusion criteria are met: analyses are whole-brain (not ROI-only), involve healthy-group task effects, and the full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

Although the study meets imaging and reporting criteria (whole-brain group fMRI with BOLD analyses, stereotactic coordinates, and coordinate reporting), it does not investigate a problem-solving task as defined by the review. The task is a probability learning and decision-making/gambling paradigm focused on learning event probabilities and making value-based choices under uncertainty, not on problem solving that requires goal-directed planning, sequencing of actions, or execution of rule-based operations to find a novel solution. Therefore inclusion criterion I5 is not satisfied. Inclusion criteria met: I6, I7, I8, I9. Inclusion criterion not met: I5. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

Full text incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). Abstract indicates a task-based PET study of deductive reasoning in human subjects, suggesting I5 (problem-solving/deductive task), I6 (group-level PET comparison in healthy adults), and I8 (PET/rCBF) are likely met. However, the provided content does not report stereotactic coordinates or confirm whole-brain voxelwise results in standardized (Talairach/MNI) space (I7 not verifiable). Because key inclusion criterion I7 cannot be confirmed from the incomplete full text, and core methods/results are missing, the study is excluded pending access to the full article. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I8. Inclusion criteria not met/uncertain: I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are clearly met based on the available information.

This study uses a task (Wisconsin Word Sorting Task) that requires subjects to discover and apply classification rules by trial-and-error, involving goal-directed rule identification, planning/set-shifting, and execution—consistent with the review’s definition of problem solving (I5). It is a task-based BOLD fMRI study in healthy adults (n=14) with group-level mixed-effects whole-brain analyses (I6, I8). The authors report voxelwise activation peaks normalized to stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) and indicate peaks/tables (I7); whole-brain results are described in text and tables (I9). The full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text is complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, patient-only contrasts, non-empirical) are met.

Study includes a rule-based reverse-alphabetizing task that requires goal-directed ordering/sequencing (meets I5). It is a task-based fMRI study reporting group-level, whole-brain analyses in healthy adults (meets I6). Images were normalized to Talairach space and task-related activations are reported as coordinates (meets I7 and I9). Analyses are BOLD-based (meets I8). Full article contains introduction, methods, results and discussion (fulltext complete). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not patient-group-only, not non-empirical). Sample size is small for fMRI (n=8 scanned), but group whole-brain BOLD results are reported, so inclusion criteria are satisfied.

This task-based PET study examines a verbal mental-operation task in healthy adults using whole-brain H2(15)O rCBF and SPM analyses. The MO-v task requires a clear goal and rule-based, sequential mental operations (advancing the day of the week according to numeric cues), satisfying the review's definition of problem solving (I5). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses in healthy control participants (I6), uses standard stereotactic normalization (MNI/Talairach) and reports coordinate results in tables/figures (I7), and provides rCBF (PET) voxelwise results (I8). Voxelwise results are available in text/tables/figures (I9). No exclusion criteria apply: the study is not ROI-only (E3), does include healthy-group task effects rather than only between-group contrasts (E5), and is empirical (not a review; E6). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I5. The task is a two-choice decision-making (risk/reward) wheel-of-fortune paradigm, which involves choice selection and reward anticipation but not a problem-solving task as defined (i.e., it does not require identifying and/or performing multi-step critical thinking, planning or sequencing operations to reach a correct or previously unknown solution). The full text is complete and the study does satisfy other inclusion criteria: I6 (whole-brain group-level fMRI in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI space), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), and I9 (voxelwise results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete.

The study is a task-based, whole-brain fMRI investigation in healthy adults (N=20) reporting MNI coordinates and BOLD-related activation maps. However, the cognitive task probes event simulation, situational inference, and future prediction—not a goal-directed problem-solving paradigm as defined (no requirement to identify/plan/execute operations to reach a novel solution within semantic/algebraic/logical/mechanical rule sets). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group fMRI in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI space), I8 (BOLD analysis), I9 (voxelwise results available). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete. Hence excluded due to not meeting I5.

This is a methods/empirical fMRI paper developing and validating a sparse paradigm-free mapping (SPFM) approach and demonstrating it on a visuomotor finger-tapping task. It does not investigate problem-solving: the task is sensorimotor finger tapping rather than goal-directed problem solving (I5 not met). Although the study reports BOLD voxelwise maps and figures (meets I8 and I9), it does not present a whole-brain group-level task effect in healthy adults (analyses are per-subject and small-N individual datasets; I6 not met). There is no clear reporting of stereotactic coordinates for task-related increases in standard space in the provided text (I7 not met). Therefore it does not satisfy all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and is excluded.

This is a whole-brain PET study with healthy adult controls that reports Talairach coordinates and rCBF results (meets I6, I7, I8, I9). However, the experimental task (modified word-stem completion prompting evaluative judgments of ambivalent emotional stimuli) is an emotional evaluative/conflict-resolution task, not a goal-directed problem-solving task as defined by I5 (no evidence of planning/sequencing actions or executing rule-based operations to reach a solution). Therefore I5 is not met and the study does not address the review’s problem-solving objective. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Although this study uses task-based fMRI with whole-brain group analyses in healthy adult controls and reports stereotactic coordinates and BOLD-related results (meets I6, I7, I8, I9), the experimental paradigm is a two-choice probabilistic decision-making/feedback task coupled with an aversive interoceptive breathing load. This does not meet the review's definition of a problem-solving task (I5) which requires goal-directed evaluation, planning/sequencing of actions, and execution within a rule-set to arrive at a (sometimes novel) solution. Therefore I5 is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This study uses a mental rotation (visuospatial congruency) task rather than a task that clearly meets the review's definition of problem solving (I5). Although it reports whole-brain, group-level fMRI BOLD results with stereotactic normalization and coordinate tables, it does not provide evidence that the task entails goal-directed problem-solving processes (evaluation, planning/sequencing, rule-based solution generation) across domains. Inclusion criteria met: I7 (Talairach normalization and coordinate reporting), I8 (task-based BOLD fMRI), I9 (voxelwise results available in text/figures/tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task is mental rotation/visuospatial discrimination, not clearly a problem-solving task per the review definition), I6 (no clear whole-brain group-level task effect reported for healthy adults alone — results are reported for the combined group and patient vs control comparisons, not a controls-only whole-brain activation map). No exclusion criteria from the list (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

Full text presents a PET study of visual working memory and associative learning in healthy adults. It meets inclusion criteria I6 (whole-brain, group-level PET analysis in healthy adults), I7 (reports Talairach coordinates), I8 (reports rCBF PET analyses), and I9 (voxelwise results reported). It does NOT meet I5: the tasks are working memory and conditional associative learning paradigms (remembering position/shape and retrieving learned colour-response mappings), not problem-solving as defined (goal-directed planning/critical thinking/sequencing to find novel solutions). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore EXCLUDE because I5 is not satisfied.

Full text is complete. Exclusion decision because the study does not meet the meta-analysis problem-solving task definition (I5). The Semantic Object Retrieval Task (SORT) requires semantic association judgments (whether word pairs evoke a third object) and indexes semantic retrieval/association, not the goal-directed problem-solving processes defined in I5 (evaluating a problem, planning/sequencing actions, executing operations within a rule set to reach a novel solution). The study does meet other inclusion criteria: I6 (includes whole-brain group-level fMRI analyses including healthy adult controls), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI space: e.g., left IPL −51, −48, 51; right IPL 45, −60, 54), I8 (task-based BOLD fMRI used), and I9 (voxelwise results/coordinates reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Therefore EXCLUDED because inclusion criterion I5 is not satisfied.

This study is excluded because it does not meet the review’s definition of a problem-solving task (I5). It reports an fMRI stop-signal (response inhibition) paradigm, not a task requiring goal-directed problem solving/planning or applying rule-based operations to arrive at novel solutions. Although the study includes BOLD-based analyses (I8 satisfied) and group data from healthy adults, the analyses are ROI-based connectivity/BN modeling limited to four predefined ROIs and do not present whole-brain, voxelwise task activation results with stereotactic coordinates (violates I6 and I7). This meets exclusion criterion E3 (reports only ROI results). Inclusion criteria met: I8. Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (problem-solving task), I6 (whole-brain group-level analysis), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates), I9 (not applicable because no whole-brain voxelwise coordinates reported). Full text appears complete for screening purposes (methods, results, discussion present).

This is a task-based fMRI study in 40 healthy adults that reports whole-brain, group-level BOLD results with stereotactic (MNI) coordinates and coordinate tables. However, the experimental paradigm is an auditory dichotic listening task probing cognitive control/conflict and attentional selection, not a problem-solving task as defined by the review (goal-directed operations requiring planning/sequencing or evaluating to reach a previously unknown solution). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5. No exclusion criteria are met.

Although this is an empirical whole-brain PET study in healthy adults reporting task-related rCBF coordinates, it does not examine a problem-solving task as defined in the review. The task used is a delayed non-match-to-sample (DNMTS) working memory/recognition task measuring memory load, RT and accuracy; it does not require goal-directed problem solving, planning/sequencing, or execution of operations within a rule-based framework to reach a novel solution. Therefore inclusion criterion I5 (study of a problem-solving task as defined) is not met. The full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study reports whole-brain, task-based BOLD fMRI in healthy adult participants performing a probabilistic reversal learning task. The task requires subjects to detect changes in stimulus–reward contingencies, evaluate feedback, adjust strategy, and execute rule-based responses—meeting the review’s problem-solving definition (goal-directed evaluation, planning/sequencing, and rule-based execution). The paper presents group-level whole-brain analyses, voxelwise ICC and activation results, and reports stereotactic MNI coordinates for task-related increases. Voxelwise results and coordinates are available in figures/tables. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text is complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, includes healthy-group task effects, is empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and is suitable for inclusion.

The experimental paradigm is a parametric mental image scanning (spatial imagery) task, not a problem-solving task as defined by I5 (goal-directed search requiring evaluation, planning/sequencing of actions or rule-based operations to arrive at a solution). The study does meet other inclusion criteria: whole-brain group-level fMRI analyses in healthy adults (I6); results reported in standardized stereotactic space (Talairach/MNI) (I7); reports BOLD fMRI analyses (I8); and voxelwise results are indicated via tables/figures (I9). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) appear to apply. Therefore, exclude because I5 is not satisfied.

This fMRI study used a virtual radial arm maze (RAM) involving goal-directed navigation and working memory, but it does not meet the review’s required criteria for inclusion. Exclusion criteria met: E3 — analyses are ROI-based: the Methods and Results describe analyses performed on predefined ROIs (Harvard-Oxford masks and other region masks) and multivariate statistics per ROI; no whole-brain voxelwise, group-level activation maps or peak coordinates for task-related activations are reported. Inclusion criteria met: I8 — BOLD (fMRI) analyses are reported. Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task is framed as working memory/decision-making rather than an explicit problem-solving task as defined by the review), I6 (no whole-brain group-level voxelwise analysis reported), I7 (no stereotactic peak coordinates in Talairach/MNI for task-related activations are provided), I9 (no voxelwise coordinate results or activation tables/figures of whole-brain effects are provided). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore exclude.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that investigates learning, encoding, and execution of multi-rule tasks. The experimental paradigm requires participants to encode instructed rule sets and to apply them to make decisions (e.g., B2 two-choice judgments), which fits the review's operational definition of problem solving as execution of operations conforming to rule sets to reach correct responses. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level analyses, provides stereotactic (MNI) coordinates for activations, and is based on BOLD fMRI data. All required Inclusion criteria (I5–I9) are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply (e.g., results are not ROI-only, the sample is healthy adults, empirical task effects are reported). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

The study is an empirical, task-based fMRI (BOLD) whole-brain investigation in healthy adults that reports group-level effects with stereotactic (MNI) coordinates (meets I6, I7, I8, I9). However, the experimental task is a semantic feature judgment (deciding whether two object names share a color or shape), which is a semantic retrieval/evaluation task and does not satisfy the review's definition of a problem-solving task requiring a goal-directed process of figuring out how to reach a solution via planning/sequencing or executing operations to arrive at a novel or rule-based solution (I5 not met). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

Excluded: The study is a task-based fMRI experiment in healthy adults and reports whole-brain BOLD analyses with voxelwise results referenced in supplementary tables/figures (meets I6, I8, I9). However, the experimental task is a perceptual estimation task (estimating number of dots) with monetary feedback and social comparison; it does not meet the review's definition of a problem-solving task that involves goal-directed planning/sequencing or execution of operations to reach a solution (I5 not met). Additionally, the provided full text does not explicitly present stereotactic coordinates in MNI/Talairach space within the main text (I7 not met based on provided content). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an empirical, whole-brain task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that reports BOLD results with stereotactic (MNI) coordinates, but it does NOT investigate a problem-solving task as defined by the review. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level effects in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI), I8 (reports BOLD analysis), I9 (coordinates reported in main text/figures). Inclusion criterion NOT met: I5 (task is an emotional vs. non-emotional interference/attention Stroop-like paradigm using face-word congruency, not a problem-solving task involving goal-directed planning/sequencing to reach a previously unknown solution). No exclusion criteria apply (E3,E4,E5,E6 not met). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore exclude on the basis of failing I5.

Excluded because the study does not meet key inclusion criteria for this meta-analysis. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level analyses across healthy adults using 1000 cortical ROIs) and I8 (BOLD fMRI data reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task is a semantic decision / categorization task — deciding abstract vs. concrete words — which does not clearly meet this review's operational definition of a problem-solving task involving planning/sequencing or operations to arrive at a novel solution), and I7 (no stereotactic coordinates in Talairach/MNI space for task-related activations or increases are reported). Exclusion criteria met: E3 (results are reported in an ROI/parcellation and graph-theory metric framework rather than voxelwise stereotactic coordinate activations; no coordinate tables/voxelwise peaks provided). Full text appears complete. Therefore the paper is excluded.

Full text is complete. The study performed whole-brain, task-based fMRI and reports group-level effects in healthy seronegative adults and HIV patients, provides stereotactic coordinate results and BOLD analyses. Therefore it satisfies I6, I7, I8, and I9. However, the experimental task is a visual multiple-object tracking attention paradigm (tracking 2–4 balls) and does not meet the review's definition of a problem-solving task (no goal-directed critical evaluation, planning/sequencing actions to derive a novel solution or execute operations within a rule-based framework). Thus I5 is not met. No exclusion criteria from the list apply. Based on this, the study must be excluded because it does not study problem-solving as defined in I5.

The study is an empirical task-based fMRI investigation in healthy adults using the Beauty Contest game, which is a goal-directed, rule-based task requiring subjects to reason, plan, and execute choices to win (meets the review’s definition of problem solving). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses (n=20) in healthy adults, provides stereotactic (MNI) coordinates for activations, and uses BOLD fMRI analyses. Voxelwise results and figures/tables of activation are reported. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria are met.

The study does not investigate a problem-solving task as defined (I5 not met). It examines spontaneous thought and offline memory reprocessing (resting-state and memory-recall fMRI), not goal-directed problem solving involving planning/sequencing operations to reach a solution. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level analyses in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI space), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), I9 (voxelwise/coordinate results reported). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete. Therefore excluded because it fails to meet I5 (problem-solving task).

This study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I5: the tasks are spatial learning/navigation and memory encoding/retrieval (virtual maze, viewpoint shift, path integration) rather than explicit problem-solving as defined (goal-directed planning/sequencing and execution of rule-based operations to arrive at a novel solution). It does meet I6 (whole-brain group-level fMRI analyses in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates in standardized space), I8 (BOLD fMRI analyses), and I9 (voxelwise results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This study does not investigate a problem-solving task as defined by the review. Participants passively watched videos and made button presses to indicate change points (event segmentation/attention/vigilance), which does not constitute goal-driven problem solving involving planning, sequencing actions, or applying rule-based operations to arrive at a solution. The paper does include whole-brain group-level fMRI analyses (registered to Talairach), reports BOLD-based results, and presents voxelwise results in figures/region lists, but it does not report task-related stereotactic coordinates within the provided full text. Therefore inclusion criteria I6, I8, and I9 are met; inclusion criteria I5 (problem-solving task) and I7 (explicit stereotactic coordinate reporting) are not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

Although this is an empirical, whole-brain BOLD fMRI study in healthy adult participants that reports stereotactic coordinates (MNI) and group-level effects, it does NOT investigate a problem-solving task as defined by the review. The concurrent task is an RSVP target-detection attention task (easy vs. hard) requiring perceptual detection and response selection, not a problem-solving paradigm involving setting a goal and devising/planning/ sequencing operations to reach a previously unknown solution (I5 not met). Inclusion criteria met: I6, I7, I8, I9. No exclusion criteria apply. Therefore the study must be excluded because it fails I5 (task definition). Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adults that reports Talairach coordinates and BOLD effects, but the experimental task is semantic true/false judgment (semantic memory retrieval), not a problem-solving task as defined in inclusion criterion I5 (goal-directed planning/sequencing/executing operations to arrive at a solution). Full text is complete. Therefore the study fails to meet I5 and must be excluded.

This is an empirical, task-based whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adults (N=16) using an arithmetic verification task that requires goal-directed computation/verification using algebraic rules (mental calculation and evaluation of correctness). The study performed group-level random-effects, whole-brain analyses (SPM99) with normalization to Talairach space, reports BOLD-based activation maps and stereotactic results (tables/figures), and thus satisfies the meta-analysis requirements. Full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so full text appears complete.

The task is a free word association/inhibition paradigm in a mixed sample (patients + healthy controls) and does not meet the review's definition of a problem-solving task (I5). The study examines semantic association and inhibitory control and lacks goal-directed planning/sequencing or operations to arrive at a correct solution as required for problem-solving. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level fMRI effects including healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI space), I8 (task-related BOLD fMRI analysis), I9 (voxelwise results reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (task is not a problem-solving task per the meta-analysis definition). No exclusion criteria were triggered. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

The study does not meet I5 (problem-solving task). The task is a semantic living/nonliving categorization (easy vs. ambiguous words). Although the ambiguous condition requires more deliberation, it is a classification/judgment task rather than a problem-solving task as defined (no requirement to plan, sequence actions, or generate/execute rules to reach a novel solution). The study does meet other inclusion criteria: I6 (whole-brain group-level fMRI analyses in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI space), I8 (BOLD fMRI results), and I9 (voxelwise results reported/available). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Thus excluded because it fails I5 while meeting I6–I9.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants that examines rule-based quantitative reasoning (perimeter comparison) requiring subjects to override an intuitive heuristic (area) — a goal-directed cognitive task involving evaluation and inhibitory control consistent with problem-solving as defined. The study reports group-level whole-brain analyses (second-level ANOVA) using SPM2, BOLD fMRI acquisition, and provides stereotactic coordinates (MNI normalization) for task-related activations. Voxelwise results are presented in the text/tables. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete.

This study reports BOLD-fMRI investigations using an n-back working memory paradigm in healthy adults and patients with schizophrenia. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (provides whole-brain group-level analyses in healthy adult participants) and I8 (reports BOLD fMRI analyses). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (the task is an n-back working-memory/update task, which does not meet the review’s definition of a problem-solving task involving goal-directed planning/sequencing/critical-thinking to arrive at a novel solution), I7 (the full text does not present stereotactic coordinate tables in Talairach or MNI space in the provided content), and I9 (no explicit voxelwise coordinate tables or supplement clearly reporting stereotactic coordinates are provided in the full text excerpt). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete for screening. Therefore the paper is excluded because it does not study a problem-solving task as defined by the review.

The study is excluded because it does not meet key inclusion criteria for this meta-analysis. It does study a problem-solving-like task (virtual maze) with whole-brain stereotactic coordinate reporting (I5, I7) and the reporting format is acceptable (I9). However, participants are regular marijuana users meeting DSM-IV criteria for dependence (i.e., not a healthy adult sample), so I6 (healthy adult group-level effects) is not met. The imaging modality is FDG PET measuring regional cerebral metabolic rate of glucose (rCMRglc), not BOLD fMRI or regional cerebral blood flow (rCBF), so I8 is not met. Because it lacks a healthy adult task effect/population relevant to the review, exclusion criterion E5 applies (doesn’t include any healthy-group task effect). Full text appears complete. Therefore the paper must be excluded.

The study uses a passive speech comprehension fMRI task (forward vs backward narratives) rather than a problem-solving task involving goal-directed planning, evaluation, sequencing or execution to reach a solution. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5. It does, however, meet other methodological criteria: whole-brain group-level fMRI analyses in healthy adult participants (I6), reports stereotactic coordinates (I7), reports BOLD analyses (I8), and allows voxelwise/coordinate reporting (I9). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Given the focus on language comprehension rather than problem solving, the study is excluded from this meta-analysis.

The study is EXCLUDED because it does not meet I5 (does not investigate a problem-solving task as defined). Although it is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults with whole-brain, group-level analyses reporting BOLD results and stereotactic (MNI) coordinates, the experimental task required participants to judge whether behavior was communicative or strategic (evaluative judgment), not to formulate, plan, or execute actions to reach a goal or solve a specified problem via rule-based operations. Full text is complete; no exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met.

The study reports a task-based BOLD fMRI experiment using the Paced Visual Serial Addition Test (PVSAT), which requires applying an arithmetic rule (adding consecutive digits) to reach correct responses and thus meets the review’s definition of a problem-solving task. It includes healthy adult controls and presents whole-brain, group-level task activation maps (one-sample t-tests in controls and between-group analyses), with activation peak coordinates summarized after normalization to standard space (MNI). Resting-state and task BOLD analyses are reported using whole-brain voxelwise statistics (FWE-corrected). Therefore inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only results, lack of healthy task effect, non-empirical paper) are met. Full text is complete for screening.

Study reports a task-based fMRI experiment (Experiment 2) using a compound remote-associates problem-solving task in healthy adults. It includes group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses of BOLD signal during preparatory intervals, reports cluster-wise task-related effects and references a Table (Table 1) listing voxelwise cluster results (i.e., stereotactic results available), and thus meets criteria for whole-brain, task-based fMRI problem-solving studies. Core sections (methods, results, discussion) are present in the provided full text. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, disease/age/gender-only comparisons, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) apply.

The study is an fMRI investigation of semantic ambiguity resolution (homonym association judgments), not a problem-solving task as defined by the review. While it includes a clear group-level whole-brain BOLD analysis with stereotactic coordinates in healthy adults (meets I6, I7, I8, I9) and the full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion), it does not satisfy the meta-analysis definition of problem solving (I5). The task requires semantic association judgments rather than goal-directed problem solving that involves evaluating the problem, planning/sequencing actions, or deriving previously unknown solutions. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Therefore the study is excluded for failing to meet I5.

This study was excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I5: the task is a prototype-distortion category-learning/perceptual classification paradigm rather than a goal-directed problem-solving task as defined (planning/sequencing operations to reach a solution or applying critical thinking to solve novel problems). It does meet the other inclusion criteria: I6 (whole-brain, group-level fMRI in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic MNI coordinates), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), and I9 (voxelwise results reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) were triggered. Full text appears complete.

This study does not meet the meta-analysis definition of a problem-solving task (I5). The 6-armed bandit task is a reinforcement-learning/explore–exploit decision-making paradigm aimed at maximizing rewards through learning and choice under uncertainty, but it does not explicitly require the kinds of goal-directed problem solving operationalized in I5 (evaluating a problem, planning/sequencing rule-based operations to arrive at a correct or novel solution across semantic/algebraic/logical/mechanical frameworks). The paper does meet whole-brain, group-level fMRI analysis (I6) and reports BOLD-based results (I8). However, the provided full text does not include stereotactic coordinate tables or explicit MNI/Talairach coordinates in the excerpt (I7 not satisfied from the supplied content). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants (n=28) using BOLD fMRI and whole-brain random-effects analyses. Tasks (complex multiplication and figural-spatial face-counting) meet the review’s definition of problem solving (goal-directed operations, rule-based computation or spatial reasoning to arrive at solutions). The paper reports group-level whole-brain results with voxelwise FWE-corrected clusters and stereotactic coordinates in MNI space, and includes BOLD analyses. ROI analyses are supplemental to whole-brain results. The full text provided includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and References, so fulltext appears complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only reporting, patient-only groups, non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I5–I9 and is appropriate for inclusion.

The study is an fMRI investigation of decision-making (Iowa Gambling Task) in Parkinson’s patients and controls. Inclusion criteria met: I7 (data were normalized to MNI space and stereotactic coordinates/seed coordinates are reported), I8 (reports BOLD fMRI analyses), I9 (voxelwise results/coordinates and figures are indicated). Exclusion criterion met: E5 (the paper’s reported neuroimaging results focus on between-group contrasts (PD vs controls) and emphasize differences in PD relative to controls; the manuscript does not provide clear whole-brain, group-level task effect coordinates for the healthy control group alone in the provided text). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (the IGT is a decision-making/reinforcement task and does not clearly meet the review’s defined problem-solving task definition), and I6 (no clear whole-brain group-level task effect reported specifically for healthy adults in the provided results). Full text appears complete for screening.

Full text appears incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group PET results reported in healthy subjects) and I8 (PET provides rCBF-related task analysis). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task is an inhibition/Hayling task, not a clear problem-solving task as defined), I7 (no stereotactic coordinates reported in the available content), I9 (no indication that voxelwise coordinate results are provided in tables/figures). Exclusion criteria met: none (no evidence of ROI-only reporting, only between-group contrasts, disease-only comparisons, or non-empirical article). Because the full text is incomplete and key information to verify problem-solving characterization and coordinate reporting is missing, the study is excluded from this review at this stage.

This is a task-based, whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adults that reports Talairach coordinates and BOLD analyses, but the cognitive task (MSIT) probes attention/conflict and executive control rather than the type of problem-solving defined in inclusion criterion I5 (planning, sequencing, or generating solutions to reach a goal or previously unknown solution). Thus I5 is not met. Inclusion criteria met: I6, I7, I8, I9. Inclusion criterion not met: I5. No exclusion criteria applied (none met). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This PET study reports whole-brain rCBF analyses in a group of healthy adult participants with stereotactic coordinates (MNI) and voxelwise results (fulfilling I6, I7, I8, I9). However, the experimental task is a stochastic two-alternative decision-making/gambling task examining exploration vs. exploitation, sympathetic activity, and neural correlates. It does not meet the review's definition of a problem-solving task (I5) — it lacks an explicit goal-directed problem-solving paradigm requiring planning/sequencing or executing operations within a formal rule set to derive a correct or novel solution (e.g., semantic, algebraic, logical, mechanical puzzles). Therefore it fails to satisfy all inclusion criteria and must be excluded. Full text appears complete.

While this is a task-based, whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adults that reports stereotactic coordinates and BOLD results (meets I6, I7, I8, and I9), the experimental tasks (mental rotation, imagined perspective-taking, object manipulation) investigate spatial transformation and embodiment processes rather than problem-solving as defined by the review (goal-directed problem solving involving evaluation, planning/sequencing actions, and executing rule-based operations to reach a previously unknown solution). Therefore it does not meet I5 and must be excluded. Full text appears complete.

Excluded because the task is a Flanker selective-attention/inhibitory control task, not a problem-solving task as defined by I5 (no goal-directed multi-step problem solving, planning, or execution to arrive at a novel solution). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level fMRI analyses in healthy adult participants) and I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task does not meet the review's definition of problem solving) and I7 (stereotactic coordinates in Talairach/MNI are not provided in the provided full text content; while clusters/regions are reported, explicit coordinates/tables are not evident in the supplied text). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply based on the provided full text. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study does not satisfy all required inclusion criteria and should be excluded.

This is a task-based, whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adults that reports group-level BOLD results with stereotactic coordinates (MNI) and voxelwise analyses. However, the experimental tasks are classification/decision-rule tasks (forced-choice, same-different, independent-classification) addressing criterial classification and selection processes, not goal-directed problem solving that requires planning, sequencing, or deriving a novel solution. Therefore it does not meet inclusion criterion I5. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level analyses), I7 (stereotactic coordinates reported), I8 (BOLD fMRI analyses), I9 (voxelwise results reported). No exclusion criteria are triggered. Conclusion: EXCLUDE because I5 (problem-solving task) is not satisfied.

This study does not meet the review's definition of a problem-solving task (I5). The mental clock task is a spatial mental imagery and angle-comparison judgment; it manipulates perceptual/metric difficulty (symbolic distance effect) but does not require planning, sequencing, or evaluation to generate a novel solution or reach a goal via problem-solving processes as defined by the meta-analysis. The full text is complete and the study meets other neuroimaging criteria (whole-brain group-level fMRI, Talairach coordinates, BOLD analyses). Therefore it is excluded for not meeting I5.

This study is a task-based, whole-brain fMRI investigation in healthy adults reporting BOLD group-level effects in stereotactic space; however, the experimental paradigm examines probabilistic prediction/uncertainty and feedback-based learning rather than a problem-solving task as defined by the review (i.e., having an explicit goal and requiring planning/sequencing or rule-based operations to reach a previously unknown solution). Therefore inclusion criterion I5 (problem-solving task) is not met. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level effects in healthy adults), I7 (stereotactic coordinates/standard space reporting), I8 (BOLD analysis), and I9 (voxelwise results reported/indicated). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Conclusion: EXCLUDED because I5 not satisfied.

This is a task-based 15O-PET study in healthy adults that reports group-level whole-brain rCBF analyses (meets I6 and I8). However, the task is a stochastic reversal learning/decision-making paradigm focused on exploration/exploitation rather than a problem-solving task as defined in I5 (no evidence of explicit goal-directed problem solving requiring planning/sequencing to reach a novel solution). Additionally, the provided full text does not present stereotactic coordinate tables or explicit Talairach/MNI coordinates for reported activations (I7 not satisfied based on the text provided). Therefore it does not meet all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This study is excluded because it does not investigate a problem-solving task as defined by the review (I5). The fMRI and behavioural tasks used (Rapid Visual Information Processing, Inspection Time, and Serial Threes/Sevens arithmetic/attentional tasks) assess sustained attention, early perceptual discrimination, working memory and simple arithmetic speed, but do not require goal-directed planning, sequencing of actions, or execution of operations to discover previously unknown solutions in the sense of problem solving across domains. The paper does meet other neuroimaging inclusion criteria: it includes whole-brain, group-level fMRI analyses in healthy adults (I6), reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI space (I7), reports BOLD analyses (I8), and provides voxelwise results/figures (I9). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results and discussion.

This task-based fMRI study uses the Tower of London planning/problem-solving paradigm (meets I5). It reports whole-brain, voxelwise seed-based connectivity analyses and second-level group contrasts (difficult>easy) across participants including a healthy control group, yielding group-level effects (meets I6). Analyses were performed in MNI space with the MPFC seed coordinate reported (MNI −4/54/−8) and cluster-based results described, indicating stereotactic reporting (meets I7). The study reports BOLD fMRI analyses (meets I8). The manuscript indicates cluster/coordinate-based results derived from whole-brain contrasts and figures/tables (meets I9). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, includes healthy-group task effects, is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based BOLD fMRI study of healthy adult participants performing arithmetic (addition/subtraction) — a rule-based problem-solving task that involves goal-directed computation and execution of operations. The paper reports group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses, uses stereotactic (MNI) space coordinates (tables/figures referenced), and describes BOLD acquisition and voxelwise results. Core sections (introduction, methods, results, discussion, conclusion) are present. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not patient-group-only contrasts, empirical data in healthy adults). Therefore all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 are satisfied.

This is a task-based fMRI (1.5T BOLD) study in healthy adult volunteers (group n=14) performing the PASAT, which involves rule-based arithmetic operations (adding consecutive digits) and thus satisfies the review's problem-solving definition (goal-directed calculation/planning and execution). The study reports whole-brain random-effects group analyses, provides stereotactic coordinates (MNI transformed to Talairach) in tables/figures, and presents voxelwise task-related increases. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so it appears complete. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9; no exclusion criteria are met.

Full text provided is incomplete (only abstract/metadata). Based on available information: the study used 15O-water PET in eight healthy adults and reports task-related rCBF changes and group-level activations (satisfies I8 and likely I6). However, the experimental tasks are semantic association/recognition (Pyramids and Palm Trees paradigm), which do not clearly meet the review's definition of a problem-solving task requiring goal-directed planning/sequencing/executing operations (I5 not met). I cannot confirm stereotactic coordinate reporting in Talairach/MNI space (I7 not met) or availability of voxelwise coordinates/tables (I9 not verifiable) because the full text is missing. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Because key inclusion criteria cannot be confirmed and the full text is incomplete, the study is excluded.

This is an fMRI study in healthy adult participants (n=17) using a transitive reasoning (logical problem-solving) task that requires evaluating premises and applying logical rules to determine validity — meeting the review’s definition of problem-solving. The study reports group-level whole-brain SPM analyses (random-effects), BOLD fMRI results, and stereotactic coordinates (e.g., 42,20,-8; -34,22,-8) in standardized space. Behavioral and imaging results are fully reported (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (includes methods, results, and discussion). Therefore it satisfies I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 and should be INCLUDED.

Full text appears incomplete (only abstract/metadata provided). Based on available information: Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level effects in healthy adult participants are reported) and I8 (rCBF PET analysis). Inclusion criteria not met or not verifiable from provided content: I5 (task is mental rotation, which does not clearly meet the review's definition of a problem-solving task requiring planning/sequencing/evaluative operations) and I7 (no stereotactic coordinates reported in the provided abstract; cannot confirm Talairach/MNI coordinates). No exclusion criteria are explicitly met. Therefore I exclude the study because it fails to meet I5 and I7 and the full text is incomplete, preventing confirmation of additional required details.

This study does not examine a problem-solving task as defined in the review. It uses a Go/No Go response-inhibition paradigm and resting-state contrasts during an acute massage intervention, which does not involve goal-directed planning, sequencing, or execution to arrive at a solution. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level fMRI in healthy adults), I7 (reports MNI stereotactic coordinates), I8 (reports BOLD fMRI analyses), I9 (voxelwise results reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (does not study a problem-solving task). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore EXCLUDED because it fails to meet I5.

Although this is an empirical, whole-brain task-based fMRI study in healthy adults reporting BOLD results in MNI coordinates (satisfies I6, I7, I8, I9), the experimental task probes working-memory recoding and recognition (segmenting and binding of prelearned chunks) rather than a problem-solving task as defined in the review (goal-directed novel problem solving requiring planning/evaluation/sequencing to arrive at a previously unknown solution). The task involves recognition of learned sequences and memory manipulation within a constrained, trained stimulus set, not domain-general problem solving across domains. Therefore I5 (task is a problem-solving task per review definition) is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete. Inclusion criteria met: I6, I7, I8, I9. Inclusion criterion not met: I5. Exclusion criteria applied: [].

This is an empirical, whole-brain task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that reports group-level BOLD results in stereotactic (Talairach) coordinates. However, it does not investigate a ‘‘problem-solving’’ task as defined for the review. The experimental tasks are simulated driving maneuvers (turning, responding to traffic) and a concurrent auditory true/false general-knowledge task; these probe attention, visuomotor control, and auditory/semantic judgment under distraction rather than goal-directed problem solving involving evaluation, planning/sequencing of actions within a rule-based framework to arrive at a (novel) solution. Therefore I5 is not met. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level analysis in healthy adults), I7 (stereotactic coordinates reported), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), I9 (voxelwise results reported). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

The sugar production factory (SPF) task is a goal-directed task requiring subjects to attain a specified target by planning and adjusting actions based on feedback, meeting the review’s definition of problem solving (I5). The study used whole-brain, task-based BOLD fMRI with group-level (inter-subject) one-sample t-tests in healthy adult participants (I6, I8). The methods explicitly reference stereotactic procedures and anatomical labelling with the Talairach Daemon and standardized templates, and voxelwise activation maps/contrasts are described (figures/tables referenced), satisfying I7 and I9. No exclusion criteria apply: results include whole-brain analyses (not ROI-only), report healthy-group task effects, and are empirical. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; therefore fulltext_incomplete=false.

The study reports task-based whole-brain BOLD fMRI of a planning/problem-solving task (Tower of London 4-step planning) in healthy adult participants. It includes group-level whole-brain analyses using SPM, normalization to MNI space, and reports task-related activation maps/cluster lists (voxelwise results). The task meets the problem-solving definition (goal-directed planning/sequencing to reach a target). The paper provides methods, results, and discussion (full text content present). Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9, and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

Although this is an empirical, whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adults reporting BOLD results in standardized (Talairach) space, the task is a visual line-search/target-detection paradigm emphasizing cognitive control, working memory, and stimulus–response mapping. It does not meet the review's definition of a problem-solving task (I5) — there is no evidence that participants needed to identify/plan a sequence of actions or perform critical thinking to find a novel solution; the task involves detection and maintenance of target orientation and S–R updates rather than problem solving across domains. Therefore include criteria I6, I7, I8, and I9 are satisfied, but I5 is not. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based, whole-brain BOLD fMRI study using an N-back working memory task in unaffected siblings of schizophrenia patients and healthy comparison subjects. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level fMRI analyses including healthy comparison subjects), I7 (stereotactic coordinates reported in Talairach space), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), I9 (voxelwise results reported in tables/figures). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (the experimental task is an N-back working memory paradigm, not a problem-solving task as defined by the review). Exclusion criteria met: E5 (the paper emphasizes between-group contrasts—siblings vs. controls—and does not present an independent healthy-group task effect for a problem-solving task). Therefore the study does not address the review objective of problem-solving tasks in healthy adults and must be excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study of semantic event sequencing (an executive problem-solving task involving goal-directed planning/sequencing and rule-constrained operations). It reports whole-brain, group-level analyses for a healthy control group (within-group contrasts and between-group comparisons), provides stereotactic coordinates (MNI) for task-related increases, and uses BOLD fMRI analyses. Voxelwise results and coordinates are reported in the main text, with additional ROI analyses but not limited to ROI-only results. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This study is an fMRI investigation of decision-making/prediction under uncertainty with an aversive interoceptive manipulation (two-choice prediction task with breathing load). Although it is task-based fMRI, reports whole-brain BOLD results with stereotactic coordinates and includes healthy control participants, it does not investigate a problem-solving task as defined by the review (goal-directed problem solving requiring evaluation, planning/sequencing of actions and executing rule-based operations to reach a correct/novel solution). The paradigm is a reinforcement/prediction/decision task rather than a problem-solving task (e.g., semantic, algebraic, logical, mechanical problem solving). Therefore inclusion criterion I5 is not met. Full text is complete.

This is an event-related, task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants using a mental rotation task with a clear goal-directed procedure (decide whether two objects are identical or mirror images), requiring subjects to compute and execute spatial transformations to reach the goal. The paper reports whole-brain, random-effects (group-level) analyses, uses finite impulse response modeling of BOLD fMRI data, and reports stereotactic coordinates (MNI) and voxelwise contrasts (whole-brain and ROI) for task epochs. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I5 (goal-directed problem-solving-like task involving planning/sequencing of operations), I6 (whole-brain group-level analyses in healthy adults), I7 (stereotactic coordinates in MNI space), I8 (BOLD fMRI analyses), and I9 (voxelwise results reported). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only; empirical healthy-group task effects are reported). Full text appears complete (background, methods, results, discussion).

This fMRI study examines pragmatic language (metaphor and sarcasm) and mentalizing, not problem-solving as defined by the review (goal-directed planning/sequencing/executing operations to arrive at a solution). Although the paper meets several methodological inclusion criteria (whole-brain group fMRI analyses with reported stereotactic coordinates and BOLD contrasts), it does not investigate a problem-solving task (I5 not met). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Inclusion criteria met: I6, I7, I8, I9. Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task is language/pragmatics comprehension, not problem-solving). Full text appears complete and adequate for screening. Hence exclude.

The study is excluded because it does not meet key inclusion criteria for the review. Inclusion met: I8 (uses task-based BOLD fMRI). Inclusion not met: I5 (the task is rule representation/task-switching evaluating executive function, not a defined problem-solving task as required), I6 (whole-brain group-level fMRI effects are reported only in children; no whole-brain group-level task fMRI effects are reported for healthy adults), I7 (stereotactic coordinate results for adult task-related effects are not reported for healthy adults in the manuscript excerpt). No exclusion criteria from the list (E3–E6) are specifically violated. Full text appears complete. Therefore the study does not satisfy all required inclusion criteria (notably I5 and I6) and must be excluded from a meta-analysis of problem-solving fMRI in healthy adults.

The study does not meet inclusion criterion I5: the task used is a probabilistic reversal learning (reinforcement learning) task producing prediction error signals, not a problem-solving task as defined (goal-directed critical thinking/planning/sequencing to arrive at a solution in semantic/algebraic/logical/etc. domains). It does meet I6 (group-level task-based fMRI analyses in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates), I8 (reports BOLD analyses), and I9 (voxelwise results/coordinates reported in text/figures). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore excluded because I5 is not satisfied; inclusion criteria met: I6, I7, I8, I9; inclusion criteria not met: I5.

This is an empirical, task-based BOLD fMRI study in healthy adults that examines single-digit multiplication (a rule-based arithmetic problem-solving task involving goal-directed evaluation and execution of operations and strategies). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses, with results presented in MNI stereotactic coordinates and FWE-corrected voxelwise thresholds. BOLD methods, GLM analysis, and voxelwise coordinate tables/figures are provided. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not a non-empirical paper, includes within-group task effects). Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9.

Full text unavailable (only title/metadata provided). Cannot verify any required inclusion criteria from the provided content. Therefore excluded. (a) Exclusion IDs met: none (no evidence of E3–E6). (b) Inclusion IDs met: none. (c) Inclusion IDs not met / could not be confirmed: I5 (cannot confirm task-based problem-solving definition and task details), I6 (cannot confirm whole-brain group-level analyses in healthy adults), I7 (cannot confirm reporting of stereotactic coordinates), I8 (cannot confirm BOLD or rCBF analysis), I9 (cannot confirm availability of voxelwise coordinate results). Full text incomplete, so decision based on incomplete information.

The study is excluded because it does not investigate a problem-solving task as defined (I5 not met). The task involved free verbal description of Rorschach inkblots and measurement of syntactic complexity, not a goal-directed problem solving paradigm requiring evaluation, planning/sequencing actions, or rule-based operations to reach a solution. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level fMRI analyses including healthy adult controls), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates/Talairach space), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), I9 (voxelwise results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria are met (exclusion_criteria_applied=[]). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

Full text appears incomplete (only title/abstract provided). Based on available information: the task is a word stem completion (lexical retrieval/search) which does not clearly meet the review's definition of a problem-solving task (I5 not met). The abstract indicates group fMRI activations (BOLD) consistent with whole-brain group analyses, so I6 and I8 are satisfied. There is no explicit reporting of stereotactic coordinates in the provided content, so I7 cannot be confirmed. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Because I5 (task meets problem-solving definition) and I7 (coordinates reported) are not confirmed, the study is excluded pending full-text review.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults using the Montreal Card-Sorting Task (a variant of the Wisconsin Card-Sorting Task) that requires goal-directed classification, evaluation of task rules, planning of set-shifts, and execution of rule-based responses — matching the review definition of problem solving. The study reports whole-brain, random-effects group analyses on BOLD fMRI data, provides stereotactic coordinates in Talairach space for voxelwise peaks, and presents voxelwise results in figures/tables. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9; no exclusion criteria are met.

Although the study is a task-based fMRI investigation in healthy adults, reports whole-brain group-level analyses with stereotactic coordinates (MNI) and BOLD results, and provides voxelwise results, it does not examine a problem-solving task as defined by the review (goal-directed problem solving requiring planning/sequencing and execution of rule-based operations to reach a previously unknown solution). The virtual maze task is a spatial learning/navigation and memory paradigm (passive encoding of a virtual environment and inferencing relative positions), not an explicit problem-solving paradigm per the meta-analysis definition.
