Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level fMRI analysis in healthy adults — mixed-effects group maps reported on 10 healthy participants), I8 (task-based BOLD fMRI data reported), and I9 (voxelwise/group results presented in figures and ROI tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task does not satisfy the review's problem-solving definition). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I5: the task (Balloon Analogue Risk Task) is a risk/reward decision-making task, not a problem-solving task as defined (i.e., requiring identification/planning/sequencing to reach a correct or novel solution). It DOES meet I6 (whole-brain, group-level fMRI analyses in adults), I7 (reports stereotactic MNI coordinates), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), and I9 (voxelwise/coordinate results reported in main text/tables). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore exclusion is based on failing I5 while satisfying I6–I9.

This study is excluded because it does not meet the meta-analysis's definition of a problem-solving task (I5). The Weather Prediction Task (WPT) used here probes probabilistic association learning and gradual cue–outcome learning rather than explicit problem solving requiring goal-directed planning, sequencing of actions, or critical evaluation to arrive at a novel solution. The full text does meet other inclusion criteria: I6 (whole-brain group-level fMRI analyses in healthy adults are reported), I7 (task-related activations reported in stereotactic space, with coordinate tables/supplementary materials referenced), I8 (BOLD fMRI measures are used), and I9 (voxelwise results available in figures/tables/supplement). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore excluded based on failure to satisfy I5.

This study uses a random number generation (RNG) task to probe executive functions, but RNG does not meet the review's definition of a problem-solving task (I5). RNG requires suppression of habitual responses and controlled response generation, not formulation of a goal-directed plan or execution of rule-based operations to arrive at a correct/novel solution in the sense required by the meta-analysis. The study does meet other inclusion criteria: I6 (whole-brain group-level fMRI in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates in Talairach/MNI space), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), and I9 (voxelwise results presented). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore excluded due to failure to satisfy I5 (problem-solving task definition).

This is a longitudinal fMRI study in RR-MS patients using a go/no-go inhibition task (response inhibition/attention), not a problem-solving task as defined by I5 (goal-directed planning/sequencing or applying rules to arrive at a solution). The full text is complete. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (healthy adult group-level whole-brain analyses present), I7 (stereotactic coordinates reported), I8 (BOLD fMRI analyses), I9 (voxelwise results available in text/tables). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (task does not involve problem solving per the review definition). No exclusion criteria are triggered. Therefore exclude.

This is an fMRI methods/results paper analyzing scale-free and multifractal dynamics during rest and an auditory detection task. It does not investigate a problem-solving task as defined by the review (no goal-directed planning/sequencing or rule-based problem-solving across semantic, algebraic, logical, mechanical domains). Therefore inclusion criterion I5 is not met. The study does meet I6 (whole-brain group-level analyses in healthy adults) and I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis); qualifying voxelwise results are presented as group maps/figures so I9 is also satisfied. It does not clearly report stereotactic coordinate tables for task-related activation (I7 not met). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based BOLD fMRI study of logical problem solving (elementary deductive inference: modus ponens and disjunction elimination), which fits the review’s definition of problem solving (goal-directed, rule-based operations to arrive at a correct conclusion). It used whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses in healthy adults (N=14) with normalization to MNI space and SPM reporting; voxelwise BOLD results and cluster coordinates are reported/available in figures/tables and supplementary materials. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I5 (task-based problem solving), I6 (whole-brain group-level effects in healthy adults), I7 (stereotactic coordinates in MNI space), I8 (BOLD analysis), and I9 (voxelwise results available in main/supplementary materials). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not only group comparisons, empirical task effect in healthy subjects). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Full text is complete. The study is an event-related fMRI investigation of probabilistic reversal learning in healthy adults. It meets I6 (group-level whole-brain analyses in healthy adults), I7 (reports MNI stereotactic coordinates), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), and I9 (voxelwise results reported in tables/figures). However, it does not meet I5: the task is probabilistic reversal learning/associative learning and behavioral shifting, not a problem-solving task as defined (goal-directed planning, evaluation, sequencing or execution of operations within semantic/algebraic/logical/mechanical rule frameworks to arrive at a previously unknown solution). No exclusion criteria are met (E3–E6). Therefore, excluded because I5 is not satisfied.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study using the paced visual serial addition task (PVSAT), which involves rule-based arithmetic operations and working memory consistent with the review's definition of problem solving (I5). The study reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses in healthy adult controls (I6), uses BOLD fMRI (I8), and reports stereotactic normalization to MNI space with specific coordinates cited (e.g., x=-2,y=28,z=22) and voxelwise results presented in figures/tables (I7, I9). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, includes healthy-group task effects, and is empirical).

This is an event-related fMRI study of task-switching using simple stimulus–response reversal (press left/right key for +/–, reverse mapping on switch trials). While the paper reports whole-brain, group-level BOLD results with stereotactic coordinates (Talairach) in healthy adults and provides both voxelwise and ROI analyses, the experimental task does not meet the review's operational definition of a problem-solving task (I5). The task requires response-mapping and executive control/switching, but not goal-directed problem solving that requires planning, sequencing actions to reach a goal, or generating solutions within semantic/algebraic/logical/mechanical rule frameworks. Therefore I5 is not satisfied. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This fMRI study does not meet the review's definition of a problem-solving task (I5). The tasks are ordinal judgment and short-term memory retrieval (order STM, alphabetical and numerical order comparisons), which are decision and comparison tasks rather than goal-directed problem-solving involving planning/sequencing to reach a novel solution. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level fMRI in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI space), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), I9 (voxelwise results reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task is not a problem-solving task as defined). Exclusion criteria met: none (no E3–E6 violations). Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study in adults that reports whole-brain, voxelwise group analyses and stereotactic coordinates for task-related activations. The tasks (exact and approximate calculation) require goal-directed operations and execution of rule-based arithmetic to reach correct or plausible sums, fitting the meta-analysis definition of problem-solving. The study includes healthy adult controls with within-group whole-brain fMRI results and between-group comparisons, reports BOLD fMRI analyses, and provides coordinates in standardized space. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so it appears complete.

The study is excluded because it does not meet key inclusion criteria for this review. Inclusion criteria met: I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI space), I8 (reports BOLD fMRI analyses), I9 (voxelwise results reported in text/figures). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task is a paced verbal fluency/language retrieval task, not a defined problem-solving task involving goal-directed planning/sequencing to reach a solution), I6 (no clear whole-brain, within-healthy-group, group-level task effect reported — main task effect is reported for ARMS + controls combined and group comparisons are between ARMS and controls, but a healthy-controls-only whole-brain task activation is not presented). Exclusion criteria met: E5 (study effectively lacks a healthy-group task effect reported as a whole-brain within-group result and relies on between-group contrasts and combined-sample task effects). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore excluded.

Although this is an fMRI study in healthy adults that reports whole-brain group analyses with stereotactic (MNI) coordinates and BOLD results (satisfying I6, I7, I8, I9), the task is moral evaluation/decision-making (judging emotional aversiveness, utilitarian outcomes, and overall moral acceptability) rather than a problem‑solving task as defined by the review (I5). The paradigm does not require participants to identify/plan or execute a sequence of operations to reach a correct or novel solution; it elicits evaluative judgments between options. Therefore I5 is not met and the study must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study (BOLD) in healthy adult participants that investigates analogical mapping processes during metaphor comprehension — a form of relational/analogical reasoning that involves selecting and mapping relevant features (i.e., critical thinking/relational mapping). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses, provides voxelwise results with MNI coordinates, applies SPM2 analyses with FDR correction, and includes both whole-brain and volumetric ROI results. These characteristics satisfy the meta-analysis requirements for a problem-solving/analogical reasoning task measured with task-based fMRI and reporting stereotactic coordinates and BOLD results. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-based BOLD fMRI study in healthy adults (n=20) using a multiplication verification task that requires goal-directed operations, planning/sequencing, and execution of arithmetic rules—meeting the review's problem-solving definition. The paper reports whole-brain, random-effects group analyses (difficulty contrast D>M ∩ M>E), uses Talairach normalization and provides stereotactic results (Table I/figures), and presents BOLD analysis and Granger causality connectivity results. Subgroup comparisons are present but do not replace the primary healthy-group task effects. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, non-empirical, or patient-only contrasts) are met. Therefore the study satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 and is appropriate for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study using the Tower of London, a canonical problem-solving/executive-planning task (satisfies I5). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group analyses using SPM (random-effects) and provides group-level task activation maps for healthy adult control participants (satisfies I6). Activation coordinates are reported in standardized MNI space (satisfies I7). The study uses BOLD fMRI (satisfies I8). Voxelwise results and coordinate tables/figures are presented in the main text/tables (satisfies I9). No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only (E3), healthy-group task effects are reported (E5 not met), not limited to disease/age/gender comparisons (E4 not met), and this is original empirical research (E6 not met). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Excluded because the study does not meet the review’s problem-solving/task criteria and uses ROI-limited molecular PET measures rather than whole-brain task-based activations. Exclusion IDs met: E3 (reports only ROI results — ventral striatum focused binding potentials). Inclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs not met: I5 (task is the Iowa Gambling Task, a decision-making/gambling task rather than a defined problem-solving task per the review definition), I6 (no whole-brain group-level analyses reported — analyses limited to ventral striatum ROI), I7 (no stereotactic coordinate results reported), I8 (does not report BOLD or rCBF task-related analyses; reports raclopride binding potential/dopamine release). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=false. The study is therefore excluded.

This is an empirical, task-based BOLD fMRI study in healthy adult participants using a cognitive set-shifting (rule discovery/selection, feedback evaluation, planning and response execution) paradigm that requires goal identification, strategy generation, planning and rule-based execution — fitting the review’s definition of problem solving. The analysis used whole-brain, group-level random-effects GLMs, transformed to Talairach space with reported peak activations (voxelwise maps/ROIs derived from whole-brain thresholds), satisfying requirements for stereotactic coordinates and voxelwise BOLD results. All inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 are met. No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only reporting, not a non-empirical paper, includes within-group task effects in healthy adults). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This empirical fMRI study uses a goal-directed evidence-accumulation task where subjects must infer which deck supplied the draws (clear goal and requirement to evaluate evidence and update beliefs), which fits the review's problem-solving definition (I5). It reports whole-brain, group-level analyses including within-group effects for healthy control adults (I6), provides stereotactic coordinates in MNI space (I7), and reports BOLD fMRI results (I8). Task-related voxelwise results are presented in tables/figures and supplementary materials (I9). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only reporting, non-empirical paper, or absence of healthy-group task effects). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion, tables, supporting information). Therefore include.

Excluded because the study does not investigate problem-solving tasks as defined (I5 not met). It instead examines emotion regulation, resting-state connectivity, and reward processing in women with subclinical depressive symptoms. The study does satisfy I6 (whole-brain, group-level fMRI analyses in adult participants), I7 (reports results in MNI space), I8 (BOLD fMRI analyses), and I9 (voxelwise results reported/illustrated). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of working memory (n-back) in healthy adults using ROI/VOI-based analyses rather than voxelwise whole-brain stereotactic reporting. Exclusion criterion met: E3 (reports only ROI results) — the methods and results describe manually delineated VOIs/ROIs and percentage signal-change analyses without presenting voxelwise whole-brain coordinate tables. Inclusion criteria met: I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task is an n-back working memory task, not a problem-solving task as defined), I6 (no voxelwise whole-brain group-level analysis is reported — analyses are ROI-based), I7 (no stereotactic coordinates in Talairach/MNI space are provided in the supplied full text). Therefore the study does not satisfy the meta-analysis requirements and is excluded.

Full text is incomplete (only abstract provided). The study investigates decision-making under risk (Game of Dice Task) in Parkinson’s patients and healthy controls using fMRI, but the task appears to assess risky decision-making/feedback processing rather than the defined problem-solving construct (goal-directed planning/sequencing to reach a solution). The abstract reports group activations for healthy subjects (suggesting whole-brain group-level effects) and uses fMRI (BOLD), but does not report stereotactic coordinates in the abstract and critical methodological details are unavailable. Therefore I cannot confirm all required inclusion criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults with whole-brain, group-level BOLD analyses reported in MNI space (meets I6, I7, I8, I9). However, the task is social conflict resolution (friend/foe judgments resolving verbal/non-verbal incongruity), which does not meet the review's definition of a problem-solving task (I5) involving goal-directed planning/sequencing operations to reach a solution across domains. No exclusion criteria (E3-E6) apply. Therefore the study is excluded because it does not satisfy I5.

This is an fMRI study of semantic processing using a synonym-judgement task (concrete vs abstract word comprehension) with contextual cueing, not a problem-solving task as defined by the review (goal-directed planning/sequencing/executive problem resolution). It includes whole-brain group-level BOLD analyses with stereotactic (MNI) coordinates and reports results in tables/figures, so it satisfies I6, I7, I8 and I9. However it does NOT satisfy I5 (the task is semantic judgement/comprehension rather than a problem-solving paradigm involving planning/sequencing/executing operations to reach a solution). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore the paper must be excluded.

This study is excluded because it does not meet the review's definition of a problem-solving task (I5). The tasks used (Hayling sentence completion emphasizing inhibition; and N-back working memory/update task) probe inhibition and working memory/attention, not the goal-directed problem-solving processes as defined by I5 (evaluating a problem, planning/sequencing actions to reach a previously unknown correct solution). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (reports group-level whole-brain analyses including a healthy control group), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates in Talairach space), I8 (BOLD fMRI analyses), I9 (voxelwise results available in tables/figures/supplement). Exclusion criteria met: none (no ROI-only reporting, healthy-group effects are present, not a non-empirical paper). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore excluded for failing I5 (task definition).

This study is an fMRI investigation of ambiguous doubly-quantified sentence comprehension (language/ambiguity resolution) rather than a task explicitly framed or designed as a domain-general problem-solving task. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level fMRI in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic/MNI normalization and coordinate tables/figures), I8 (reports BOLD analyses), I9 (voxelwise results presented in tables/figures). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (the task does not clearly constitute a problem-solving task as defined by the review — it is a language comprehension/interpretation decision about sentence-picture correspondence rather than a goal-directed planning/sequencing problem-solving operation to derive a novel solution). No exclusion criteria were triggered. Full text appears complete. Therefore the study is excluded for not meeting I5.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that includes whole-brain analyses and reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI space and BOLD results (meets I6, I7, I8, and I9). However, the behavioral tasks are recognition/memory and task-control/performance-monitoring paradigms (e.g., old/new recognition, living/non-living judgments, unmasking/reveal tasks) rather than problem-solving as defined in I5 (no evidence of goal-directed problem solving requiring planning/sequencing or executing rule-based operations to arrive at a novel solution). Therefore I5 is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This paper reports task-based whole-brain BOLD fMRI in healthy adults using an fMRI-adapted Trail-Making Test (a sequencing/set-switching executive task consistent with problem-solving processes), so it meets I5 (problem-solving-like task), I6 (group-level whole-brain effects in healthy adults), and I8 (BOLD analysis). However, in the provided full text there is no explicit reporting of task-related stereotactic coordinates (Talairach or MNI) or coordinate tables/labels: activations are described by slices and anatomical regions but no standardized coordinate results are shown or referenced in the main text. Inclusion criterion I7 (reporting stereotactic coordinates in Talairach or MNI space) is not satisfied in the available full text, so the study cannot be included. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered by the provided content.

This PET study examines a self-ordered object task with a clear goal (select each object only once) requiring planning/sequencing, monitoring, and rule-constrained responses, which fits the review’s operational definition of a problem-solving task (I5). It reports whole-brain group-level PET analyses in healthy adult participants (n=8, ages 19–26) with voxelwise subtraction and pixel-wise correlations (I6). Task-related activations are reported as stereotactic coordinates (Talairach x,y,z) for multiple regions (I7) and the primary neuroimaging metric is regional cerebral blood flow (rCBF) from PET (I8). Results are reported in the main text with coordinates (acceptable per I9). The full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not a clinical group comparison, includes healthy-group task effects, and is empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included.

Full text is complete. The study meets inclusion criteria I6 (whole-brain, group-level analyses including healthy adult controls), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI space), I8 (reports rCBF PET analyses), and I9 (voxelwise results and coordinate data are reported). However, it does NOT meet I5: the experimental paradigms are nonverbal theory-of-mind (attribution of intentions) and physical-causality perception tasks rather than a defined problem-solving task as specified (goal-directed problem solving involving planning/sequencing or executing operations within a rule set to reach a previously unknown solution). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Therefore the article is excluded because it fails the core content inclusion criterion I5.

This is a task-based BOLD fMRI study in healthy adult participants that required goal-directed hypothesis-testing and rule discovery to classify stimuli (i.e., participants had to discover and apply verbal/multi-component rules to arrive at correct category labels). The design involves group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses, reports stereotactic coordinates (MNI with conversion to Talairach) in tables/figures, and presents BOLD activation results. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5 (task requires rule discovery/hypothesis-driven problem solving), I6 (whole-brain group-level effects in healthy adults), I7 (stereotactic coordinates reported), I8 (BOLD fMRI), and I9 (voxelwise results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not a non-empirical paper, includes healthy-group task effects). Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This study does not meet the review requirement for whole-brain group-level analysis (I6). The authors explicitly state they did not scan the whole brain due to sinus artifacts and report activations from a limited set of slices; therefore it lacks whole-brain coverage/analysis. Additionally, the primary task is a go/no-go inhibition paradigm (not a problem-solving task as defined by I5); although WCST (set-shifting) data are referenced/compared, WCST was not the primary whole-brain problem-solving analysis in this paper. Inclusion criteria met: I7 (reports Talairach coordinates), I8 (event-related BOLD fMRI), I9 (voxelwise results reported in figures/tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no whole-brain analysis/group-level whole-brain coverage), and I5 (primary task is inhibitory; WCST data are secondary/comparative). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) were directly triggered by the paper content.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adults using multiplication verification and magnitude judgment tasks that require algebraic/number operations consistent with problem-solving demands. The study reports whole-brain, group-level SPM analyses of BOLD fMRI data with stereotactic Talairach coordinates for activated loci. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I5 (problem-solving arithmetic/magnitude tasks), I6 (whole-brain group analysis in healthy adults), I7 (Talairach coordinates), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), and I9 (voxelwise results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, no between-group-only contrasts, not a review). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study reports task-based fMRI in healthy adults with whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses, MNI coordinates, and BOLD results (meets I6, I7, I8, I9). However, the experimental tasks are perceptual discrimination and stimulus–response mapping manipulations (identifying the shortest line, changing mapping), requiring application of learned rules rather than solving a novel or open-ended problem. The tasks do not involve goal-directed problem solving as defined (evaluating a problem, planning/sequencing actions to discover/derive a solution, or generating a previously unknown solution). Therefore it does not meet I5 (problem-solving task) and must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

Full text is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults with whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses reporting MNI coordinates and BOLD results (meets I6, I7, I8, I9). However, the experimental task investigates humor/joke comprehension (detection and resolution of incongruity, funniness ratings) rather than a goal-directed problem-solving paradigm as defined in I5 (planning/sequencing/executing operations to reach a correct or novel solution). No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study does not satisfy I5 and must be excluded. Full text appears complete.

This fMRI study uses WCST variants that require subjects to deduce sorting rules, plan and execute responses, and use feedback—meeting the review's definition of problem-solving (goal-directed rule discovery and application). It reports whole-brain, group-level (random effects) analyses in healthy adults, provides stereotactic coordinates in MNI space (tables/figures), and reports BOLD fMRI results. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, patient-only contrasts, non-empirical) apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adults using a 3-operand mental arithmetic task that requires applying rule-based operations to reach a correct answer (qualifies as problem solving). It reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses (SPM5 second-level ANOVA), BOLD fMRI results, and stereotactic coordinates (MNI/Talairach) for task-related activations/deactivations. Voxelwise results are presented in figures/tables and supplements. All relevant inclusion criteria are met, and none of the exclusion criteria apply. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided and appears complete for screening purposes.

The study is an empirical, task-based fMRI experiment in healthy adults (N=18) that includes tasks requiring rule-based sequencing and operations (Reverse Polish arithmetic and hierarchical integration) that constitute problem-solving as defined (goal-directed computation via rule-based operations to arrive at a correct result). Whole-brain group-level analyses were performed using SPM8 (cluster-level correction reported). Sterotactic coordinates are reported in tables/figures (MNI space), and analyses are BOLD fMRI based. The full text provided contains Introduction, Methods, Results and Discussion, so full text appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9) and no exclusion criteria apply.

The task is an ocular motor delayed response (ODR) paradigm indexing spatial working memory and inhibitory control, not a problem-solving task as defined in I5 (goal-directed generation of solutions via planning/sequencing within a semantic/algebraic/logical/mechanical rule set). Therefore the study does not meet I5. The full text is complete. The study does satisfy other imaging-related inclusion criteria: whole-brain group-level analyses in healthy adults (I6), stereotactic coordinates in Talairach space (I7), reports BOLD fMRI analyses (I8), and presents voxelwise results in figures/tables (I9). No exclusion criteria are triggered (e.g., not ROI-only, includes healthy-group task effects). Hence excluded due to failure to meet I5.

This study does not examine a problem-solving task as defined in the review objective. It uses a continuous verbal 2-back working memory task (not a problem-solving paradigm requiring goal-directed planning/operations across semantic, algebraic, logical, mechanical frameworks). Additionally, the paper focuses on resting-state and functional connectivity (partial correlations) and does not report task-related stereotactic coordinate activations in Talairach/MNI space for problem-solving contrasts (I7 not met). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain analyses in healthy adults) and I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task is not a problem-solving task) and I7 (no task-related stereotactic coordinate results reported for problem-solving). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) explicitly apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Full text is incomplete: only title/abstract/metadata provided. Abstract indicates an fMRI task of rule- vs similarity-based categorization in healthy young adults, which likely meets I5 (a rule-based task involving execution of rules). However, I cannot confirm critical required details from the full text: (I6) whether whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses were reported; (I7) whether stereotactic coordinates (Talairach/MNI) for task-related increases are reported; and (I8) explicit reporting of BOLD or rCBF analyses (although fMRI is mentioned, the abstract does not explicitly state BOLD results or coordinate tables). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are evident from the abstract. Because core methodological/result details required to determine eligibility are not accessible, the study must be excluded pending full-text retrieval.

Although the study uses task-based fMRI in healthy adults and reports whole-brain, coordinate-based BOLD results (satisfying I6, I7, I8, I9), it does not investigate a problem-solving task as defined by the review. The sequential investment paradigm examines economic decision-making and learning from experienced and fictive outcomes, not the type of problem solving that requires identifying/planning/sequencing operations to reach a goal or arrive at a correct previously unknown solution. Therefore I5 is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants that includes a Tower of London planning task which meets the review’s definition of problem-solving (goal-directed planning/sequencing of moves). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level GLM analyses with cluster-corrected activations and presents results in MNI space (including ROI centers of gravity and group activation maps), and includes BOLD signal analyses. Voxelwise/whole-brain results are reported in figures/tables. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8 and I9. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not a review, includes within-group task effects in healthy adults). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

The study does not meet I5: although it uses task-based fMRI in healthy adults and reports whole-brain, group-level BOLD results with stereotactic coordinates, the experimental tasks (mental rotation, silent verb reading with recognition) do not constitute a problem-solving paradigm as defined in the review (no explicit goal requiring participants to figure out a novel solution via planning/sequencing operations to reach an unknown solution). Thus I5 is not met. Inclusion criteria met: I6, I7, I8, I9. Exclusion criteria met: none.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=15, mean age 24.6) who actively solved algebraic equations — a clear problem-solving task. The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxel-wise analyses (ANOVAs with subject as a random factor), thresholding and cluster criteria, and presents stereotactic results in Talairach space. BOLD (fMRI) analyses are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants using a number-subtraction mental-calculation task that requires goal-directed processing, planning and execution of arithmetic operations (meets I5). It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses using SPM99 (random-effects one-sample t tests) in healthy adults (meets I6). Stereotactic coordinates are reported (Talairach) for activations (meets I7). The study uses BOLD fMRI (meets I8). Voxelwise results are presented in figures/tables in the main text (meets I9). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not a patient/group-comparison-only study, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

Although this study reports whole-brain, voxelwise BOLD fMRI results in standardized MNI coordinates (meets I7, I8, I9), it does not meet core inclusion criteria for this meta-analysis. The task used (Hayling Sentence Completion Test) is a verbal initiation/semantic completion paradigm and does not clearly constitute a problem-solving task as defined (goal-directed planning/sequencing or rule-based solution operations) (fails I5). Additionally, participants are a cohort of individuals at high genetic risk for schizophrenia (unaffected relatives), not a sample of healthy adult participants as required (fails I6). The full text is complete. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are specifically triggered by the report.

This study does not investigate problem-solving as defined by the review (a goal-directed task requiring planning, sequencing, or rule-based operations to arrive at a solution). It is an fMRI study of intention understanding of symbolic gestures (social cognition), not a problem-solving task, so inclusion criterion I5 is not met. Met inclusion criteria: I6 (whole-brain, group-level fMRI in healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI space), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), I9 (voxelwise results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria from the review apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the article must be excluded because it fails I5 (task definition).

Full text is complete. Meets inclusion criteria I6 (whole-brain, group-level effects including healthy adults), I7 (reports stereotactic coordinates in Talairach space), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), and I9 (voxelwise results presented in tables/figures). Does NOT meet I5: the tasks are working memory (2-back), intentional encoding, and recognition — these are memory tasks, not problem-solving tasks as defined (goal-directed deliberation, planning/sequencing operations to reach a solution within a rule set). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Therefore excluded because the key inclusion criterion I5 (problem-solving task) is not satisfied.

This study is excluded because analyses were restricted to a VMPFC ROI rather than a whole-brain task effect (exclusion E3). Inclusion criteria met: I7 (reports stereotactic MNI coordinates), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), and I9 (voxelwise/stereotactic results reported in main text). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (the task is the Iowa Gambling Task — a risky decision-making task, not a problem-solving task as defined by the review), and I6 (no whole-brain group-level task analysis in healthy adults; group analyses were performed within an anatomically defined VMPFC mask). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is a task-based fMRI study of mathematical problem solving in healthy adults (N=39) that used whole-brain voxelwise analyses and BOLD fMRI. The task meets the review’s definition of problem solving (goal-directed transformations/planning/execution to reach unknown solutions). Group-level whole-brain GLM analyses are reported (voxel-wise t-tests, thresholding, and statistical maps), and results are described regionally; voxelwise results are indicated to be available in figures/maps (satisfying allowance for coordinates in figures/tables/supplement). BOLD signal analyses and MVPA/HMM approaches are central to the paper. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not a between-group-only comparison, not a review). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore all applicable inclusion criteria are met and the study should be included.

This is a task-based (event-related) whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adults using the Wisconsin Word Sorting Task, which requires discovering and applying classification rules by trial-and-error (goal-directed problem solving involving evaluation, planning/set-shifting, and rule-based execution). Group-level mixed-effects whole-brain analyses were performed and reported; results were transformed into Talairach space and peak coordinates are given in tables. BOLD signal changes are reported. Voxelwise results are presented in tables/figures. Thus the study meets all inclusion criteria (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9) and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

(a) Exclusion IDs met: none. (b) Inclusion IDs met: I6 (performs whole-brain analyses with group-level maps in healthy adult participants) and I8 (BOLD fMRI data reported). (c) Inclusion IDs not met: I5 (the tasks are perceptual discrimination (/ra/ vs /la/) and a numerical magnitude comparison/distance-effect task, which are not problem-solving tasks as defined by the review—they lack goal-directed multi-step planning, rule-based problem solving, or execution of strategies to reach a novel solution) and I7 (the provided full text does not report stereotactic coordinates in Talairach or MNI space for task-related activations; only illustrative group weight maps are described). Therefore the study does not meet all required inclusion criteria for a meta-analysis of problem-solving tasks and is excluded.

Full text is complete. This is an fMRI study of moral judgment and cognitive conflict using personal/impersonal moral dilemmas. While it meets imaging-related inclusion criteria (I6: group-level whole-brain analyses in 41 healthy adults; I7: stereotactic/voxelwise results reported; I8: BOLD fMRI data; I9: voxelwise results presented in tables/figures), it does not meet the meta-analysis’s problem-solving task definition (I5). The tasks are moral judgment/decision-making dilemmas (evaluating permissibility of actions) rather than explicit problem-solving tasks requiring goal formulation, planning/sequencing operations within a rule framework to arrive at a correct or optimal solution. Therefore it fails I5 and must be excluded. Exclusion criteria: none met. Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion present).

This study does NOT meet the meta-analysis definition of a problem-solving task (I5). The mental rotation task is a visuo-spatial transformation/identification task (identical vs mirror) rather than a goal-directed problem-solving paradigm requiring evaluation, planning/sequencing, or executing rule-based operations to reach a previously unknown solution. It does meet other inclusion criteria: I6 (group-level whole-brain random-effects fMRI in healthy adults), I7 (stereotactic coordinates reported), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), and I9 (voxelwise results/tables). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore EXCLUDED because I5 (problem-solving task definition) is not satisfied.

This study is excluded because it does not meet I5: the task is a number-comparison/choice task (choose larger or smaller digit) and does not involve problem-solving as defined (no goal-directed planning, sequencing of actions to arrive at a novel solution or complex evaluation/strategy). It does meet I6 (whole-brain, group-level task-based fMRI in healthy adults), I7 (reports MNI coordinates), I8 (BOLD analysis), and I9 (voxelwise results reported in figures/tables). No exclusion criteria (E3-E6) are met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

The study uses a phonologic verbal fluency (word generation) task rather than an explicit problem-solving paradigm as defined by the review (I5). Although the paper includes a whole-brain, task-based fMRI analysis with healthy adult participants and reports stereotactic coordinates and BOLD-based results, the primary task is language/fluency production and not a goal-directed problem-solving task requiring planning/sequencing to reach a novel solution. Full text appears complete. Therefore the study fails to meet inclusion criterion I5 (problem-solving task). Inclusion criteria met: I6, I7, I8, I9. Inclusion criteria not met: I5. Exclusion criteria met: none ([]).

This is a task-based fMRI study of mental arithmetic (addition, subtraction, multiplication, division) in healthy adults that involves goal-directed problem solving under rule-based operations (arithmetic), meeting the review's problem-solving definition. The study reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses (n=11 healthy adults) with BOLD fMRI, provides voxelwise contrast results (complex vs. simple for each operator), and states stereotactic coordinate reporting (MNI transformed to Talairach). Voxelwise results are described and conjunction analyses reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not a patient-group comparison, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9.

Meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis: (I5) The task is a goal-directed landing decision requiring evaluation of information, planning (land vs. go-around) and execution under rule-based payoff structure; (I6) Whole-brain, group-level fMRI analyses in healthy adult participants (n=15) are reported; (I7) Task-related activation peaks are reported in stereotactic space (MNI converted to Talairach) with coordinates; (I8) BOLD fMRI data are used and analyzed; (I9) Voxelwise results and coordinates are reported in the main text and supplementary materials. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study reports an event-related task in healthy adults requiring participants to select the larger of two two-digit numbers (goal-directed, rule-based comparison). This meets the review's broad I5 definition (goal plus execution of rule-based operations to arrive at a correct solution). It includes whole-brain, group-level BOLD fMRI analyses in healthy adults (I6, I8), reports stereotactic coordinates (Talairach/MNI) for task-related activations (I7), and provides voxelwise results in figures/tables (I9). The full text contains methods, results, and discussion (fulltext complete). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not a between-group-only comparison, and is an empirical study). Confidence is moderate (0.75) because classifying simple magnitude-comparison tasks as “problem-solving” is somewhat borderline, but the task conforms to the supplied inclusive definition of problem-solving (rule-based operations to reach a correct solution).

Full text is complete. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level fMRI analysis in healthy adults), I7 (reports MNI stereotactic coordinates), I8 (reports BOLD analyses). I9 (voxelwise results reported in text/figures) also satisfied. Inclusion criterion I5 (task is a problem-solving task as defined) is NOT met: the task is a working-memory manipulation (reordering remembered letters according to specified cues) rather than a problem-solving task requiring goal-directed planning, generating novel solutions, or evaluating multiple solution strategies. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Therefore the study does not meet all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and is excluded.

While this is an empirical whole-brain task-based fMRI study in adults that reports MNI coordinates and BOLD results (meets I6, I7, I8, I9), the task is a theory-of-mind/person-description paradigm (reasoning about others’ thoughts/emotions) rather than a problem-solving task as defined in the review (goal-directed problem solving involving planning/sequencing or rule-based operations such as semantic, algebraic, logical, mechanical problem solving). Therefore inclusion criterion I5 is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Because I5 is required and not satisfied, the study must be excluded.

This empirical fMRI study uses a problem-solving/planning paradigm (One Touch Spatial Planning; Tower of London variant), meeting the task definition (I5). It reports whole-brain, voxel-wise group-level analyses (including planning>counting contrasts and FDR/FWE-corrected results) and functional connectivity analyses, satisfying I6. Stereotactic coordinates are reported for peak activations (e.g., DLPFC seed x=28 y=32 z=52 and other coordinates), meeting I7. The study uses task-based BOLD fMRI (SPM8 EPI protocol), satisfying I8. Coordinate results and whole-brain findings are described in the main text and supplemental whole-brain analyses, satisfying I9. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, and is sufficiently complete for screening. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, non-empirical, or only between-group/no healthy task effect) are met. Therefore the study should be included.

This study is a task-based fMRI investigation in healthy adults that reports whole-brain, group-level BOLD results in stereotactic space (meets I6, I7, I8, I9). However, the task (Mental Clock Test: judging whether a clock-hand angle is >90° or <90° for visually presented or imagined stimuli) is a spatial judgement/mental imagery task, not a problem-solving task as defined by the review (i.e., having a goal requiring planning/sequencing actions or performing critical-thinking operations to reach a previously unknown solution). Thus inclusion criterion I5 is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

Full text presents a perceptual classification task (SOeasy/SOdifficult) and an alphabet continuation stimulus-independent condition (SI). These are cognitive/working-memory and perceptual-discrimination tasks, not a problem-solving task as defined by the review (goal-directed solving requiring planning/sequencing to arrive at a previously unknown solution). Therefore I5 is not met. The study does meet other inclusion criteria: I6 (whole-brain, group-level fMRI in healthy adults), I7 (reports MNI/Talairach coordinates), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), and I9 (voxelwise results reported/illustrated). No exclusion criteria are triggered. Full text appears complete. Exclusion is based on failure to meet I5.

Excluded because the task is a number Stroop with emotional priming (a cognitive control/conflict task), which does not meet the review's operational definition of a problem-solving task (I5). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level fMRI in healthy adults), I7 (images normalized to MNI space and coordinate/contrast results reported), I8 (task-based BOLD fMRI), I9 (voxelwise/coordinate results reported in tables/figures). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (task does not require goal-directed problem solving involving planning/sequencing to reach a novel solution; it is an executive attention/counting task). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore exclude.

Although this fMRI study meets methodological criteria (whole-brain analyses, group-level effects, stereotactic coordinates, and BOLD reporting), it does not meet the content definition of a problem-solving task (I5). The experiment investigates working memory manipulation (letter–number sequencing) and age-related neural differences in maintenance vs. manipulation; its primary focus is WM control/strategy and neural activation, not problem solving as defined (goal-directed reasoning/planning to reach a previously unknown solution across semantic/algebraic/logical/mechanical domains). While the task involves reordering according to a rule (numbers ascending, letters alphabetical), the authors frame it as WM manipulation rather than problem solving, and the cognitive demands reflect WM and control/strategy processes rather than domain-general problem solving. Therefore I5 is not satisfied. Inclusion criteria met: I6, I7, I8, I9. Inclusion criteria not met: I5. Exclusion criteria: none applicable. Full text appears complete for screening.

This fMRI study investigates arbitrary delayed paired-association learning and working memory (PAa and DMSv tasks) in healthy adults, not problem-solving as defined by the review (goal-directed planning/sequencing to reach an unknown solution). It therefore fails inclusion criterion I5. It does meet other methodological criteria: whole-brain, group-level task-based fMRI (I6), reports stereotactic coordinates in MNI/Talairach (I7), reports BOLD analyses (I8), and qualifies for voxelwise results reported in text/figures (I9). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This PET study is whole-brain, group-level, in healthy adults and reports stereotactic coordinates and rCBF results, but it does not examine problem-solving as defined in the meta-analysis. The tasks (concurrent discrimination with fixed/random pairing, forced-choice recognition, response reversal) probe learned stimulus–response retrieval, habit expression, recognition memory and set-shifting/executive adaptation rather than goal-directed problem-solving that requires planning/sequencing operations to reach a novel solution. Therefore inclusion criterion I5 (study of a problem-solving task per the meta-analysis definition) is not met. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level analysis in healthy adults), I7 (stereotactic coordinates reported), I8 (rCBF PET analysis), I9 (voxelwise results reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

Although this study is a task-based fMRI BOLD investigation that reports whole-brain group-level effects with stereotactic coordinates in healthy adult controls, it does not examine a problem-solving task as defined by the review. The task is a probabilistic reversal learning/reinforcement-learning paradigm focused on reward prediction and adaptive choice switching, rather than goal-directed problem solving that requires evaluating a problem, planning/sequencing actions within semantic/algebraic/logical/mechanical rule-sets to find a previously unknown solution. Therefore inclusion criterion I5 is not met. Full text is complete and other inclusion criteria (I6, I7, I8, I9) are satisfied; no exclusion criteria are triggered.

This is an fMRI study of healthy adults (N=24) using a task in which participants pursued a goal (maximize earnings) by inferring stock values from multiple cues, evaluating information sources, selecting/planning strategies (ALL, AUD, VIS), and executing buy/reject responses — meeting the review’s problem-solving definition. The study reports group-level whole-brain fMRI BOLD analyses, provides stereotactic coordinates (MNI) in tables/figures, and reports voxelwise results. All required inclusion criteria are met (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9). No exclusion criteria are triggered (not ROI-only; not a clinical/group-comparison-only or non-empirical paper). The provided full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables, references).

This study is a task-based BOLD fMRI investigation of moral reasoning that includes healthy control subjects and reports whole-brain, group-level activation maps with stereotactic coordinates. However, it does not meet the meta-analysis’s definition of a problem-solving task (I5). The moral dilemma paradigm elicits moral judgments (utilitarian vs. non-utilitarian decisions) and network interactions during moral reasoning rather than requiring subjects to identify, plan, sequence, or execute rule-based operations to arrive at a correct or novel solution as specified for problem-solving tasks. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain group-level effects in healthy adults), I7 (stereotactic coordinates reported), I8 (BOLD analysis), I9 (voxelwise results available in tables/figures). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (task does not fit the provided problem-solving definition). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

Full text is incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). Based on the abstract: Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI reasoning/problem-solving using Raven-like relational integration), I8 (fMRI BOLD analysis reported). Inclusion criteria that cannot be verified from the provided content and are therefore treated as not met: I6 (uncertain whether a whole-brain analysis with group-level effects in healthy adult participants is reported in the available text), I7 (stereotactic coordinates in Talairach/MNI space are not present in the provided abstract), I9 (cannot confirm whether voxelwise coordinate results are reported in tables/figures/supplement). No exclusion criteria (E3-E6) are explicitly met based on the available content. Because the full text is incomplete and key inclusion criteria cannot be confirmed, the study is excluded pending review of the complete article.

Full text appears incomplete (only title/abstract provided). Based on available information, the study is an fMRI investigation of nonspatial visual working memory in healthy adults, not a problem-solving task as defined by the review (no evidence of goal-directed problem solving, planning/sequencing to reach a novel solution). Inclusion criteria met from available text: I6 (whole-brain fMRI in healthy adults) and I8 (BOLD signal/fMRI). Inclusion criteria not met or not verifiable: I5 (task is not a problem-solving task per the review definition), I7 (no stereotactic coordinates reported in the provided abstract/full text), I9 (coordinate reporting not verifiable). No exclusion criteria from E3–E6 are clearly met. Given the key mismatch with I5 and incomplete full text, the study is excluded.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation of risk-taking/decision-making in binge drinkers versus healthy volunteers, not a problem-solving task as defined in I5. Although it satisfies other methodological criteria (whole-brain, group-level analyses in healthy adults; stereotactic coordinates reported; BOLD fMRI analyses; voxelwise results presented), it does not examine problem solving (goal-directed planning, sequencing, or rule-based solution of novel problems). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Therefore the paper must be excluded for failing inclusion criterion I5.

The study is an original task-based whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adults reporting BOLD results with stereotactic coordinates and group-level analyses. However, the experimental task (motor pursuit of an artificial prey for monetary reward) does not meet the review’s operational definition of a problem-solving task: it does not require identifying a problem and engaging critical thinking processes to evaluate, plan/sequence actions, or arrive at a correct, previously unknown solution within semantic/algebraic/logical/mechanical rule frameworks. Instead it is a motivated motor/navigation task assessing reward-related neural activity. Therefore I5 (problem-solving task) is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based BOLD fMRI study of reasoning (fluid reasoning/RPM) in healthy adults that tests problem-solving-related processes. It reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (correlation maps and activation clusters across participants) and defines ROIs from these maps. The manuscript explicitly describes BOLD results during reasoning, provides whole-brain statistical maps and figures, and references supplemental tables/figures (supplemental Tables/Figures) where voxelwise results and ROIs are detailed (i.e., stereotactic results typical of SPM2 analyses). An independent test sample was used and group effects are reported. Therefore inclusion criteria I5 (task-based problem solving), I6 (whole-brain group-level effects in healthy adults), I7 (stereotactic activation results reported via maps/supplement), I8 (BOLD analysis), and I9 (voxelwise results available in figures/supplement) are satisfied. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

Full text provided appears incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata). The study reports task-based fMRI (so I8 is met), but the abstract does not provide sufficient information to confirm: I5 (whether the task meets our problem-solving definition), I6 (whole-brain group-level analyses), I7 (stereotactic coordinates reported), or I9 (voxelwise results availability). No exclusion criteria (E3,E4,E5,E6) are indicated in the abstract. Because key inclusion criteria cannot be verified from the incomplete full text, the study is excluded pending retrieval of the complete article (methods, results, coordinate tables).

This is a task-based fMRI study using the Tower of London planning task, which meets the review’s definition of problem solving (goal-directed planning/sequencing). The methods describe whole-brain, voxelwise SPM99 analyses with random-effects group-level results reported for healthy control subjects and patients; imaging data were normalized into Talairach space and BOLD signal (blood oxygenation level–dependent) effects are reported. Coordinate-based results are presented in tables (Tables 3–6). The study therefore provides task-related whole-brain BOLD activation maps in healthy adults during a problem-solving/planning task. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, includes healthy-group task effects, is empirical). Full text appears complete (background, methods, results, discussion).

The study is an empirical, task-based fMRI investigation of anagram problem solving in healthy adult participants (N=15). It explicitly manipulates goal constraints and examines problem-solving processes (generation, evaluation), satisfying the problem-solving definition. It reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses (SPM2) with voxelwise stereotactic coordinates after normalization to the MNI template, and BOLD (T2*) activation results (including tables of peak coordinates and statistical thresholds). Voxelwise results are reported and corrections for multiple comparisons are described. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based whole-brain fMRI study of causal attribution (causality judgments, causal-link perception, motion control) in healthy adult participants that reports group-level BOLD results and stereotactic coordinates (MNI). However, the experimental task involves causal judgment/inference (evaluating whether a stated cause is appropriate) rather than a problem-solving paradigm as defined by I5 (a goal-directed need to devise and execute a plan/sequence of operations within a rule set to arrive at a solution). The task lacks explicit goal-directed planning/sequencing or execution of operations to solve a novel problem; it is an attribution/judgment task. Therefore it does not meet inclusion criterion I5. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Inclusion criteria met: I6, I7, I8, I9. Inclusion criterion not met: I5. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Full text appears complete. The study uses continuous verbal fluency tasks (phonological, lexical, semantic) in healthy adults under S-ketamine and reports whole-brain BOLD fMRI results with stereotactic coordinates. However, it does not meet inclusion criterion I5: the tasks are language fluency/search tasks rather than problem-solving tasks as defined (goal-directed planning/sequencing to arrive at a correct or novel solution). It does meet I6, I7, I8, and I9. No exclusion criteria are triggered.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (n=13) that investigates problem solving using the Match Problems divergent-thinking task (generate-and-evaluate cycles, set-shifts), which fits the review’s problem-solving definition. The study reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain BOLD analyses using SPM2, provides stereotactic MNI coordinates for task-related activations (tables/figures), and reports corrected statistics. Methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not a between-group-only comparison, not non-empirical). Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I9 are met and the paper should be included.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that examines decision-making in prisoner's dilemma (PD) and stag hunt (SH) games. The PD is explicitly described and analyzed as a dominance-solvable problem requiring iterative thinking, deliberation, and computational reasoning to derive an optimal solution, meeting the review's definition of problem solving (goal-directed reasoning, planning/strategy, and execution to reach an optimal choice). The study reports whole-brain, group-level GLM analyses (n=23 for fMRI), BOLD results, and stereotactic Talairach coordinates for significant activations. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not non-empirical, includes healthy-group task effects). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (10 right-handed females) that investigates mental rotation. The task requires a goal (decide whether two 3D objects are same or mirror), and subjects must perform spatial transformations/operations to reach a correct decision, which fits the problem-solving definition (I5). The study reports whole-brain group analyses (GBAM) with group-level effects (I6), provides stereotactic Talairach coordinates for activation foci (I7), and uses BOLD T2*-weighted fMRI with regional/per-voxel analyses (I8). Voxelwise/group results are reported in maps, coordinates, and figures (I9). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the article meets all inclusion criteria and is eligible for the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study of temporal context retrieval and non-memory ordering/recognition tasks (recency and age-ordering of faces). While it includes whole-brain, group-level BOLD analyses with stereotactic coordinates and coordinate tables (I6, I7, I8, I9 satisfied), it does NOT investigate a problem-solving task as defined by the review (I5). The tasks are memory retrieval and perceptual/order judgments rather than goal-directed problem solving requiring planning/sequencing to derive a previously unknown solution. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

The paper reports an empirical task-based BOLD fMRI study in healthy adults (n=25) that includes arithmetic equation verification and an operation-span (OSPAN) paradigm. The arithmetic component and equation verification constitute algebraic/problem-solving operations (goal-directed evaluation and execution of rule-based operations). The study provides whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (cluster-thresholded) and hippocampal ROI analyses, with results warped to MNI space and coordinate-based tables/figures reported. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I5 (problem-solving task present via arithmetic/equation verification), I6 (whole-brain group analyses in healthy adults), I7 (results reported in standardized MNI space), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), and I9 (voxelwise results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not between-group-only, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

Excluded because the study does not investigate problem-solving tasks (inclusion I5 not met). It reports a spatial working memory fMRI experiment in schizophrenia with ROI-focused analyses rather than a task designed to probe problem-solving across domains. Exclusion criterion E3 applies: the reported results are presented primarily as ROI timecourse analyses (despite mention of group t-maps, stereotactic coordinate results are not reported). Inclusion criteria met: I8 (BOLD analysis reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task is not a problem-solving task), I6 (no clear whole-brain group-level task effects in healthy adults are reported as voxelwise/coordinate results), I7 (no stereotactic coordinates reported), I9 (no voxelwise stereotactic results presented in tables/figures/supplement). Full text appears complete and contains methods, results and discussion, so exclusion is based on content, not incompleteness.

This is an empirical, whole-brain H2 15O-PET activation study in healthy adults (n=6) using the Tower of London task, which operationalizes problem solving/planning (goal-directed sequence planning). The paper reports voxelwise, group-level SPM analyses of normalized images (stereotaxic/template registration) and provides tables/figures of regional cerebral blood flow (rCBF) task-related increases and correlational coordinates, satisfying requirements for rCBF analyses and stereotactic coordinate reporting. The task involves goal identification, planning/sequencing, and execution components, matching the review’s problem-solving definition. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not non-empirical, includes healthy-group task effects). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion with coordinate tables; thus fulltext_incomplete=false.

Full text is complete and the study is an empirical whole-brain fMRI investigation in healthy adults reporting group-level BOLD results and stereotactic coordinates. However, the experimental task is a theory-of-mind (cooperation/deception) mentalizing task, not a problem-solving task as defined by the review (i.e., a task requiring a goal-directed process to figure out a way to reach a goal involving planning/sequencing operations to arrive at a correct or novel solution). Thus inclusion criterion I5 (problem-solving task) is not met. The manuscript does meet I6, I7, I8, and I9, and no exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This study is excluded because it does not meet I5 (problem-solving task). The tasks (REF, ROT, JRD) are spatial memory/imagery and perspective-transformation/pointing tasks rather than goal-directed problem-solving as defined (identifying/evaluating a problem, planning/sequencing operations, and executing rule-based steps to reach a novel solution). It does meet I6 (whole-brain group-level fMRI analysis in healthy adults), I7 (reporting Talairach-normalized coordinates), I8 (BOLD fMRI analysis), and I9 (voxelwise results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are applicable. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adults using the Brixton rule-attainment task that requires generating and testing rules to predict the next stimulus (meets problem-solving definition: goal, need to infer a method, hypothesis generation, planning and rule-based execution). The paper reports whole-brain group-level random-effects analyses, reports stereotactic MNI coordinates for significant activations in tables and figures, and uses BOLD fMRI analyses. All required inclusion criteria are satisfied (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9). No exclusion criteria apply: the study includes whole-brain results (not ROI-only), involves healthy-group task effects, and is empirical. Full text provided is complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of a pseudoarithmetic/problem-solving task in healthy adult participants that reports BOLD results and stereotactic coordinates for ROI centers. However, the imaging analyses are restricted to two a priori ROIs (ACC and lPFC) with percent-activation analyses; the paper does not report any whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses or whole-brain coordinate peaks. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I6 and meets exclusion criterion E3 (reports only ROI results). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).
